### `Pass 187.0` (`52beaf6`, 2026-08-31) — **★★★★ A RESIZED WIDGET IS REDRAWN AT THE NEW SIZE, NOT STRETCHED INTO IT — ONE REPORTED DEFECT WAS FOUR, ALL THE SAME SHAPE** — ★★★★ **THE WORST OF THE FOUR SILENTLY DISCARDED THE RESIZE AND REPORTED `resized: true` WITH A `rect_after` NAMING A BOX NEVER WRITTEN: EVERY ASSERTION ANYONE HAD WRITTEN WAS ON THE OUTCOME, AND THE OUTCOME WAS A LIE** — ★★★ **THE REGENERATOR THAT EXISTED TO PREVENT THE STRETCH REPRODUCED IT FAITHFULLY, AT THE OLD SIZE, WHILE ITS OWN DOC COMMENT ASSERTED THE OPPOSITE** — ★★ **THE REFUSE-VS-DISCLOSE ASYMMETRY `pdfceGUI` DECLINED TO RESOLVE IS RESOLVED UNDER `R206`: THE TWO VERBS NOW AGREE, AND THE DEFAULT IS THE REFUSAL** — filed 2026-08-31 (351st filing)

**Sourcing.** As for `Pass 188.0` above — same shell, same commands, one
filing.

#### The shape all four share, stated once

A widget's appearance is a form XObject whose `/BBox` **§12.5.5 maps onto the
annotation's `/Rect`**. So **artwork that does not follow a resize is not "the
old artwork" — it is the old artwork MAGNIFIED**, anisotropically, by
`Δw/Δh`. Every one of the four defects below is that sentence with a different
route into it.

#### ROUTE 1 — the reported one

`regen_after_property_change` answered `Ok(false)` for **every field type
except Text and Choice**, so a check box, radio button or push button was
**never redrawn at all**. Drag a 12 pt check box to 40 pt and pdfce's own 1 pt
border draws at **~3.3 pt**. The operator: *"Form shape outlines of checkboxes
and such scale when I drag them larger."*

★ **And that is the case `resize_annotation` REFUSES BY NAME for a foreign
appearance.** The widget path took the same unsatisfiable operation
**silently**, on artwork **pdfce itself drew** and could therefore have rebuilt
exactly. ⇒ **Two verbs facing the same impossibility, one refusing and one
proceeding in silence, is a defect even before you decide which is right** —
which is what `R206` is for, and is why the resolution below is a
*reconciliation* rather than a preference.

`/Btn` now goes through `regen_button_appearance`. **Ownership is decided by
BYTES** — rebuild from the **unmodified** geometry and compare, the same test
`resize_annotation` and `set_markup_style` already use. *"Could pdfce draw a
check box like this?"* is true of **every conforming check box in existence**,
which is precisely the set that must not be touched. All-or-nothing across a
field's widgets, so **a radio group cannot come out half-restyled**.

#### ★★ ROUTE 2 — Text and Choice WERE rebuilt, at the OLD size

The regenerator reads `field.widgets[i].rect`, a snapshot taken **before** the
caller stages its `/Rect` write. **Measured:** a text field dragged
**100×24 → 300×100** came back with `/AP` `/BBox [0 0 100 24]` — *a
regeneration that faithfully reproduced the defect it existed to prevent*, then
handed it to §12.5.5 to stretch **3× by 4.17×**.

`edit_widget`'s own doc comment asserted the opposite — *"rebuilds the
appearance whenever the extent changes … keeps the correct case correct"* — so
**the claim, the code and the pixels disagreed three ways**. Nobody had looked
because **an empty text field's stretched border reads as a border**.

#### ROUTE 3 — a push button's caption change redrew nothing

The caption is painted **into** the plate, and `needs_regen` did not include
`edit.caption.is_some()`. So `/MK` `/CA` changed, the field list showed the new
word, and **the button kept displaying the old one**.

#### ★★★ ROUTE 4 — THE WORST, FOUND BY READING RATHER THAN BY A REPORT

On a **Shape-B** widget — a separate dictionary under a `/Kids` parent, which
is what a field placed on three pages looks like and what **every radio group
is** — `set_widget_ap` built a **whole-dictionary write from the PRE-command
dictionary** and pushed it onto the command. Writes apply in order, last one
winning, so that `/AP` write **silently discarded the `/Rect` write staged
moments earlier**.

Measured on `forms/multi-widget-form.pdf`, resizing **140×22 → 380×100**:

| observed | value | reading |
|---|---|---|
| `/Rect` after | **140 × 22** | the resize, thrown away |
| `/AP` `/BBox` | **380 × 100** | the rebuild, applied |
| `outcome.resized` | `true` | |
| `outcome.rect_after` | `Rect { .. 400, 250 }` | **a box never written** |

A widget whose artwork §12.5.5 must now **squash into a third of its size**,
from a call that returned `Ok`.

★★★★ **EVERY ASSERTION ANYONE HAD WRITTEN WAS ON THE OUTCOME, AND THE OUTCOME
WAS A LIE — which is why 4,861 passing tests said nothing.** Shape A (the
one-widget field, where the field dictionary **is** the widget) took the
`merged_ap` branch, which has always folded correctly. **The bug needed a
multi-widget field, and multi-widget fields are exactly the ones nobody resizes
in a test.**

⇒ **The reusable half, and it is `R159`'s mechanism pointed at a different
instrument:** an outcome struct is a **reader the verb writes itself**, so
asserting on it can only ever see what the verb *believes*. `R159` says a
defect that lives in the BYTES must be asserted in the BYTES; here the lenient
"parser" was the verb's own return value. The new test file asserts on the
`/AP` `/BBox`, not on the outcome — **on three of these four routes the outcome
was correct and the bytes were not.**

Fixed by **folding `/AP` into the write already in flight** rather than adding
a second one. `rotate_widget` was on the same path and is fixed by the same
change.

#### ★★ THE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, WHICH IS THE PART A CONSUMING SHELL MUST READ

`WidgetEdit` now carries a whole **`ResizeOptions`** — the same type
`resize_annotation` takes, **reused rather than copied so a shell cannot mirror
`keep_rect_differences`' opt-OUT spelling backwards.** `pdfceGUI` shipped the
operator's three Inkscape switches on 2026-08-28 and they were **structurally
unreachable** from a form field; they reach one now, and **their answer is
passed through, never derived**.

`pdfceGUI` named the refuse-vs-disclose asymmetry between `resize_annotation`
and `edit_widget` and **explicitly declined to resolve it** — correctly, that
is this side's call under **`R206`**. The two verbs now **agree**, and the
default is `resize_annotation`'s: **refuse**, with
**`allow_appearance_distortion`** as the escape hatch. New `EditError` usage:
`ResizeAppearanceNotRebuildable { subtype: "Widget", .. }`. **A silent stretch
is exactly the report that opened this Pass.**

**The refusal is narrow by construction:** it needs a real change of **extent**,
**AND** artwork pdfce did not draw, **AND** neither escape — because a uniform
scale with `scale_stroke_width` on is satisfied **exactly** by §12.5.5's matrix,
and refusing it would refuse a resize that comes out right. A border or caption
change on an unrebuildable field **still proceeds with a disclosure**: nothing
is stretched when the geometry did not move.

Two new outcome fields, `stroke_width` and `rect_differences_scaled`, **named
and meaning exactly what their `AnnotationResize` twins do**.

#### ★ NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY — filed so it is not smuggled in later

**`/BS` `/W` still does not change a check box's or radio button's drawn
border**, which pdfce authors at a fixed **1.0**. That is **the artwork's
existing contract**, not an oversight: changing it would alter how **every
pdfce-authored check box already in the wild** renders. That is a decision to
take on its own terms, with the operator, and not under a bug report. **Filed
as a Backlog item this filing.**

**Rounded corners:** `pdfceGUI` checked and there is **nothing to scale**; no
engine work was requested and none was done. Their closing line is **adopted as
the standing answer** — a genuine toggle needs a **rounded-rectangle
primitive** first, scoped with the operator, not improvised under a bug report.

#### CLI

`pdfce-cli edit-widget` gains `--scale-stroke-width`, `--keep-rect-differences`
and `--allow-appearance-distortion`, **spelled as `resize-annotation` spells
them**, and prints both new disclosures. **Driven against the binary rather
than trusted from the unit tests** — a shell flag can be parsed and never used,
and unit tests hit core directly.

#### Tests

`crates/pdfce-core/tests/widget_resize_appearance.rs`, **9 tests**, asserting
on the `/AP` `/BBox` rather than on the outcome. **Six sabotages run
separately, each caught by exactly the tests that should catch it:** old-rect
regen (**2**), button regen ignoring the staged rect (**2**), `/Btn` falling
through to `Ok(false)` (**5**), the Shape-B fold removed (**1**), the caption
trigger removed (**1**), the ownership test always answering "ours" (**1**).
**Sum of caught-by counts = 12 over 6 sabotages = 2.0 tests per sabotage**;
every sabotage was caught by at least one, and no sabotage survived.

The foreign-artwork case uses a **real fixture rather than a mock**:
`forms/demo-form.pdf` carries a hand-authored check box whose `/AP` is
`0 0 14 14 re f 4 4 6 6 re f`.

### `Pass 186.0` (`7c2ee96`, 2026-08-31) — **★★★★ EVERY CONTENT-EDITING VERB READS THE SESSION, NOT THE DISK — ONE CAUSE, TWO DEFECTS, AND THE SECOND ONE ADDRESSED A DIFFERENT SHEET AND RETURNED `Ok`** — ★★★★ **THE ENTIRE 4,861-TEST SUITE WAS GREEN BEFORE *AND* AFTER THE FIX: IT WAS NOT WEAK, IT WAS ***VACUOUS*** WITH RESPECT TO THE PROPERTY, AND THE PROPERTY NEEDS TWO VERBS IN ONE SESSION TO BE VISIBLE AT ALL** — ★★★ **DECISION `111`: A PAGE INDEX MEANS THE PAGE AS THE SESSION HAS IT** — ★★ **THE FIX CREATED A HAZARD STRICTLY WORSE THAN THE DEFECT AND HAD TO GUARD IT: `reflow_block` NOW REFUSES BY NAME** — filed 2026-08-31 (351st filing)

**Sourcing.** As for `Pass 188.0` above — same shell, same commands, one
filing. Answers `pdfceGUI`'s
`request_edit_verbs_read_the_base_not_the_overlay` (2026-08-31,
`D:\Dev\FeatureRequests\pdfce_FeatureRequests\open\`).

#### The cause

`EditSession` had **two page-tree readers living side by side**. The authoring
verbs used the overlay-aware `EditSession::pages()`; **eight content-editing
entry points** used `page_tree::pages(&self.base)` — **the document as it was
on disk**.

#### DEFECT 1 — a lost capability, reported by the operator with its own workaround

`add_image`, `paste_objects`, `flatten_fields` and `add_text` append a **new
content stream**, and the first and last add a **new resource**. All of it
lands in the staging overlay and **none of it exists in the base**. So the
base-derived page's `/Contents` did not name the appended stream, a base-only
resolver could not classify the resulting `Do` — and **`vector/decompose.rs`
emits NO object for a `Do` it cannot classify.**

The object was therefore **visible on the canvas and absent from the model the
geometry verbs address**: the shell's decomposition held **N+1** objects,
`page_objects` held **N**, and dragging the new one answered
`ObjectOutOfRange`.

The operator found the workaround himself and reported it as one: *"When I add
a new image to a pdf I can't edit it unless I save the document first. I assume
this probably affects more than just images."* **He was right, and the class
was wider than he guessed.**

#### ★★★★ DEFECT 2 — NOBODY HAD REPORTED IT: THE VERBS ADDRESSED A DIFFERENT SHEET

`delete_pages`, `insert_pages`, `reorder_pages` and the merge verbs all commit
into the **overlay**, so the base still held the original page order and count.
**A shell computes a page index against the overlay — as it must, because that
is what the operator is looking at — and handed it to a verb that resolved it
against the base.**

Delete page one, and what the operator calls page 0 was planned and committed
against a **different sheet**, with **no refusal and no disclosure**.
`delete_objects` there **destroys real content and returns `Ok`**.

`pdfceGUI` filed this half as an **arithmetic consequence** of a measured count
mismatch, explicitly **not driven**, because it needs a fixture with
distinguishable per-page content. **It was driven here** on
`fixtures/synthetic/pageops/four-pages.pdf` and **reproduced exactly**: before
this commit, `page_objects(3)` on a **three**-page document returned **the text
of page four**.

#### What changed

- The **eight** `page_tree::pages(&self.base)?` sites become `self.pages()?`.
- `current_page_content` collapses **from two branches to one**:
  `ContentStream::from_page(&self.view(), page)`. The old staged branch read
  the first content object's staged bytes directly and **could not see a stream
  appended beside it**; the old base branch **could not see a staged stream at
  all**. The "double-handling" worry the base branch documented **does not
  apply** — `make_raw_stream` writes `/Length` and nothing else, so
  `decode_stream` runs an empty filter chain and hands the raw bytes straight
  back.
- `page_content_and_objects` and the two `&self` decomposition helpers build
  `DocumentXObjects` / `DocumentFonts` from the **session view**. Their previous
  comment reasoned that *"page `/Resources` are not rewritten by content
  surgery, so base and session agree on them"* — **true of content surgery,
  false of `add_image` and `add_text`.** ⇒ `R93` again: a doc comment stating a
  cross-module invariant, true of the case it was written against and never
  re-checked against the ones added since.
- `ContentStream::from_page` **no longer emits a separator before an EMPTY
  payload**. `text_edit_command` folds a multi-stream page into its first
  object and empties the rest **in place**, so an unconditional separator would
  append **one whitespace byte per emptied stream on every re-read** — and **a
  session re-reads its own content on every subsequent edit.** An unbounded
  growth defect, found only because the branch collapse made it reachable.
- **The decomposition memo's key is widened** from `(first content id, its
  staged span)` to **the whole dependency set**: page id, every `/Contents`
  entry with its staged span, and the effective `/Resources`. `add_image`
  touches **none** of the old key's inputs, so the memo served the pre-insert
  model back — **and a stale index is not a stale answer, it is an edit applied
  to the wrong object.** (First of the two occurrences that mint **`R237`**;
  the second is `Pass 188.0`'s form half.)
- **New verb `EditSession::page_content_generation(page_index) -> u64`**, asked
  for **by name** by `pdfceGUI`: a 64-bit FNV-1a digest of that same key, so a
  shell can assert model agreement **continuously** instead of decomposing
  twice. Its **three non-promises** — not a content digest, not stable across
  sessions or saves, not minimal — are documented **at the verb and in
  `docs/core-api/`**.

#### ★★ A HAZARD THIS PASS CREATED AND HAD TO GUARD

`reflow_block`'s planner is **base-indexed**: `plan_reflow_from_doc` takes
`(&self.base, page_index)` and **re-derives the page itself**. Swapping the
surrounding reads to the overlay **without a guard** would have made it splice
**one sheet's reflowed bytes into a DIFFERENT sheet's content object** —
**strictly worse than the defect being fixed**, which at least kept both halves
consistent with each other.

It now **refuses by name** when the base page at `page_index` is not the
overlay page at `page_index`. Teaching the planner the overlay is a **real
feature** — it needs extraction provenance the staging buffer does not carry,
the same reason its existing already-edited refusal exists — and **is not this
Pass**.

⇒ **A consistency fix applied to a half-consistent system can produce an
inconsistency worse than the one it removes.** Two wrong readings that agree
with each other are survivable; one right and one wrong is not. **The guard, not
the swap, is the load-bearing part of this Pass.** Recorded in decision `111` as
the rule's one named, narrow exception.

#### ★★★★ WHY THE ENTIRE EXISTING SUITE WAS GREEN ON BOTH HALVES — THE REUSABLE HALF

**Every test in this crate that exercised a content-editing verb did so on a
session whose page set had not been structurally edited and whose content had
not been appended to this session.** On such a session **base and overlay agree
by construction**, so every assertion passed **identically before and after**.
The full workspace run was green on the first try after the fix, **and would
have stayed green forever without it**.

⇒ **The suite was not weak — it was VACUOUS with respect to this property, and
running it harder would never have said so. The property needs TWO VERBS IN ONE
SESSION to be visible at all.**

This is the sharpest instance this project has recorded of the difference
between *coverage* and *discrimination*: **4,861 tests, 0 of which could
distinguish the two states.** A per-verb test suite tests verbs; a property
that only exists **between** verbs has no home in it. Sits beside `R159` (an
instrument that repairs the reading on the way out) and `Pass 188.0`'s
seven-fixtures-one-blind-spot finding — **three different ways for a complete-
looking measurement to be blind by construction, two of them in this one
filing.**

#### Tests

`crates/pdfce-core/tests/session_overlay_skew.rs`, **10 tests**, all of the
two-verbs-in-one-session shape. **Three sabotages run separately:** reverting
the page tree reddens **10 of 10**; reverting the resolvers reddens **5**;
narrowing the cache key reddens **4**.

★ **Two tests survived the first sabotage and were STRENGTHENED rather than
kept** — one was **vacuous** (it compared a post-image count against a baseline
taken *after* the image, so both measurements were the base count while the
image was being erased) and one **passed for the wrong reason** (deleting the
**last** page made `page_objects(3)` fail for an unrelated resolution error
that *looked like* the right answer). That is `NEXT_SESSION.md` §C item 4's
three-causes-of-a-surviving-sabotage checklist, applied and paying out on its
first use after being written down.

#### ★ RESIDUAL, NAMED SO IT IS NOT REDISCOVERED AS A NEW BUG

`edit_text`, `format_text` and the two `preview_*` verbs pass `&self.base` to
the text planner as the **object resolver**, so a `/Font` created this session
is named by the overlay page's `/Resources` and **cannot be resolved through
it**. The outcome is a **clean refusal, not a wrong edit**, and it is **the
same outcome as before this Pass** — the resource used to be *invisible* and is
now *unresolvable*. Fixing it means threading a view through `text_edit`'s
**~40 `doc: &Document` signatures**. **Filed as a Backlog item this filing.**

**Not affected, verified rather than assumed:** annotations are addressed by
`ObjId` through the overlay-aware `value()` / `locate_annotation()` / `graph()`,
so markup, ce dimensions, form fields, adopted widgets, redaction marks,
attachments and bookmarks **were editable the instant they were authored and
still are**.

### `Pass 185.2` (`c17f1b5`, 2026-08-30) — **★★★★ THE OPEN ITEM `Pass 185.1` FILED ONE COMMIT AGO IS CLOSED, AND IT WAS NEVER A SECOND CLASS: THE SAME VERB, THE SAME `NoPageTreeRoot`, WALKING THROUGH THE GUARD BECAUSE THE GUARD WAS BUILT FROM THE THING IT WAS PROTECTING** — ★★★ **A GUARD BUILT FROM *"THE TREE"* IS NOT A GUARD AGAINST *LOSING* THE TREE: THE CATALOG POINTS AT THE PAGE TREE AND IS NOT IN IT** — ★★ **THE SYMPTOM NAMED IT FROM THE FIRST CRASH — `NoPageTreeRoot`, NOT `NoPages` — AND WAS READ PAST, IN EVERY PANIC MESSAGE INCLUDING THE ONES QUOTED IN THE PREVIOUS COMMIT** — filed 2026-08-30 (349th filing, together with `Pass 185.1` below)

★★★★ **FILED HERE UNASKED, AND THE REASON IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE DISPATCH
IT ARRIVED DURING.** This role was dispatched to file `Pass 185.1` alone, with
one explicit instruction: *"record `Pass 185.1` in whatever shape makes a stale
reader unable to conclude the class is closed."* **`c17f1b5` was committed and
pushed at 18:52:52, while that filing was being written** — twenty-two minutes
after `e77459b` — and it **closes the class.** Filing `185.1` as OPEN and
stopping would have produced the exact inverse of what was asked for: a
permanent append-only record asserting OPEN about something that had been
CLOSED for half an hour. **The status is therefore filed at the tip, not at the
commit this role was pointed at.** See the *Two writers, one tree* note at the
end of the `Pass 185.1` entry — this is the second time in two filings the
working tree moved mid-filing, and the first time it moved a **verdict**.

**Sourcing.** `git log` / `git rev-parse HEAD origin/main` / `git status
--porcelain` / `git show --stat c17f1b5` and its per-path diff; `git log -1
--format=%B c17f1b5`; live read of `crates/pdfce-core/src/edit.rs:25228`–`25260`.
`HEAD` = `origin/main` = **`c17f1b5`** — **already pushed.**

#### ★★★★ THE DEFECT, AND WHY IT IS ONE CLASS RATHER THAN TWO

`Pass 185.1`'s `page_tree_object_ids` was built from `page_slots`, which returns
each page's `ancestors`. **That chain stops at the `/Pages` ROOT.** The
**catalog** — the object that *points at* the page tree — is not a member of it.
So an `/AcroForm` whose `/Fields` named the **catalog** passed the guard,
`delete_field` removed it, and the document had no `/Root` from which to find a
page tree at all.

⇒ **A guard built from "the tree" is not a guard against losing the tree,
because the thing that REACHES the tree is not IN it.** That sentence is the
Pass, and it generalises past forms and past PDFs: whenever a protected set is
enumerated by walking the structure being protected, **the edges that make the
structure reachable are outside the walk by construction.**

★★★ **THE SYMPTOM HAD NAMED IT FROM THE FIRST CRASH.** The error is
`NoPageTreeRoot`, **not `NoPages`**. Losing a page gives a document with fewer
pages; losing the **root** is what that variant means — and it was in every
panic message read, *including the ones quoted verbatim in `e77459b`'s own
commit message*. The engineer's own account: *"I read past it."* **This is the
`Pass 184.0` shape again** — the answer already present in the material being
quoted, unextracted — and it is the third instance recorded this month of a
correct diagnosis sitting inside text somebody was already reading.

★★ **AND THE PREVIOUS COMMIT WARNED ABOUT THIS IN THE ABSTRACT TWO PARAGRAPHS
BEFORE DOING IT.** `e77459b`'s message argues, correctly, that *"a guard added
to one [route] is exactly the kind of fix that leaves the other two broken
beside it"* — and then built all three guards from **one wrong set**. The
generalisation was right; it was applied across *routes* and not across *the
set's own construction*. ⇒ **A reproducer written from one case, going green,
is evidence about that case and not about the class it was written to
represent** — which is the same sentence `185.1` filed as its open item, now
paid for a second time from the other direction.

#### What changed

- `EditSession::page_tree_object_ids` now inserts **`self.graph().catalog_id()`**
  alongside the pages and their ancestors (`edit.rs:25256`–`25260`), with the
  reason stated inline: *"the only object whose loss produces `NoPageTreeRoot`
  rather than an empty document."*
- `crates/pdfce-core/tests/form_delete_page_tree.rs` gains a **third**
  reproducer, `deleting_a_field_that_is_the_catalog_never_produces_an_unreadable_file`,

- **33 lines changed in `edit.rs`, 71 added in the test** — 98 insertions, 6

The catalog fixture reproduces **deterministically before** the fix and passes
after. **★ SABOTAGED:** with the catalog line removed from the protected set,
the new test **FAILS** — so it is testing *this* fix rather than some other
refusal that happens to stop the delete. That check is the direct descendant of

and of `Pass 184.0`'s *"a surviving sabotage has three causes and only one is a
weak test"*. **It is also exactly what `Pass 185.1` did not do** — its
reproducer went green and was read as covering the class.

`cargo test --workspace --all-features` green; fmt and clippy clean;

#### ★★ WHAT THE ENGINEER GOT RIGHT, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS THE REASON THIS PASS EXISTS AT ALL

**Filing the second hit as OPEN rather than assuming the first fix closed the

say 'the absence of a reproduction is not evidence of a fix', and that sentence
is the only reason this was still being chased an hour later instead of shipped
as done."*

⇒ **A correctly-filed open item is not bookkeeping; it is the mechanism that
kept a live corruption in view for the hour it took to find.** Had `185.1`
shipped as *"three routes guarded, class closed"* — which its green reproducer
fully supported — the catalog case would have gone out in a release, silent, in

#### ★★★ HOW IT WAS CAUGHT — AND THE OBSERVATION-HARNESS FINDING NOW STANDS AT `n = 3` IN ONE SESSION

libFuzzer wrote **no artifact**: Rust's abort on Windows exits `0xc0000409`
before libFuzzer's crash handler saves one, so there was **nothing to reduce**.
What worked was **`-seed=N` to make the run replayable**, plus **grepping the
output for the panic HEAD rather than tailing it**.

★★★★ **THREE OBSERVATION HARNESSES DISCARDED THE EVIDENCE THAT EXPLAINED A
FAILURE, IN THREE DIFFERENT TOOLS, ON ONE DAY:**

| # | harness | what was lost | who found it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | libFuzzer on Windows | the crashing input — no artifact written, `0xc0000409` beats the handler | engineer, `Pass 185.1` |
| 2 | `tail -40` on a background fuzz capture | **the panic head** — kept only the bottom of the backtrace, which names libFuzzer's internals instead of the verb | engineer, `Pass 185.2` |
| 3 | `\| tail -25` on a gate sweep | **the failing test's entire output** — see `Pass 185.1`'s gate section | this role, this filing |

⇒ **`tail` is the wrong tool for the output of anything that can fail, because
the part that names the cause is at the TOP of a panic and at the TOP of a test
failure, while `tail` is reflexively reached for on the assumption that the
interesting part is the summary.** Redirect to a file; `grep` the file for the
head. Instances 2 and 3 were **independent and simultaneous**, in the same
repository, by two agents who had not spoken — which is what makes this a
property of the reflex rather than of either session. Filed to
`D:/dev/rag/rust/` as its own finding.

★★★★ **AMENDED 2026-08-31 (353rd filing, `Pass 190.0`): THE SIZING BELOW WAS
WRONG, AND ITS WRONGNESS IS A BIGGER FINDING THAN THE SIZING WAS.** Four

severity is as much a part of an open item as a reproduction is. Known vs

before it ships**: the unit is **any assertion made after a mutation over
committed state, or over two independent derivations of one quantity**, whether
or not it lives in a named helper — and the `fn debug_assert_*` grep is the

`cargo +nightly fuzz build` and **never `cargo fuzz run`** — its own words,
lines 806–808: *"Actual fuzz CAMPAIGNS stay manual/local."* Both crashes in this
arc were found by a **person choosing to fuzz**. ⇒ `R236` schedules a target's
**compilation**, not its **execution**, and that gap is written into the rule
rather than left for a future reader to discover.

#### ★★★★ WHAT SHIPPED

`fuzz/fuzz_targets/form_edit_sequence.rs` (NEW, 204 lines) plus **three
committed seeds** under `fuzz/corpus/form_edit_sequence/seed_*` (`demo-form`,
`js-carriers-form`, `nested-form` — 1,114 / 1,331 / 1,246 bytes, **3,691 bytes
over 3 seeds = 1,230 bytes each**), matching `fuzz/.gitignore`'s existing
`seed_*` convention so a fresh clone bootstraps coverage rather than starting
from random bytes against a PDF parser.

It drives **four verbs** in an input-derived sequence over whatever field names
the mutated document actually has: `set_button_action`, `rename_field`,
`delete_field`, `delete_field_group`. It exists because **`form_model` fuzzes
the form READ side and nothing fuzzed the WRITE side** — while `Pass 184.0` had
just added a traversal that walks **every live object of an arbitrary
document** looking for action dictionaries, bounded by one constant
(`forms::MAX_ACTION_NEST_DEPTH`) that had never been driven. That is
untrusted-input parsing by any reading of `ARCHITECTURE.md` §10, and it shipped
without a target.

The refusal: **`EditError::FieldObjectIsInPageTree { name, object }`** — the
**110th** `EditError` variant (`docs/core-api/index.md:17` updated 109 → 110 in
the same commit, which discharges the `check-core-api-verbs.py` failure the
348th filing recorded as owed and correctly attributed to the engineer's
then-uncommitted work). Two private helpers implement it,
`EditSession::page_tree_object_ids` and `EditSession::refuse_if_in_page_tree`.

★ **The page-tree node set comes from `page_slots`**, which already returns each
page's `ancestors` — the tree **as the reader walks it**, rather than a second
traversal that could disagree with it. ★★ **That choice is right and was still
insufficient, and `Pass 185.2` is the reason:** the reader's walk of the tree
does not contain the **catalog** that reaches the tree. The principle survives;
the set was incomplete.

#### ★★★★ WHAT IT FOUND — AND THE SEVERITY IS IN THE `#[cfg]`, NOT IN THE PANIC

**Within two minutes of the target first existing.** An `/AcroForm` whose
`/Fields` names an object that is **also a `/Page`**. `forms::parse_acroform`
models it as a field — **correctly**, because the form dictionary says it is one
and §12.7.3 states no rule that a field may not also be something else — and
`delete_field` then removed the page.

★★ **The panic is not the defect; the panic is the only reason anyone saw the
defect.** The sole complaint came from `debug_assert_page_tree_still_walks`
(`edit.rs:12079`), which is `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`. **In the build operators
run it is compiled out.** There the verb returns `Ok`, the save returns `Ok`,
and the output is a file **pdfce itself cannot reopen** — the outcome that
guard's own panic message names, verbatim, as *"the shape that shipped the
2026-08-20 `/Contents` corruption"*. A `cargo-fuzz` build has debug assertions
on, which is the only reason this was visible at all.

⇒ **Minted below as `R236`: a `debug_assert` postcondition is a TRIPWIRE FOR A
FUZZER, NOT A GUARD FOR AN OPERATOR.** The verb had been shipping since
`Pass 20.x`. The postcondition that would have caught it landed at `Pass 111.0`
and sat silent for ~74 Passes — not because it was wrong, but because **nothing
was generating the input that makes it speak.**

#### ★★★ THE GUARD'S COVERAGE — FOUR VERBS, THREE SETS, AND THE FOURTH VERIFIED HERE RATHER THAN ASSUMED

The engineer guarded three routes separately, and stated the reason:
`delete_field`, `delete_field_group` and `delete_widget` **build their removal
sets in three different functions**, so a guard added to one is exactly the kind
of fix that leaves the other two broken beside it. Each calls
`refuse_if_in_page_tree` on its **own** set, and the reproducer asserts the
field and group routes independently for the same reason.

★★ **This role checked for a fourth route and found one; it is clean — stated
as a measurement, not as agreement.** `cut_field` also removes a field. It does
**not** build a fourth removal set: it is `copy_field` → `delete_field` →
`coalesce_last`, so it inherits the guard. And the refusal is **clean on the way
out**, because `copy_field` is `pub fn copy_field(&self, …)` — **`&self`,
side-effect-free** — so a refused cut has committed nothing and staged nothing
before it returns. ⇒ **"All three deletion routes" is complete rather than
merely exhaustive of the routes the engineer happened to look at**, and the
completeness rests on a delegation and an immutable receiver, both read here.

★★★ **AND THE ROUTE-COMPLETENESS CHECK WAS THE WRONG AXIS, WHICH IS
`Pass 185.2`'S FINDING ARRIVING FROM A THIRD DIRECTION.** Three routes were
guarded; a fourth was verified to delegate; **all four consulted the same
incomplete set.** Route coverage was total and the guard was still wrong. ⇒
**Enumerating the CALLERS of a guard says nothing about the correctness of what
the guard CONTAINS**, and the caller enumeration is the easier, more visible,
more satisfying check — which is why it absorbed the attention of the commit
message, of this role's verification, and of the reproducer, while the set
itself went unexamined by all three.

**What is NOT claimed:** no census was run over every verb that can remove an
object. `delete_page`, annotation deletion and the vector-edit removals were
**not** examined for this collision, and the guard does not reach them. Scoped
out with reason — the collision is *form-object is also a page-tree node*, and
those verbs do not resolve an object **through the `/AcroForm`** — but written
down as unexamined rather than left silent, and `Pass 185.2` is a live warning
about how such a boundary reads in hindsight.

#### ★★★★ STANDING RULE MINTED — `R236`

Full text under *Standing rules*. In one line: **a `debug_assert`
postcondition over state derived from untrusted input is a tripwire for a
fuzzer, not a guard for an operator; writing one is an admission that a
corruption class is undetectable in the shipping build, so it owes a
`cargo-fuzz` target over the verbs it guards, or a written exemption at the
helper itself.**

**The warrant, in short:** the existing fuzz obligation triggers on *new* code
that *parses* untrusted input. `delete_field` is neither — it is old, and it
**edits** a structure somebody else parsed. The existing trigger did not fire
and structurally could not, for the verb that carried a release-silent
corruption for seventy-four Passes. **`R236`'s trigger is the postconditions,
not the diff.**

**Ledger, with denominator (hard rule 10):** **2 of 2** named postcondition
helpers enumerated by `grep -rn "fn debug_assert"` across `pdfce-core` +
`pdfce-render`; **1 in scope** (`debug_assert_page_tree_still_walks`, now
covered by `form_edit_sequence`), **1 exempt with the exemption already written
by whoever wrote it** (`debug_assert_not_in_path`, `writer/content.rs:649`:
*"A content builder has no untrusted input, so this is an implementation-bug
**tripwire** in tests, never a runtime refusal."*). ★★★ **The word "tripwire",
and the whole distinction, already existed in this codebase and the consequence
had simply never been drawn in `edit.rs`** — the same shape as the XFA item in
`CLAUDE.md`, *the answer already sourced in one document while another still
asked the question*. Minted at `n = 1`, argued in the rule's own text against
this project's habit of declining `n = 1`.

#### ★★★ DECISION `110` — REFUSING IS NOT "HARD-CODING A CHOICE THE STANDARD LEAVES OPEN"

Full text in `ARCHITECTURE.md` §12. Recorded because a **standing operator
instruction points the other way** and a future session will be right to ask.
`MEMORY.md` carries Ken's 2026-08-08 ruling — *"never hard-code a choice the
standard leaves open"*, make spec ambiguity a **setting** — and §12.7.3 does
leave this open: nothing forbids an object from being both a field and a page.

**A refusal is the opposite of choosing a reading.** The settings rule governs
cases where two interpretations each produce a defensible *result* and pdfce
must produce one anyway (`overprint_zero_tint_scope` is the canonical shape:
every render must paint *something*). Here the two dispositions — *delete the
page* and *strip the field-ness* — are both **inferences about a malformed
document, made silently, on a destructive verb**, which is project rule 4 from
the other direction. **A setting would be required if pdfce had picked one; it
declined to pick.** ★★ **The flip condition is named** so the decision can
disagree with the future rather than merely outlive it: if a **named real
producer** is ever found emitting the shape, the case stops being
malformed-input handling and becomes producer-compatibility, and the setting
becomes correct.

**(b) The three verbs' refusal — CLEAN.** `docs/core-api/02-editing-and-saving.md`'s

**★★ (c) THE FUZZ-TARGET COUNT — TWO SURVIVORS.** Both re-verified present at

- **★★★ Survivor 1 — `fuzz/Cargo.toml`, header comment, lines 15–17: a

  ★★★★ **THIS IS THE TWIN OF A LIST DELETED FIVE DAYS AGO.** Verified by

  comment named EIGHT targets and listed them by hand… the list had been wrong
  for months — the same stale-count defect `R212` is about… **A hand-maintained
  list beside an automatic mechanism has nothing forcing it to stay true**, so
  it is now a pointer rather than a list."* **The diagnosis was exactly right.
  The sweep that acted on it searched the file it was correcting** — and the
  identical list in `fuzz/Cargo.toml`, the file the workflow's own replacement
  text *points at*, was never looked for. ⇒ **Clause (e) says a sweep is only as
  good as its spelling of the claim. This adds: a sweep is only as good as its
  list of PLACES — and the place a correction names inside its own replacement
  text is the first one it fails to check.**

- **★★★ Survivor 2 — `.github/workflows/ci.yml:777`: THE CORRECTION IS ITSELF
  STALE.** The replacement for survivor 1's twin reads *"There are 24 (measured
  2026-08-25, `ls fuzz/fuzz_targets/*.rs | wc -l`)"*. **There are 27** — same
  command, run here. Three targets landed in five days and the number was not
  touched.

  ★★★★ **HARD RULE 10'S COROLLARY — *A CORRECTION IS A CLAIM* — CAUGHT IN THE
  ACT, AND IT IS THE MOST INSTRUCTIVE THING IN THIS FILING.** That figure is
  **impeccably sourced**: dated, and carrying the exact shell command that
  produced it. It was **correct when written.** It is wrong now. ⇒ **Sourcing a
  figure makes it AUDITABLE; it does not make it DURABLE.** And note what the
  fix reached for: *"a pointer rather than a list"* — then wrote a **count**
  beside the pointer, which is **the same defect at lower resolution.** A list
  of 8 goes wrong loudly; a count of 24 goes wrong silently and still reads as
  precision. **The pointer half (`see fuzz/fuzz_targets/*.rs`) is the durable
  half and needed no number at all.**

  **Recommended remedy: DELETE the parenthetical count; do not gate it.** A gate
  is trivially writable (compare `ls fuzz/fuzz_targets/*.rs | wc -l` against any
  integer near "target") and is still wrong, for the reason that comment itself
  derived: the durable fix is to stop maintaining by hand what a mechanism
  maintains automatically. A 25th `tools/check-*` to keep a comment's adjective
  true is a permanent cost for a sentence with no reader. **Engineer's call;
  filed as a recommendation, not a decision.**

- **★★★ Survivor 3 — `crates/pdfce-core/src/edit.rs:12034`, and this Pass
  DIRECTLY FALSIFIES IT.** In `debug_assert_page_tree_still_walks`'s own doc

  entirely in catching a developer's mistake at the moment it is made, and **a
  release build's operator gains nothing from paying for it. CI runs the test
  suite in debug, so the guard is live exactly where it earns its cost.**"*

  **The word "exactly" is the overclaim, and the Pass is its refutation.** That
  sentence rests on an unstated premise — *anything the guard would catch is
  already reachable from CI's debug test suite.* The fuzzer found a case CI's
  suite did not contain (twice), and the release-build outcome is **not** "the
  operator gains nothing": it is a silently corrupted file. The guard earns its
  cost in **two** places, and the second is the one that found the defect.
  ★ **What is NOT falsified, so a fix does not over-correct:** the performance
  rationale (`O(pages)` per command), the `debug_assertions` gating decision,
  and the before/after-state design (`base_page_tree_walked`) are untouched and
  correct. The block's own *"# ★ What it would and would NOT have caught, stated
  honestly"* section is the natural home for the addition — it already
  enumerates the guard's reach and is where a future engineer decides whether a
  new postcondition should be a `debug_assert` or a real refusal.

- **★★ Survivor 4 — a Pass mis-stamp, small but exactly the class.**
  `edit.rs:25234` now reads *"the leaves, the nodes above them, **and the

**Nothing was edited in `crates/`, `fuzz/` or `.github/` by this filing.**

#### ★★★ THE GATE SWEEP — THE TWO RUNS DISAGREED, AND THE TREE HAD A SECOND WRITER

The dispatch reported `bash tools/run-gates.sh` **PASS on all 30 commands** at
`e77459b`, `check-core-api-verbs` included. Re-run here, twice, it did not
reproduce that on the first attempt. **All four figures below are measurements
taken here, with their times, per hard rule 8's "a check has a timestamp".**

| time (measured, `stat`/`git log`) | event | result |
|---|---|---|
| 18:30:57 | `e77459b` committed | — |
| **18:43:09** | **gate sweep 1 completes** | ★ **FAILED 1 of 30 — `cargo test --workspace`.** Filing gates **clean** (see deferral note) |
| 18:51:47 | `cargo test --workspace` standalone, exit code captured | **exit 0** — 1,912 + ~380 tests over 40 binaries + doctests, `0 failed` |
| **18:52:52** | **`c17f1b5` (`Pass 185.2`) committed by the engineer** | — |
| **19:00:24** | **gate sweep 2 completes**, full log retained | `cargo test --workspace` **PASSED**; FAILED 2 of 30 — **`check-commits-filed.py` + `check-passes-filed.py`**, which is **correct and expected**: this filing is what discharges them |

★★★★ **THE EXPLANATION IS NOT "FLAKY" — THE TREE HAD TWO WRITERS.** Sweep 1
ran in the window immediately before `c17f1b5`, while the engineer was editing
`crates/pdfce-core/src/edit.rs`, running
`cargo test --workspace --all-features`, and running a seeded fuzz campaign —
**in the same working tree and the same `target/` directory.** A sweep run
against a tree another agent is writing to measures **neither the commit nor the
tree**. The same-day precedent is one filing old: the 348th recorded
*"a `git status` taken at the start of a filing is a MEASUREMENT WITH A SHELF
LIFE"*. **This filing hit it twice — once mid-sweep, once mid-filing — and the
second time it moved a VERDICT** (see `Pass 185.2`'s opening).

★★★ **AND THE SELF-INFLICTED HALF, WHICH IS THE TRANSFERABLE ONE.** Sweep 1's
failure **cannot be diagnosed, because this role piped it through `| tail -25`**
and kept only the summary. The failing test's entire output was discarded by the
observer. **That is the same defect as `Pass 185.1`'s own open item** — an
observation harness that cannot report the input that produced a failure — and
**the engineer independently hit the third instance of it in `Pass 185.2`**
(`tail -40` on a fuzz capture, keeping the bottom of a backtrace instead of the
panic head). Three harnesses, three tools, one day, two agents who had not
spoken. See the table in `Pass 185.2`. ⇒ **Never pipe a gate sweep or a fuzz run
through `tail`; redirect to a file and grep the file for the head.**

★★ **A MECHANIC WORTH KNOWING, because it explains the dispatch's PASS-30 and
is easy to misread as a contradiction.** `check-passes-filed` / `check-commits-filed`
**DEFER the tip commit** — *"a commit cannot cite its own hash; its filing is a
later commit"*. So in sweep 1, with `e77459b` at the tip, both filing gates were
**clean**; in sweep 2, with `c17f1b5` at the tip, `e77459b` was no longer the tip
and was reported **UNFILED**. ⇒ **A `run-gates.sh` PASS-30 taken AT the tip is
not evidence that the tip is filed** — it is evidence that the question was
deferred. Both the dispatch's PASS-30 for `e77459b` and `c17f1b5`'s own PASS-30
are true readings *and* say nothing about filing, which is precisely why this
filing exists. **The gate is behaving exactly as designed; the misreading would
be the reader's.**

The engineer's reading was **no change**; this role agrees, and the *why* is
written down because **"no change" and "not checked" look identical in an absent
note** — the failure this file's maintenance contract exists to prevent. Two
halves, unticked for **different** reasons:

   ("Delete a field, a single widget, or a grouping node…") describes what an
   operator can do with a **well-formed** document, and that is unchanged. The

   line 227 (*"refuses a signed signature field before removing anything"*) —
   and both are reachable on a **valid** document in ordinary use.

   the catalog, a shape **no real producer has been observed to emit**
   (decision `110`). Adding it lengthens an already-overlong row for a case no
   operator meets. ★ **If decision `110`'s flip condition is met — a named
   producer emitting the shape — this row changes. That is the trigger to
   watch.**
2. **Test infrastructure has never been a row here and should not become one.**
   Measured: `grep -i fuzz docs/FEATURES.md` → **0 rows**, against **27**
   existing fuzz targets. A fuzz target is not something an operator can reach;
   ticking `core` for it would break the file's own ticking bar.

**Net: 0 rows changed, 0 boxes ticked across both Passes, and neither is an
oversight.**

#### ★★ THE STANDING RECOMMENDATION — LEFT OPEN FOR THE OPERATOR, AND THIS PASS IS A SECOND DATA POINT *AGAINST* SCHEDULING BEING SUFFICIENT

The 348th filing's recommendation stands **unchanged and unexecuted**: add a
*"what schedules this?"* clause to `.claude/agents/pdfce-librarian.md`. The
engineer's ruling is correct: *"I agree with the argument and it is not mine to
add."* **Amending an agent file is the operator's act** — the same boundary hard
rule 9 draws around the user's global config, and the same one that produced
rule 11's two amendments (drafted by this role, declined unilaterally, added by
the engineer when he asked). It stays here, on the append-only record, for Ken.

★★★ **And the engineer added the observation that matters most, pointing the
opposite way from the one the recommendation assumes.** The fuzz-gate lesson
**was** scheduled — it lives in his agent memory *and* in the standing "always"
list — **and it still took saying it out loud in a handoff before he acted.**
Recorded twice, recurred twice.

⇒ **Scheduling is NECESSARY and, on this evidence, NOT SUFFICIENT.** That is
sharper than the recommendation and does not weaken it: an unscheduled lesson
has *no* mechanism, a scheduled one has a *weak* mechanism, and the gap between
them is the whole distance from zero. But a future filing must not read *"add
the clause"* as *"and then it will act"*. **Two data points now sit on opposite
sides of the same rule** — `Pass 185.0` showed an unscheduled lesson failing to
act, `Pass 185.1` shows a scheduled one failing to act — and both belong in
front of Ken when he rules. ★ **`R236` is this filing's attempt at the other
half**: a trigger keyed on an artefact you can `grep` for, rather than on
anybody remembering.

#### ★★★★ WHAT THE GATE CHECKS — AND THE REFUSAL IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART

Two rules, both decidable from the YAML alone
(`tools/check-ci-job-names.py`, `DECLARE_THRESHOLD = 8`):

1. a job running **more than 8** `run:` steps must declare a count as
   `(N checks)`;
2. **any declared count must equal the actual `run:` step count.**

**Rule 2 is load-bearing and rule 1 alone would have been another lesson.** A
collective name is honest on the day it is written and stays honest by doing
nothing; **the COUNT is the part that decays**, and a stale count is a claim a
gate can falsify.

★★ **It deliberately does NOT judge whether a name fairly describes its job.**
That is not decidable from text — a two-step job named after one step is fair
when the second step is a detail of the first — and a gate that pretended
otherwise would fail on honest names and get silenced (`R209`'s territory, and
`a_warning_that_fires_when_nothing_is_wrong_gets_ignored_when_something_is.md`).
**The general shape, which is the part that travels: where a judgement is not
mechanisable, gate the NUMBER attached to the judgement instead.** The judgement
stays with the author; what the gate removes is the case where **nobody made it
at all** — which is exactly how a 1-step job reached 19 steps under its original
name.

**The threshold is a judgement and is stated as one, from a measurement.** The
workflow's jobs run **1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 6 and 20** commands (re-counted here
from `ci.yml`, not relayed). Every job at 6 or below has a name fairly covering
all its steps — six `cargo tree` invocations under *"verify pdfce-core /
pdfce-render have zero GUI deps"* is **one subject, not six**. The gap between 6
and the outlier is where the misdirection bites. Raising the threshold silences
the gate; lowering it forces collective names onto jobs that do not need them.

#### ★★★ VERIFICATION — AND THE ENGINEER'S SABOTAGES AND THIS ROLE'S TEST DIFFERENT THINGS

Re-run here, verbatim:

```

and every declared count is right.

run-gates: PASS — 30 command(s), including 2 filing gate(s).
```

The `--self-test`'s four cases were read rather than trusted: a 1-step job needs
no declaration (**not** reported), a 19-step job with no declaration (reported),
a **correct** declaration (not reported), a **wrong** count (reported). ★ **A
gate whose own logic is untested can silently check nothing — the exact class
this Pass is about — so the self-test is not ceremony here.**

**Independent sabotage, run in this filing** through the module's own

| count made stale, `(20 checks)` → `(19 checks)` | ★ **CAUGHT** — *"says '(19 checks)' and runs 20"* |
| ★★ **one `run:` step appended to the job** | ★★ **CAUGHT** — *"says '(20 checks)' and runs 21"* |

★★ **The fourth row is the one that matters, and it is not in the engineer's

verification owes a test that fires the trigger, not only one that observes its

#### ★★★★ THE FINDING ABOVE THE PASS — A LESSON NOBODY SCHEDULED IS A LESSON THAT DOES NOT ACT

The 345th filing minted `Pass 185.0` on the strength of a RAG file written

correct, complete and actionable on the day it was written, and in the eighteen

**5 → 7**. **Writing it down a second time would have produced a third correct
file** — and that is the trap, because *record it better* is the reflex a
recurrence produces, and recording is the thing that already failed.

⇒ ★★ **THE ACTIONABLE HALF IS A QUESTION TO ASK OF EVERY FINDING AT FILING
TIME: "what schedules this?"** If the answer is *"a future session will read
it"*, **that is the same answer the 2026-08-12 file had**, and it is not an
answer. A schedule is a work item in the tracker of whoever owns the file, a
gate that fails, or a line in a document read **unconditionally** — not a
document read when somebody greps for it. **A RAG file is an ANSWER; it is not
an APPOINTMENT.**

was addressed to **nobody in particular**, and sixteen steps were appended
without anyone reading it. The remedy that finally worked converted exactly that
sentence into a condition a machine evaluates on every push.

**Criterion B, as this role wrote it in the 344th filing and as

than a patch."*

★★ **Every clause of that was true and the whole of it was beside the point.**
The engineer's own account, accepted here:

| walk | question it answers | consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `forms::scan_javascript` | ★ *"what would a reader actually RUN?"* | **CARRIERS** — an action nothing can reach runs never, so unreachable actions are correctly excluded |
| this Pass's sweep | ★ *"what strings in this file NAME this field?"* | ★★ **the OBJECT UNIVERSE** — an action in an object no carrier reaches still holds the stale name, and rewriting it is harmless and right |

⇒ **The sweep is a strict SUPERSET of the carrier walk and therefore cannot
under-report relative to it.** It is not the narrower second walker the
criterion refused; it is a broader one answering a different question, it
shares no traversal with `scan_javascript`, and **merging them would make
neither more correct.** `scan_javascript` is **untouched** — verified here:
`b62e069`'s diff to `forms.rs` is `+237` and adds a new region, with no hunk
inside `scan_javascript`.

★★★ **THE GENERALISABLE SHAPE, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS FILED AND NOT JUST THE
OUTCOME.** The engineer's own words, and this role wrote the plan he is
correcting:

> *"I let the DIFFICULTY of the obvious implementation stand in for the
> difficulty of the problem."*

**The refactor was correctly assessed as risky.** The risk assessment was
sound, the `Pass 133.0` history was real, the anti-second-walker rule was
correctly cited. **All of it was reasoning about an implementation nobody
needed to write.** ⇒ **A hard implementation is evidence that the
implementation is hard. It is not evidence about the problem**, and the two
get conflated precisely when the hard implementation is the first one that
comes to mind — because its difficulty is vivid and the alternative has not
been thought of yet.

★★ **The diagnostic, in the form a future session can apply before committing
to a refactor:** *state the question the existing machinery answers, and the
question you actually need answered, as two sentences side by side.* If they
differ, **reuse is a coincidence, not an economy** — and the anti-duplication
rule (which is real, and which this project does keep re-learning) **does not
apply between two components that answer different questions.**

#### ★★ FINDING 3 — A SURVIVING SABOTAGE IS NOT ALWAYS A WEAK TEST: THREE REASONS, THREE REMEDIES

**Four sabotages; two of the first attempts survived, for reasons that are not
the same reason.** The project's corpus — the engineer's own
`feedback_sabotage_catches_false_comments`, and this role's several *"a
surviving sabotage means…"* notes — reads as though survival implies a weak
test. ★★ **It does not, and distinguishing the three is what turns a survival
into information rather than an accusation.**

| # | why it survived | ★ what it actually meant | remedy |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ★★ **the assertion could not SEE the change** — `saved()` returns the base bytes **plus** the incremental update, so `contains("(Name)")` was satisfied by the base's own `/T (Name)` **whatever the sweep did** | **a vacuous assertion.** The one genuine weak test of the three | re-assert on the discriminating shape (`/Fields [(Name)]`), not on a substring the base already contains |
| 2 | ★★★ **the guarantee is enforced SOMEWHERE ELSE** — `delete_field` discards the sweep's writes with `_`, so **no argument passed *to* the sweep can make it repair** | **the code is STRUCTURALLY correct.** The sabotage was inert because the property is not the sweep's to violate | move the sabotage to the **enforcement point** — remove the discard. That one is **CAUGHT** |
| 3 | ★★ **the mutation was semantically NULL** — treating `/JS` as a target list changes nothing on its own, because the script text matches no field name | **the defect is a CONJUNCTION**, not a single edit | compose it: greedy-substring matching **and** `/JS`-as-target together are the plausible error. Combined: **CAUGHT** |

★★★ **The polarity table the corpus already carries gets a fourth row.** The
existing taxonomy in
`a_sabotage_that_does_not_compile_or_change_behavior_measures_nothing_verify_the_mutation_before_trusting_the_catch.md`
runs: vacuous gate ⇒ false PASS; unfired sabotage ⇒ false *"weak"*;
wrong-oracle sabotage ⇒ false *"strong"*. ⇒ **Add: a sabotage against a
structurally-enforced guarantee ⇒ a false *"weak"* aimed at code that is
CORRECT BY CONSTRUCTION — the one case where the honest response is to write
the reason down and stop, not to strengthen the test.** Strengthening a test
against a guarantee it cannot reach produces a test that asserts a tautology.

★ **The uncomfortable half, in the engineer's own words:** *"the same trap had
bitten a different test in the same file twenty minutes earlier and I walked
into it again."* ⇒ **The append-only-artifact trap is not learned by meeting
it once**, which is the argument for it being a corpus entry with a name rather
than a remembered incident. Escalated to `D:/dev/rag/rust/` as its own file:
**an assertion over an append-only artefact cannot see what the base already
contained.** ★★ **This generalises past PDF** — incremental save, append-only
logs, `tar` append, event stores: `contains()` over the whole artefact is a
**union** query, and a union query cannot falsify anything about the newest
member.

**after** the preceding field and inserted a doc block **without its `pub`
line**, so the doc landed on top of the **next** field's doc block. **The
compiler caught it (E0560, twice) only because the constructors referenced the
missing field.** ⇒ ★★ **The compiler was a COINCIDENTAL oracle here, not a
guard.** A doc-only insertion — the commonest kind of edit this role and the
engineer both make — has **no constructor to break** and would have shipped
silently, leaving one field's documentation attached to another field.

recorded, the **new fact is the oracle's coincidence**.

first that is not a transit failure.** Every prior instance is *"a continuation
backslash is lost in transit"* (heredoc, shell, patch). ★★ **This one survived

#### Design decisions — one minted as `109`, the rest recorded here

★★ **Decision `109` is minted** for the repair-versus-disclose asymmetry —
`ARCHITECTURE.md` §12 carries it in full. Short form: **pdfce repairs when it
knows the answer exactly and discloses when repair would require inventing
intent.** A rename supplies both names, so the rewrite is a substitution; a
delete supplies nothing, and dropping the entry would change what the button
does **to the fields that remain**. **Same traversal, opposite conclusion** —
matching `DeleteOutcome::dangling`'s existing report-don't-repair posture for
bookmarks and links. ★ **It is minted because a future session will read the
two verbs as an inconsistency and "fix" it**, which is the only way this
asymmetry can be lost.

Recorded here rather than as decisions, because each is a consequence of `109`
or of an existing rule:

- ★ **The rename's writes ride in the SAME undoable command as the `/T`
  write**, so undo restores the name and the buttons together and **no save can
  contain one without the other.** A separate command would have made a
  half-undone rename reachable.
- ★★ **Two passes, because `/Fields` may be an indirect reference to an array
  object.** The traversal deliberately does **not** follow references — that is
  exactly what lets a per-object sweep be complete without a graph walk — so it
  **reports** those ids (`DeferredTargetList`) and a second pass visits them,
  **deduped, because one array may be shared by several actions.** ⇒ **Missing
  this repairs MOST buttons, which reads as repairing all of them** — the
  worst available outcome, since a partial repair removes the operator's reason
  to check. There is a fixture whose `/Fields` is indirect: **a shape no pdfce
  verb authors and real producers do**, which is why it needed a fixture rather
  than a round-trip. ⇒ Escalated to `C:\personal_rag\pdf\`.
- **JavaScript is never rewritten** (`R55` — every script carrier round-trips
  byte-identical). ⇒ **`action_targets_orphaned` is a FLOOR for scripted forms,
  not a total**, and the disclosures say so. Rewriting inside a script is *"a
  corruption with good intentions that surfaces when a form stops
  calculating"*.
- ★★ **The separator is the whole prefix rule.** `Name.` is an ancestor path;
  `Name` alone is a string that happens to start the same way. The fixture
  carries **`Name` AND `Nameless`**, so without the dot an action naming
  `Nameless` is rewritten to `Renamedless` — **a field that does not exist, on
  a button nobody touched.** Sabotage-checked, caught.
- ★★★ **`actions_not_retargeted` was superseded SIX HOURS after shipping, and
  the supersession is recorded in the TYPE rather than applied silently.** The
  old name **will not compile**. ⇒ **An upper bound is worth stating only while
  the exact answer does not exist**; once it does, leaving the bound in place
  is a second, weaker answer to a question that now has one. ★ **The test that
  pinned it was REWRITTEN, not deleted** — it now asserts the property the
  categorical version could not express: *an action naming a different field
  reports `0`*, where the old number would have said `1`.

heading and a table, read the prose between them before you stop.***

#### What shipped

`ButtonAction::SetHidden { targets: Vec<String>, hidden: bool }`, plus
`pdfce-cli set-button-action --hide A,B | --show A,B`. Written from
`iso32000__s__12.6.4.10.md` (Table 210), **ingested by `pdfce-spec-librarian`
for this Pass, before any code was written** — the ordering matters and is
recorded because it is the ordering `CLAUDE.md` rule 1 asks for and rarely
gets.

**Why it exists at all.** `Pass 183.0` shipped `/SubmitForm`, `/GoTo`,
`/Named` and `/URI` under the operator's ruling — *"the submit and **other
options that don't need javascript**"* — and **omitted `/Hide` by accident,
not by decision**: `docs/plan-scripting-submit-and-plugins.md` §8 Phase 1,
written four days earlier, did not list it, and the Pass built to the plan.
★ **A show/hide button is the second-commonest script-free button on a real
form after reset**, so the omission took out the set's most-wanted surviving
member.

⇒ **The failure mode is worth naming, because it will recur: a
citation-shaped ruling (*"the safeguards like we had planned"*) makes the
cited plan authoritative for SCOPE as well as for safeguards — and the plan
was never written to be a complete enumeration.** A document cited for one
purpose silently became the boundary of another. **The defence is not "read
the plan harder"**; it is to derive the *set* from the standard (which is
what this Pass did, arriving at the closed eight below) rather than from the
plan that happened to be cited.

#### ★★★ TRAP 1 — `/H`'s DEFAULT IS `true`, SO THE ORDINARY REFLEX AUTHORS A *SHOW* BUTTON THAT *HIDES*

Verbatim, and identical in both editions:

> *"A flag indicating whether to hide the annotation (true) or show it
> (false). **Default value: true.**"*

⇒ **An action that OMITS `/H` hides.** The universal reflex — *write the flag
when it is set, leave it out when it is clear* — produces a Show button that
hides, **and the file is perfectly conforming**, so no validator, no
round-trip check and no census this project owns would ever flag it.

- pdfce writes `/H` **explicitly in both directions**. Measured on the shipped
  binary: `--show` emits `/S /Hide /T [(FullName) (Subscribe)] /H false`.
- ★ **The CLI spells `--hide` and `--show` as two flags rather than one flag
  with a modifier for the same reason**: *"show" has to be written out to
  exist*, and an argument surface where the show case is the **absent** case
  reproduces the identical bug one layer up.
- **Sabotage-checked** — writing `/H` only when hiding is caught.

★★ **The generalizable half, and it is why this is escalated rather than left
in a doc comment: a boolean whose spec default is `true` INVERTS the
absent-means-off convention that every other flag in the format trains you
into.** The hazard is not that it is hard — it is that the wrong
implementation is **easy, conforming, and invisible to every mechanical check
available**. Captured cross-project as a `personal_rag/pdf` lesson (see
*Findings escalated*, below).

#### ★★★ TRAP 2 — TABLE 210 HAS NO DESCENDANT RULE, AND BOTH ITS NEIGHBOURS DO. REFUSED, NOT DEFAULTED — AND THAT IS A CARVE-OUT FROM A STANDING OPERATOR DIRECTIVE

`/ResetForm` and `/SubmitForm` both state descendant expansion in their flag
rows — *"all descendants of the specified fields in the field hierarchy"*. The
phrase was **measured**, not recalled: **2 hits per edition, both times on a
`/Fields` row, NEVER on Table 210.**

⇒ **What a grouping (non-terminal) name means to a hide action is genuinely
undefined**, and the two readings — *hide the subtree* and *hide nothing* —
differ by everything. **Refused by name**
(`EditError::ButtonActionHideTargetNotTerminal`) rather than defaulted.
**Sabotage-checked** — accepting a grouping node is caught.

★★★ **WHY THIS IS *NOT* THE STANDING "TWO DEFENSIBLE ANSWERS → SHIP BOTH, PICK
A DEFAULT" POSTURE.** The engineer asked for this on the record because a
future session will reasonably ask — and the question deserves a **criterion**,
not a precedent.

The standing directive is the operator's own, and it is global rather than
pdfce-specific: **"never hard-code a choice the standard leaves open"** — make
spec ambiguity a setting. Read literally it applies here. Applying it here
would be wrong.

| | the ordinary spec ambiguity | ★ **this one** |
|---|---|---|
| reading A | produces a document | produces a document |
| reading B | produces a **different** document | ★ **produces a button that does NOTHING** |
| can the operator tell which he got? | **yes — he inspects the output** | ★ **no. Both readings emit a conforming `/Hide` action. The difference appears only when a *reader* presses the button, in software pdfce does not control and cannot observe** |
| is a default defensible? | **yes** — a wrong default is visible, and therefore reversible | ★ **no** — a wrong default is **silence**, which is the one outcome rule 4 exists to prevent |

⇒ **The criterion, stated so it is reused rather than re-derived: "make it a
setting" PRESUPPOSES that both readings produce something the operator can
inspect. When one reading produces SILENCE, the ambiguity is not a
configuration axis — it is a thing the standard did not define, and pdfce
refuses to pick.** A setting whose wrong position is undetectable is not a
setting; it is a coin flip with a knob drawn on it.

**Filed as decision `108`** (`ARCHITECTURE.md` §12) rather than left as a code
comment, because it **narrows a standing operator directive**, and this project
records those with the directive quoted rather than paraphrased.

#### ★★ AN *ASSIGNMENT*, NOT A TOGGLE — A CAPABILITY BOUNDARY, NOT A GAP

Table 210: the action works *"by setting or clearing their Hidden flags"*, with
`/H` as a **value**. ★ **The standard OWNS a toggle — `/SetOCGState`'s `/State`
has `ToggleNoView` — and did not use it here.** That is a choice **by the
standard**, not an omission by pdfce.

⇒ **A genuinely toggling show/hide button REQUIRES ECMAScript**, which puts it
**out of pdfce's scope entirely** (`R53`, `NF4`) rather than merely unbuilt.
**Recorded as a boundary so a future session does not open it as a gap** and
spend a Pass rediscovering it. The CLI says so on every run, because *"pressing
it twice puts it back"* is exactly what an operator will assume.

#### ★★ THE COUNT THAT IS NOT THE ONE YOU EXPECT — WIDGETS, NOT NAMES

**SOURCED**, not inferred: an FQN reaches *"the associated widget annotation
**or annotations**"* — **every widget of that field, on every page**.

⇒ **`HideDisclosure::widgets_affected` is usually LARGER than the number of
names**, and it is the number of things that will actually move.
**Sabotage-checked** — counting names instead of widgets is caught.

**Filed in the form hard rule 10(a) requires** — the figure beside its
per-item form, with the denominator stated: measured on the shipped release
binary, `--show FullName,Subscribe` reports **2 fields affecting 2 widgets =
1 widget per field**. ★ **That ratio is exactly 1 here, which is the *simple*
case — and it is precisely why a test corpus of simple files cannot
distinguish the two counters from each other.** The sabotage check, not the
corpus, is what separates them.

**`targets_without_widgets`** names fields owning no widget: the action is
**authored anyway** and the fact **disclosed**. ★ **Refusing would be pdfce
inventing a reader rule the standard does not state** — the same discipline
that produced the `http` non-refusal in `Pass 183.0`, and worth naming as the
**second instance in two Passes** of one principle: *pdfce refuses for
decidability, never for taste.*

**The name form reaches WIDGETS ONLY.** A `/Text` note, a stamp or a **ce
dimension**'s `/Line` is nameable only by indirect reference, so hiding one is
not expressible here. Deliberate: an object-id-valued target is not something a
form editor's UI can offer safely, and it is not what was asked for.

#### ★ THE FRAMING CORRECTION THIS ROLE SUPPLIED, AND WHAT IT PREVENTS

**"Script-free" and "reaches nothing" are two predicates, not one.**
`SubmitForm` and `Uri` satisfy only the first — **deliberately** — and that
asymmetry is the *entire reason* `SubmitDisclosure` exists.

⇒ **Collapsing them is how a reader concludes the variant list is arbitrary —
or, far worse, that a submit is as inert as a reset.** Now a table in
`ButtonAction`'s doc block.

**And the set is CLOSED, so this is a boundary rather than six arbitrary
picks.** ISO 32000-1 defines **eight** action types that are both script-free
and reach-nothing (2.0 adds a ninth); **pdfce authors four of them** — `GoTo`,
`Hide`, `ResetForm`, `Named`. The four it does not are **sized** in the doc
block rather than left unexplained: `/SetOCGState` (a run-length sequence
grammar over `/OCProperties /OCGs` plus `/PreserveRB` against `/RBGroups` —
**not** an OCG name tree, which was the dispatch's guess and was corrected by
the spec-librarian), `/Trans` (Table 162, and pointless standalone — it acts
only *"during a sequence of actions"*, making it a `/Next` companion rather
than a button's action), `/GoTo3DView` (3D annotations pdfce does not model),
`/GoToDp` (the PDF 2.0 document-part model). `/Sound` is **excluded from that
count for a stated reason** rather than overlooked: any stream may carry `/F`
(Table 5), so it can reach a file, and 2.0 deprecates it.

⇒ **`FEATURES.md` gets the closed-set fact as a SENTENCE, not a *Planned*
row** — the engineer's lean, and this role agrees with a reason worth stating:
**a *Planned* row is a promise.** Nobody has asked for any of the four. A row
would make `FEATURES.md` predict work that is not queued, which is the opposite
of the scan it is contracted to be, and would be read as a commitment at the
next roadmap review.

#### ★★★ THE COUNT CORRECTION — THE DISPATCH SAID FIVE, THE `enum` SAYS SIX, AND TWO TREES STILL SAY FIVE

The dispatch instructed: *"add `/Hide`, i.e. the action set is now **five**
kinds."* **That is wrong, and it was caught by counting rather than by
reading.** `ButtonAction`'s variants, read live from
`crates/pdfce-core/src/edit.rs`:

| # | variant | writes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ResetForm` | `/S /ResetForm` |
| 2 | `SubmitForm` | `/S /SubmitForm` |
| 3 | `GoToPage` | `/S /GoTo` |
| 4 | `Named` | `/S /Named` |
| 5 | ★ **`SetHidden`** | ★ **`/S /Hide`** — added by this Pass |
| 6 | `Uri` | `/S /URI` |

⇒ **SIX.** *Five* was the count **before** this Pass, and `FEATURES.md` row 221
already said *five* **correctly** — so the instruction *"add `/Hide`, the set is
now five"* would have **added the new item and left the number untouched**.

★★★ **That is the most dangerous shape a stale figure takes: an edit that
touches the sentence around a number and leaves the number itself.** The
resulting line reads as **freshly confirmed** rather than as missed, because
the prose beside it is visibly current. **A number that survives an edit to its
own sentence is harder to catch than one nobody has looked at in months.**

**The correction names its world-source** (hard rule 10's corollary — *a
correction is a claim*): `sed -n '13440,13560p'
crates/pdfce-core/src/edit.rs`, run in this filing, variants counted off the
`enum` body.

★★★ **SURVIVOR 2 IS THE SAME DEFECT `a168061` WAS COMMITTED TO FIX — SAME DAY,
SAME SESSION, HOURS APART.** That commit's own message names the class:

> *"A correction that reaches a status block and stops short of the prose is

⇒ **The rule was minted, the sweep was run, the commit was made — and the next
edit reproduced the class within hours, in a different file.** Filed **not as
blame but as evidence about the class**: **naming a defect does not inoculate
the next edit against it.** That is the same lesson hard rule 11's own
corollary already records (*"naming the failure does not perform the check"*),
and this is its clearest instance yet, because the interval between the naming
and the recurrence is measured in hours rather than filings.

★ **Note also which half was updated in survivor 2 and which was not.** The
**structured** halves — the heading and the table — were both correct; the
**prose count between them** was not. **`a168061`'s finding was that
corrections reach status blocks and stop short of prose. Survivor 2 is that
finding happening again in a file the same session was editing**, and it
suggests the mechanism is not carelessness but **attention following
structure**: a table row is a slot that visibly wants filling, and a number in
a sentence is not.

★★★ **THE RULING, GIVEN PLAINLY BECAUSE THAT IS WHAT WAS ASKED FOR.**

The operator's standing rule is *"fix bugs on discovery; **never file a found
bug for later**."* The engineer judged this **a sequencing call rather than a
deferral**, on the ground that the fix is a **refactor** rather than a
correction. **This filing agrees IN HALF — and the other half is a distinction
the dispatch did not draw:**

- ★ **The REPAIR may be sequenced. ACCEPTED, on the engineer's own argument.**
  A narrow second walker would ship the very defect class the refactor exists
  to remove, so *"fix it now"* would mean *"fix it wrongly now"*. **The rule's
  purpose is not served by a worse fix arriving sooner.**
- ★★★ **The DISCLOSURE may NOT be sequenced, and deferring it IS a deferral,
  not a sequencing call.** Between now and `Pass 184.0`, an operator who
  renames a field gets **a broken form and no report**. That is not a latent
  bug awaiting a refactor — it is **live silence**, and rule 4's one binding
  obligation is *non-silence about what the operator cannot see*. ⇒ **On the
  strict reading, the Pass as shipped crosses the operator's rule — and it
  crosses it on the DISCLOSURE, not on the repair.**
- ★★ **AND THE INTERIM IS CHEAP, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THE DEFERRAL
  INDEFENSIBLE RATHER THAN MERELY IMPERFECT.** A **categorical** disclosure
  needs **no traversal at all**, therefore **no visitor and no refactor**:
  *"renaming a field does not update `/ResetForm`, `/SubmitForm` or `/Hide`
  action targets that name it; a button naming the old name will stop
  working."* A **counted** disclosure needs the walk. A **stated limitation**
  needs one sentence. ⇒ **The refactor argument justifies deferring the COUNT.
  It does not justify deferring the SENTENCE** — and the two were folded
  together in the dispatch, which is how the whole item came to look
  refactor-blocked.

⇒ **RECOMMENDATION, the actionable half of this ruling: ship the CATEGORICAL
disclosure NOW, ahead of `Pass 184.0`, as a docs-and-report change requiring no
visitor.** `Pass 184.0` then upgrades it from *categorical* to
*counted-and-repaired*. That discharges the operator's rule immediately, costs
one sentence on each of three surfaces, and leaves the refactor properly
scoped. **Filed as `Pass 184.0`'s FIRST acceptance criterion, ahead of the
refactor, so it cannot be absorbed into it and disappear.**

★ **Recorded for the next reader of the operator's rule**, since this is the
first time this project has tested it against a refactor: **the rule bites on
SILENCE, not on code.** *"Fix bugs on discovery"* is satisfiable by disclosing
a defect you have not yet repaired, and is **not** satisfiable by repairing one
you never mention. Where the two halves separate — as here — **the disclosure
is the half that is due immediately**, and the repair is the half that may be
scheduled on engineering grounds.
