#### CAUSE, AND IT IS THE SAME ONE AT THE OTHER CALL SITE

`gate_synthesis` surveys the page against `text` and refuses synthesis when a
real face *"resolves"*. With an empty `find` that survey checks **zero
characters**, so **every face passes**. `survey_page_fonts` has **exactly two
call sites**; `Pass 147.0` fixed one of them.

**Both halves were present**, exactly as reported:

1. **PINNED + empty** — `find_anchor` locates by the pin without reading
   `find`; the survey then checks nothing and `find_styled_face` returns
   whatever it reaches first.
2. **UNPINNED + empty** — `find_anchor` runs `s.text.contains(find)`, and
   **every string contains the empty string**, so it matches the page's **first
   show operator** and the answer is about an operator the caller never named.

#### FIX, AND THE JUDGEMENT THIS ROLE FLAGGED AS THE ENGINEER'S — MADE, WITH ITS REASONING

`preview_style_resolution` calls **`effective_find`**, and refuses an unpinned
empty `find` with **the same sentence** `match_run`, `plan_format`,
`plan_edit` and `preview_font_resources` all use (`EditError::Unsupported("empty
find text")`).

**★★ THE UNPINNED REFUSAL IS A BEHAVIOUR CHANGE FOR AN EXISTING CALLER AND IT
IS RIGHT.** The 299th filing's *Next up* box deliberately did not prescribe it;
the engineer's reasoning, recorded verbatim in `f1a88e6`:

> *"Today that call returns a wrong answer about the page's FIRST show operator
> — every string contains the empty string, so `find_anchor` matches it. An
> error is strictly better than a routing decision about an operator the caller
> never named, and a third behaviour across five entry points would be a third
> thing to remember."*

**Two independent arguments, and the second is the one worth carrying.** The
first is about *this* call (an error beats a wrong answer). The second is about
**the set**: with four entry points already agreeing on two behaviours, a third
behaviour is not a smaller change than a refusal — **it is a permanent cost on
every future reader of any of the five.** ⇒ ***When a change would give one
member of a uniform set a third behaviour, count the cost against the SET, not
against the member.***

**Rule 11 (CLI parity) does not apply**, stated so the omission reads as
reasoned: `preview_style_resolution` has **no `pdfce-cli` subcommand** (it is a
pure query a shell drives its buttons from), so there is no CLI surface to keep
in step. Its sibling `font-preflight` already shipped its CLI half in
`Pass 147.0`.

---

#### ★★★★★ THE PART THAT IS NOT THE FIX — AND IT IS THE MORE IMPORTANT HALF

**THREE CONSECUTIVE PASSES EACH FIXED ONE ROUTE AND LEFT ANOTHER:**

| Pass | route fixed | route left broken | found by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `145.0` | `plan_format`, `plan_edit` | **both** preview queries | — |
| `147.0` | `preview_font_resources` | `preview_style_resolution` | **a consuming project** |
| `148.0` | `preview_style_resolution` | — | **this role's sweep** |

**★★ NEITHER OF THE LAST TWO WAS FOUND BY THE ENGINEER RE-READING HIS OWN
WORK** — and *within* `147.0` he fixed the pinned half and **assumed** the
unpinned half already errored, caught only by a test written expecting to pass
(`R219` clause (e)'s founding instance, minted one filing ago).

**⇒ ENUMERATING ROUTES FROM THE *FUNCTION* BEING FIXED ENUMERATES THE INSTANCE,
NOT THE CLASS.** `Pass 147.0` enumerated the pinned and unpinned **branches** of
the function it was fixing — and did that well. The sibling **function** taking
the same two operands went unasked **in the commit that was about exactly this
hazard.** The unit of the enumeration has to be **the operand**: *every entry
point that takes it.*

##### The instrument: `crates/pdfce-core/tests/route_enumeration.rs` (+302)

Two assertions, and **only the first is a behaviour test**:

1. **All four entry points behave identically** on pinned-empty, unpinned-empty
   and explicit — checked by calling all of them. **It covers exactly the routes
   somebody remembered to list.** A fifth added next month passes it *by not
   being mentioned.*
2. **★★ EVERY FUNCTION CALLING `find_anchor` ALSO CALLS `effective_find`** — a
   **source scan**, and **the only assertion in the file that can fail on a
   route added after the test was written.**

**★★ THE FIRST CUT OF THE SCAN IS THE FINDING, NOT A FOOTNOTE.** It used a
**30-line window** after each `find_anchor` call and **reported all four
known-good sites as violations** — the resolution legitimately sits **70+ lines
later**, after the font lookup and the error paths. A window wide enough to
admit the four real sites would have been wide enough to admit **anything**.

Rewritten per **function body** — split the module on column-zero `fn`
declarations; any body mentioning `find_anchor(` must mention
`effective_find(`. **No tuning parameter**, and a unit the language already
defines.

> ***A gate with a tuning parameter has exactly one direction of travel under
> pressure — looser — and every turn is locally justified by a true positive it
> was silencing.***

**★ AND THE BAD HEURISTIC FAILED *LOUDLY*, WHICH IS THE ONLY REASON IT WAS
REPLACED.** A lenient window would have **passed forever** and been
**indistinguishable from a working gate** on every green run. ⇒ *When
prototyping a source scan, write the STRICT version first: a false positive
costs an hour, a false negative costs the class the gate was built for.*

**Three details that keep the scan honest** (read here in the test source, not
taken from the commit message):

- **A floor:** `assert!(callers.len() >= 4, …)`. A source scan **goes vacuous
  rather than red** when its anchor identifier is renamed — the loop finds
  nothing and every assertion over an empty set passes. The floor converts a
  rename into a failure.
- **`const EXEMPT: &[&str] = &[]` — empty at birth**, with the comment *"An
  entry here is a claim and owes a reason beside it"* and the instruction
  *"widen the exemption list by name, with a reason — do not delete the test."*
  An exemption is reviewable in the diff; a widened window is not.
- **The definition and `///` mentions are excluded**, so `fn find_anchor` is not
  a caller of itself and a doc comment is not a call — both would be false
  positives, and false positives are what push a later reader to loosen.

**A `ResolvedFind` newtype was considered and declined in the test's own module
doc**, with the reason: it *"changes four signatures to prevent a class that has
now been closed, and the cheap detector comes first."* ⇒ *Reach for the type on
the second firing.*

#### ★★ WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT SWEEPS — THE PROVENANCE IS THE POINT

Every prior hard-rule-11 sweep in this project's record turned up **wording**
that had gone false: a doc comment, a `println!`, a `FEATURES.md` row, a table
header. The 299th filing's turned up **executable code with the same bug the
Pass was closing**, and `Pass 148.0` is that finding shipped.

**★ The strongest evidence yet for the rule's *search-for-the-claim* clause:** a
`grep` for `preview_font_resources` returns `preview_style_resolution`
**zero** times. Nothing textual connected them. What connected them was the
question *"what else decides something from the caller's string?"* — and that
question is only askable by a reader who knows what the change **means**.

**Recorded as a boundary, not as a boast:** the sweep is a **reading**, and it
found this because the meaning-change was fresh in the same filing. It is not a
substitute for the instrument — which is precisely why the instrument
(`route_enumeration.rs` test 2) is the half of this Pass that will still be
working next month.

#### ★★★★ STANDING RULE `R224` — MINTED, ON THE 299th FILING'S OWN TRIGGER, AND THE ARGUMENT IS REACH

The 299th filing **declined** this mint and wrote the condition for revisiting
it, verbatim: *"if it recurs once more in the project record, mint it, and the
argument will be REACH, not count."*

**IT HAS RECURRED IN THE PROJECT RECORD.** `Pass 148.0` is the **third route in
one defect** and the **second miss in eight hours**, filed as a Pass — i.e. in
`ROADMAP.md`, which is what "the project record" meant.

**The decline's three reasons, re-argued against what is now known:**

1. ~~*"The carrier already exists and already fired — it is in the engineer's
   own agent memory, and this instance is already amended into it."*~~
   **FALSIFIED BY MEASUREMENT, and this is the fact the decline could not have
   had.** `.claude/agent-memory/pdfce-engineer/feedback_verify_each_instance_not_the_class.md`
   **was** amended the same night (`9d1f543`) — and
   `grep -c "preview_style_resolution\|148.0"` over it returns **0** (run here).
   The amendment records `Pass 147.0`'s pinned/unpinned split and **stops
   there**; the `preview_style_resolution` route — the worst of the three and
   the one that motivated the instrument — **is not in the carrier the decline
   deferred to.** ⇒ *A carrier that misses the instance that would have proved
   it is not a carrier for that instance.*
2. ~~*"`R219` already owns the project-visible half; this is a clause of it."*~~
   **True of `Pass 147.0`'s finding; not true of this one.** `R219` says
   *enumerate the other routes*; clause (e) says *measure the answers rather
   than recall them*. **Neither says what the enumeration's UNIT is**, and
   neither prescribes an **instrument that covers routes not yet written.**
   Those are the two obligations `Pass 148.0` produced, and they are additions,
   not restatements.
3. ~~*"Minting a rule that duplicates a live memory file would be two
   descriptions of one rule, which is `R221`'s own subject."*~~ **Survives as a
   caution and is answered on the merits.** `R221` is about two **computations**
   of one predicate that can silently drift. A standing rule and an agent-memory
   file are two **audiences**, not two computations — nothing computes from
   either, so neither can drift into a wrong answer. And reason 1 shows the
   concrete cost of the single-carrier arrangement: it went incomplete within
   one session.

**⇒ THE ARGUMENT IS REACH.** `.claude/agent-memory/pdfce-engineer/` is read by
**one agent**. `docs/ROADMAP.md` is read by **every agent and by the operator**.
The two roles that found the last two instances — a **consuming project** and
**this librarian** — can read neither the engineer's memory nor his intentions;
they read this file. **A rule about how wide an enumeration must be is useless
in the one place only the enumerator can see it.**

The rule's full text is in *Standing rules* below. **Ceiling moves
`R223` → `R224`; next free `R225`.**

#### ★★★★★ THE DEFECT, AND WHY AN OVER-PERMISSIVE ANSWER IS THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION

```
preview_font_resources(0, "", Some(pin))
  F1 accepted=true   F2 accepted=true   F3 accepted=true      <- /F3 CANNOT
  text=""            accepted_count=3                            show the run
```

**Three of three accepted; one of the three provably cannot show the run.**
That is the engineer's in-crate probe, run **before the report was believed**
(`R203`), and **nothing in the report needed correcting** — the reporter's trace
was exact at every step.

**The mechanism, now verified rather than relayed** (the 298th filing carried it
under an explicit *"RELAYED, NOT VERIFIED HERE"* label; the engineer's
reproduction and commit message discharge that label):

1. `find_anchor` with `pinned_span` set **never reads `find`** — it matches on
   `pin_names_operator`. An empty `find` therefore **locates the right
   operator, with no error.**
2. `survey_page_fonts(.., find)` passes that same empty string down.
3. `accept_font_target(.., text, ..)` tests coverage with
   `text.chars().zip(encoded.codes.iter())`.
4. **`"".chars()` yields nothing. Zero characters checked, zero refusals found.
   Every entry comes back `Accepted`.**

**★★ WHY THIS IS A PASS AND NOT A DOC LINE — the failure is INVERTED.** An
ordinary defect in a filtering query produces a *shorter* list, a refusal, or a
panic, all of which a caller notices. This one produces a **longer** one. The
consuming shell shows **more** options, nothing errors, nothing logs. And the
query exists **precisely** to stop offering faces that cannot work, so **the
control built to prevent a downstream refusal became the thing producing it.**

**★ It is strictly worse than the heuristic it replaced, and the comparison is
the reporter's own.** `pdfceGUI`'s deleted `fontinfo` name-join superset was at
least *a superset of the page's fonts, by name*. **An unconditional yes is not
related to the real set at all.** ⇒ ***"Returns more than it should" is a
HIGH-severity failure mode for an acceptance query, not benign noise*** — which
is the generalisation this filing sends to `D:/dev/rag/rust/`.

#### ★★★ THE SECOND HALF, WHICH THE FIRST CUT ASSUMED AWAY — AND IT IS THE MORE REACHABLE ONE

The engineer fixed the **pinned** case and *reasoned* that an **unpinned** empty
`find` already errored, because `match_run` refuses one on the commit path.
**A test proved otherwise:**

> `find_anchor` with no pin runs `s.text.contains(find)` — and **every string
> contains the empty string.**

So `preview_font_resources(page, "", None)` **silently matched the FIRST show
operator on the page** and surveyed against zero characters: the same silent,
inverted failure, **about an operator the caller never named**, and reachable
**without a pin at all** — i.e. *by accident* rather than by following
documentation, which makes it the **more** likely of the two to be hit.

It is now **refused, reusing the sentence `match_run` has used since
`Pass 14.1`** rather than a second spelling of it — itself an `R221`-shaped
choice one layer down (one refusal sentence, not two that drift).

**★★ BOTH OF THE REPORTER'S OFFERED REMEDIES WERE NEEDED, AND THEY WERE READ AS
AN EITHER/OR.** Their request offered (1) *resolve the text from the anchor* and
(2) *refuse an empty `find` by name*, with (2) marked as their preference
(*"a refusal we can see beats a list of universal yeses"*). **(1) closes the
pinned half; (2) closes the unpinned half. Neither closes both.** ⇒ ***When a
reporter offers two remedies for one symptom, check whether they cover
different reachability routes before choosing between them.***

⇒ **"Verify each instance, not the class."** Disposition of that recurrence is

  filing said was owed for `preview_font_resources`, stating what an empty

  `Pass 147.0`.**

**★★ THE BYTE-IDENTICAL TEST IS THE ONE TO READ, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT SPECIES
FROM "THE FIX WORKS".** A test asserting *"the pinned-empty query now returns
the right verdicts"* would pass if the two paths were fixed **separately** and
happened to agree today. Asserting **equality of the two outputs** pins the
property the defect actually was: **two functions taking the same two operands
must mean the same thing by them.** ⇒ *When the defect is a DISAGREEMENT between
two paths, the oracle is EQUALITY OF THE TWO OUTPUTS, not correctness of one* —
the same argument the 298th filing recorded for `Pass 146.0`'s round-trip CLI
tests, arriving from the opposite direction (there: *a fixture pins one path and
proves nothing about the pair*).

CHANCE.** `check-string-gaps.sh` found a lost line continuation **in a new
test**, before it shipped. **The previous instance of that class shipped into a
release binary** (`DisplayListStale`, 2026-08-18, found by a librarian sweep
after the fact). ⇒ *This is `R209`(e)'s pay-off and the argument for gates over
care, now with a live catch rather than a rationale.*

**★ SABOTAGE THAT DISCRIMINATES IS BETTER EVIDENCE THAN SABOTAGE THAT REDDENS
EVERYTHING.** The mutation reddened the two tests covering the half it broke and
left the unpinned-refusal test green. A mutation turning **all 13** red would
have shown the tests are coupled to the *file*, not to the *behaviour*. **The

correct reading and is named here so a later session does not "fix" it.

#### ★★ STANDING-RULE DISPOSITION — TWO AMENDMENTS IN PLACE, NO MINT, AND BOTH DECLINES ARE ARGUED

The dispatch asked whether the **"verify each instance, not the class"**
recurrence earns anything, and asked for the decision to be **argued rather than
defaulted**. It does not earn a mint. Two existing rules are amended instead.

**(1) `R221` — amended in place, fourth instance.** New information, not a
tally: **the first instance found by a consumer rather than from inside**, and
the first where the two drifting descriptions were **a resolution step and a
parameter list** rather than two predicates. Ceiling does **not** move.

**(2) `R219` — amended in place, and this instance CHANGES the rule rather than
counting it.** `R219` reads *"when a Pass fixes one of several routes to the
same behaviour, enumerate the other routes in the same Pass and say explicitly
which are left."* The pinned and unpinned calls **are** two routes to one
behaviour, and the engineer **did** consider the second one — **and answered
from memory instead of from a test, and was wrong.** Every prior `R219` instance
is a route that went **unasked**. This is the first where a route was **asked
and mis-answered**, which is a *different* failure with a *different* remedy:
enumeration is not enough, **the enumeration's answers have to be measured.**
That clause is added to `R219`.

**★ WHY NO MINT — three reasons, in order of weight.**

1. **The carrier already exists and already fired.** *"Verify each instance, not
   the class"* is in the engineer's own agent memory
   (`.claude/agent-memory/pdfce-engineer/feedback_verify_each_instance_not_the_class.md`),
   with **five instances from 2026-08-18** and **this one already amended into
   it in the same session** — read here to confirm, not assumed. A standing rule
   duplicating a live memory file would be **two descriptions of one rule**,
   which is `R221`'s own subject. **Minting it would violate the rule this Pass
   is an instance of.**
2. **`R219` already owns the project-visible half**, and the gap this instance
   exposes is a *clause* of `R219`, not a separate obligation. Adding a clause to
   a rule with four instances is stronger than starting a fifth rule at n = 1 in
   this file.
3. **The two-occurrence bar is about the PROJECT record, and this is the first
   occurrence in it.** The five earlier instances live in agent memory, not in
   `ROADMAP.md`. Minting on a count carried entirely in another document is the
   borrowed-evidence move hard rule 10's corollary warns about.

**★ THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT, STATED SO IT IS NOT LOST.** The honest case *for*
minting: agent memory is read by **one** agent, `ROADMAP.md` by **every** agent
and by the operator, and this failure has now cost two shipped defects in ten
days. **If it recurs once more in the project record, mint it — and the argument
will be REACH, not count.** Recorded as a live trigger, not a closed question.

⇒ **Ceilings unchanged: standing rules stay at `R223`, next free `R224`.
Decisions stay at `094`, next free `095`.** No decision record: nothing here
redraws a crate boundary, an invariant or a dependency — the shared
`effective_find` is an **application** of `R221`, the same disposition the 297th

#### ★★★★ WHY THEY DID NOT SHIP THE CONTROLS WITH A DEFAULT — THE ARGUMENT THAT SETS THE DESIGN

This is the half a future session will be tempted to "simplify", so it is
recorded as an argument rather than as a preference.

> *"Just default to Solid 1 pt"* would have worked and would have been wrong.

**A properties control has to show the CURRENT value — that is what makes it a
properties control rather than a command.** Seeded from a default it would show
*Solid, 1 pt* over a widget whose file says *Dashed, 3 pt*, or says nothing at
all, and **the operator's first press would write the invention into their
document**, silently replacing a border they never looked at.

**They cited pdfce's own precedent for the refusal, and pdfce had already
endorsed it.** The text-colour swatch shows **a sentence** rather than a
nearest-RGB approximation for a run painted in `DeviceCMYK`, *"because a swatch
showing DeviceCMYK ink as its nearest RGB would write that RGB back on the next
press."* **Same failure, same refusal.** They shipped the pane with the two
controls **ABSENT** (`R9`) and **named the gap** instead of filling it.

**⇒ This is `CLAUDE.md` rule 4 read correctly from outside the project.** A
control seeded from a guess is an **inference presented as document state**, and
rule 4 has never permitted that through either of its two narrowings. Note the
direction of travel: the rule was applied to pdfce's own API by somebody who
does not build pdfce, using pdfce's own published precedent as the warrant.
**That is what a capability boundary looks like when it is working**
(decision 058).

---

#### WHAT SHIPPED — their options (1)+(2), not (3)

```
forms::Widget::border:      Option<BorderSpec>
forms::Widget::visibility:  Option<Visibility>
forms::Widget::annot_flags: AnnotFlags
```

populated by `parse_acroform` — **the parsed model, not a separate
`widget_properties()` query.** The reason is the requester's own and is the
better of the two: **`caption` is already modelled there** because, in pdfce's
own doc's words, *"modelling it is what lets a caption be listed, copied and
compared."* **A border is the same kind of fact**, and a second locator would be
a second way to reach it — `R221`'s subject arriving from the consumer's side of
the boundary.

**★ `border: None` MEANS THE FILE STATES NO BORDER. It is NOT
`BorderSpec::default()`.** That default is solid / 1 pt **because it reproduces
the bytes pdfce has always AUTHORED** — correct for a writer, **a lie from a
reader**. The sentence *"None is a fact to display, not a value to substitute"*
is carried in three places on purpose: the field's own doc comment,
`docs/core-api/03-capabilities.md`, and the test file header. The load-bearing
test is **named for it**
(`a_widget_with_no_border_key_reads_none_not_a_default`).

##### What is READ, and the two places a default IS applied with the distinction stated

Each line below is a test, which is what makes the list a specification rather
than a description.

- **`/BS` (Table 166) wins when present**, per §12.5.4.
- Failing that, **`/Border` (Table 164) `[hRadius vRadius width [dash]]`**
  yields the width, and the style is **Dashed when a NON-EMPTY dash array is
  present** and **Solid otherwise**. The array form **has no style key**, and
  the dash array is the only thing in it that separates the two — so this is a
  **faithful reading, not an inference**. **An empty dash array is not a dash
  pattern.**
- **A `/BS` present but missing `/W` takes Table 166's default of 1 — and this
  is NOT the invention above.** The distinction is the design: **the file has
  COMMITTED to having a border by carrying a `/BS`**, so filling in the width
  the standard specifies is **reading**. **Inventing** is producing a border for
  a widget that carries **neither key**.
- **Width 0 is a VALUE** — Table 166 states *"no border"* explicitly — **never
  an absence.** Collapsing it to `None` would tell a control the file is
  **silent** when it has said something **definite**.
- **A `/S` naming a style pdfce does not model DEGRADES to Solid.** Table 166
  defaults `/S` to solid and names exactly the five, so an unrecognised name is
  a **malformed file**, not a sixth style. Degrading keeps the control usable;
  refusing would blank it.
- **A malformed `/Border`** (too short, not an array) **reads `None`** rather
  than recovering a number out of it.

##### Visibility is EXACT-OR-NONE, and the raw flag word rides beside it

`Visibility` is **deliberately the four combinations pdfce can SET**, out of a
flag word admitting dozens — **a good AUTHORING type and an incomplete READING
one.** A file may legitimately carry `Print | NoZoom`. **Collapsing such a
widget onto the nearest of the four would be the border defect wearing a
different hat**, so the mapping **refuses**, and `annot_flags` lets a control
say *"these flags are not something pdfce can set"* instead of showing nothing
or showing a lie.

**★ `/F` absent is 0 per Table 164, which IS one of the four (`ScreenOnly`)** —
so **`None` always means "present and unmappable" and never "absent"**, a
distinction a control has to be able to make. Pinned by
`an_absent_f_is_zero_which_is_screen_only_not_unknown`.

**The mapping reads `Visibility::flags()` rather than restating the four
integers, so the reader and the writer cannot drift (`R221`).** Adding a
`Visibility` variant fails the round-trip test until it is proved for that one
too — the property, not the string.

---

#### CLI (`CLAUDE.md` rule 11) — `list-fields --widgets`

```
widget 0 obj=4 rect=[20.0 150.0 250.0 172.0] border=D/3.00
         visibility=print-only flags=0x24 state=- merged=1
```

**PER WIDGET, not per field — and that is not a layout choice.** A field may own
several widgets **with different borders**: every radio group does, and so does
any field placed twice. **A field-level `border=` column would be a lie the
moment a field has two.**

**Opt-in**, so existing field rows are **byte-for-byte unchanged**. `border=-`
means **the file states none**; `visibility=other` means the flags are **legal
but not one of the four**; `flags=` carries the **raw word either way**.

reader**, and **the only test that can pin an asymmetry drives both halves**:

visibility is round-tripped.** A hand-authored fixture would test the reader
against bytes **the author chose**; this tests it against bytes **pdfce chose**
— which is the pair that has to agree. ⇢ *Generalisable: when the defect is a
disagreement between two code paths, a fixture pins one path and proves nothing
about the pair.*

not relayed.** `ls -1 fixtures/synthetic/forms/*.pdf | wc -l` → **11**;

#### A LAYERING NOTE — recorded so the next reader knows it was CONSIDERED rather than missed

`forms.rs` now imports `BorderSpec` / `BorderStyle` / `Visibility` from
`edit.rs` — **a READING module referencing types that live in the AUTHORING
one.** Left there rather than moved, on two grounds: moving them **changes a
published path** (`pdfce_core::edit::BorderSpec`) that consumers already build
against, and the alternative — **a duplicate reading enum** — is **the exact
drift `R221` exists to prevent**.

**Decision-record disposition: DECLINED, and the decline is argued rather than
silent.** `ARCHITECTURE.md` §12 is for crate boundaries, library choices and
invariant definitions. This is an **intra-crate module-layering choice made to
preserve a published path**, and its content is **`R221` applied** — the same
ground on which the 297th filing declined `accept_font_target` and the 295th
declined before it. **Filing every correct application of a standing rule as a
decision would make the log a duplicate of *Shipped*.** The engineer
independently reached the same view; the record is here so a later index check
reads the absence as a decision rather than an oversight. **Decision ceiling
does NOT move: `094`, next free `095`.**

and `check-passes-filed`.**

> **The two gates whose entire job is the ordering being violated were the two
> omitted from the sweep that was supposed to catch it.**

**★★ AND THE OMISSION WAS VISIBLE IN THIS PROJECT'S OWN RECORDS ONE FILING
BEFORE IT COST ANYTHING.** The 297th filing's *Gates* block records, verbatim:

> *"`2e6235c`'s own message reports **18** gates green at that commit and
> `cfa2c44`/`0c48bbf` report **13** — the two figures are counts of different
> bare-gate sets at different tips, not a contradiction, and both are quoted
> from the commits rather than reconciled here."*

**Declining to RECONCILE two quoted figures was correct** — hard rule 8 forbids a
confident number inferred from documents. **Declining to MEASURE the population
that reconciles them was not**, because the measurement is **one command in this
repository** (`ls tools/check-*`), and it would have shown both figures to be
**subsets of 19** and the sweep to have **shrunk by five mid-session**. **The
sweep shrank 18 → 13, and the five that dropped out include both filing gates.**
⇢ *A bare count cannot disagree with anything. That is hard rule 10(a)'s
argument — file a total beside its denominator — arriving in a place hard rule
10 was not written to cover: somebody else's gate sweep, quoted in a commit
message.*

##### Disposition — `R209` AMENDED IN PLACE (clause (e)); NO NEW RULE MINTED, and the decline is argued

**`R209` already binds this.** Its clause (a) reads *"never write 'all gates
green' unqualified — name the set."* **The commits did not write "all gates
green"; they wrote a COUNT** — *"13 gates green"* — which **reads as compliance
with (a) while satisfying none of its purpose**, because **a count without its
population is unfalsifiable**. That is a genuine gap in the rule's own text,
found by an instance, which is the standard warrant this project uses for
widening in place.

**Widened rather than minted, on the `R220` precedent argued at length in the
296th filing:** a new number for *"report the denominator of a gate sweep"*
would sit beside `R209` saying a narrower version of the same thing, and **two
rules covering one obligation is the drift this project has been avoiding all
week.** `R209`'s ceiling does **NOT** move. **Standing rules stay at `R223`,
next free `R224`.**

**`R217` also gains a note, not a number** — the sub-shape in occurrence B
(`code → dispatch-librarian → code → file`) is **not** `code → code`, and
`R217`'s working orders do not currently say what B teaches: **the deferral
window closes when the librarian is DISPATCHED, not when its filing is
committed.** A filing takes minutes to write; a commit takes seconds. Recorded
as an amendment note under `R217`; **ceiling unaffected**.

##### ★ THE PART THAT MAKES THIS MORE THAN A PROCESS NOTE

**A sweep that omits a gate is indistinguishable from a green one.** It emits
the same shape of evidence — a list of names, all passing — and **nothing in
that output says how many were not asked.** This is the **same defect as the
under-reporting gate recorded one filing ago** (`check-string-gaps.sh`, third
miss), **pointed at the SWEEP rather than at the GATE**: in both cases a green
signal was produced by an instrument that had not looked at the thing. ⇢ *`R205`
covers a gate that runs and under-reports; `R209`(e) now covers a sweep that
under-runs. Same false confidence, two different layers.*

**A mechanical remedy exists and is RECOMMENDED, not decided here:** a
`tools/run-all-gates.sh` that iterates `tools/check-*` itself, so the sweep's
membership is derived from the **directory** rather than from anybody's memory,
and prints `N of M`. That is engineering work and the engineer's call —
`check-image-colorspace-truth.py` takes a fixture-directory argument and is not a
bare gate, so the script needs a **named exclusion list**, which is exactly the
shape `check-ci-parity.py` already uses for CI. **Filed as a recommendation;
`R209`(e) is the carrier until it exists.**

#### `Pass 142.1` (`2e6235c`) — THE FONT-RESOURCE PRE-FLIGHT

**New public verb.**
`EditSession::preview_font_resources(page_index, find, pinned_span) ->
Result<FontPreflight, FormatError>` — `&self`, side-effect-free, answering
about the **session's staged content**, which is the discipline it shares
with `preview_style_resolution` and which the *Backlog* entry (293rd filing)
specified. New public types in `pdfce-core::text_edit`: `FontPreflight`,
`FontResourceEntry`, `FontAcceptance`, `FontSibling`.

**Both refinements the requester named were delivered, and refinement (2) is
the one they called the valuable half.**

1. **Entries are keyed the way `set_font` matches.** Each carries a
   `selector` **guaranteed to reach that resource**; where a page carries two
   resources with the same `/BaseFont` — the 87 % case their own survey found
   — the selector falls back to the **resource key** and `base_font_ambiguous`
   is set. The collision is **reported**, never silently deduplicated to the
   wrong one (acceptance criterion 1).
2. **Per entry, whether a real Bold and a real Italic of that family WOULD BE
   ACCEPTED** — `FontPreflight::real_bold()` / `real_italic()`. `Some` routes
   the shell's button to `set_font`; `None` routes it to `set_synthetic`.
   **`None` is not a reason to disable the control** — that sentence is in the
   API docs because the whole point of the query is to route a button, not to
   grey one out (and §3.6's *"do not grey out a bold button"* remains true;
   see the correction below for the neighbouring sentence that did not).

**★ An entry that IS the family's real bold reports ITSELF.** Reporting
`None` about itself would tell a shell to synthesize bold **on top of a real
bold face** — a stroke-widened Times-Bold. The self-case is the one a naive
implementation gets wrong, and it is pinned by test.

**★★ `R221` discipline, and this is the structural half of the Pass.** The
acceptance test was **EXTRACTED** out of `plan_font` into a new
`accept_font_target`, which is now **the single implementation** of *"would
`set_font` take this face for this run?"*. `plan_font` calls it; the
pre-flight calls it once per page font resource. **Four conditions**, all of
them `set_font`'s own: the `Pass 14.1` refuse triggers (`classify_font`), an
invertible encoding, encoding coverage of the run's characters, and the
embedded-subset carried-code floor. A pre-flight that **re-derived** the key
instead of asking `set_font`'s own matcher would have reproduced the very
defect it exists to remove — which is what the *Next up* entry warned and what
`Pass 144.0` then proved at the next level down.

`find_styled_face` is the shared *"a real styled face that would be
accepted"* search. **Its `exclude` is an `Option` on purpose**: the synthesis
gate must exclude the run's own resource, the pre-flight must not. `Pass
144.0` is its second caller, one commit later.

**CLI (`CLAUDE.md` rule 11).** New read-only subcommand
`pdfce-cli font-preflight FILE --find TEXT [--page N] [--json]`.
**Exit OK whatever the verdicts were** — a page on which every font refuses is
a successful **answer**, not a failed command; only a run that cannot be
**located** is `EDIT_REFUSED`. That distinction is the difference between a
query and a command, and getting it wrong would make a shell treat "no face
works here" as a tool failure.

**NEW FIXTURE — `fixtures/synthetic/textedit/format_twins.pdf`.** A
Times-Roman run on a page carrying **two resources with the identical
`/BaseFont /Times-Bold`**: `/FB1` remaps `o` and therefore refuses, `/FB2`
covers the run. **Nothing in the corpus had that shape**, which is why the
`base_font_ambiguous` path had no witness before. Generated by
`tools/gen-textedit-fixtures.py` (extended);
`fixtures/synthetic/textedit/PROVENANCE.md` updated — **nine files, not
eight** — and **every existing fixture regenerated BYTE-IDENTICAL**, which is
the check that says the generator change added a file rather than perturbing
the corpus.

**★ The core tests are OUT OF CRATE ON PURPOSE**
(`crates/pdfce-core/tests/font_preflight.rs`, +10):
`#[non_exhaustive]` is **inert inside `pdfce-core`**, so an in-crate test
would write a `match` **no consumer can compile**. Only an out-of-crate test
feels a consumer's constraints. Escalated to `D:/dev/rag/rust/` this filing
(see *Findings escalated*).

**SABOTAGE.** Deleting `&& c.accepted.is_ok()` from `find_styled_face` — **the
exact `Pass 144.0` shape** — turns **3 of the 10** core tests red. The suite is
not vacuous, and the sabotage was chosen to be the defect the next commit
fixes rather than an arbitrary mutation.

**`tools/check-core-api-verbs.py` CAUGHT the missing verb and the stale
count** — the gate built for the `insert_pages` incident firing on the
capability it was built for. `docs/core-api/02-editing-and-saving.md` and

#### `Pass 144.0` (`cfa2c44`) — `gate_synthesis` NAMES A FACE `set_font` ACCEPTS

`gate_synthesis` now treats a real face as *"available"* **only if `set_font`
would actually ACCEPT it for the run's text**. It calls `Pass 142.1`'s
`find_styled_face`, so **the predicate IS the accepting code** rather than a
parallel description of it. **`R221`'s third instance**, and the fix is the
rule's own remedy rather than a bespoke one.

**Three branches, and the family preference is expressed by the ORDER of two
searches rather than by a separate rule** — which is why the preference cannot
drift from the acceptance test:

1. a face of the run's **own family** is ACCEPTED ⇒ refuse synthesis, name it
   *(unchanged behaviour)*;
2. no family match accepted, **another resource is** ⇒ refuse synthesis,
   **NAME THAT ONE**, disclosing that it is a different family;
3. **nothing accepted ⇒ SYNTHESIS PROCEEDS** — pinned by a test **authored to
   fail if a future change turns this into a refusal** (acceptance criterion
   3, met as written).

**★ `R90` IS NOT WEAKENED, and this paragraph is here because the diff reads
as a loosened refusal.** `R90` says synthesis is a fallback for when no real
face **resolves**. What changed is the **predicate for "resolves"** — from
*"exists with a matching family name"* to *"would actually be accepted by
`set_font` for this run"*. That is `R90` applied **more accurately**, not less.
Acceptance criterion 4 (`R90`'s gate unchanged for every input that works
today) is pinned by branch 1's tests.

**Two public error/outcome types gain fields, and the first is the one
`pdfceGUI` needs today.**

- `FormatError::RealFaceAvailable` gains **`selector: String`** — **the string
  to retry with**. It differs from `real_font` **exactly** when a page carries
  two resources sharing one `/BaseFont`, where a name match reaches only one
  twin and possibly the one that refuses. **`pdfceGUI`'s Bold button retries
  with `real_font` today**, so this is a live consumer concern, not a
  hypothetical — and it is the substance of the channel reply.
- The same variant gains **`same_family: bool`** — `false` when branch 2
  fired, and the message says so.
- `StyleOutcome::RealFaceResolves` gains **`selector`** for the same reason.

Both consumers match with `..`, so the change is **additive in practice** even
though the variants are not `#[non_exhaustive]`-shielded from the in-crate
side.

**Measured on the release binary** (engineer's, relayed), against
`fixtures/synthetic/textedit/format_family.pdf` — the same three commands the
296th filing recorded as the reproduction:

| command | before (`703a38e`) | after (`cfa2c44`) |
|---|---|---|
| `--bold-synthetic` | names `/F3 Times-Bold` (which then refuses) | **names `/F2 'Calibri-Bold'`** with the different-family note |
| `--set-font Calibri-Bold` | *(never suggested)* | **`set_font=Times-Roman->Calibri-Bold` SUCCEEDS** |
| `--bold-synthetic` on `format_twins.pdf` | — | **names `/FB2` by resource key**, and that succeeds |
| `--bold-synthetic` on `format_color.pdf` | synthesis proceeds | **synthesis still proceeds** (branch 3 intact) |

⇒ **The remedy the refusal names now works.** That is the whole Pass in one
line, and it is the property the tests now assert rather than the string.

##### ★★★ FOUR DOC CLAIMS FALSIFIED BY THIS CODE, NONE REPORTED BY ANYTHING, ALL CORRECTED IN THE SAME CHANGE — this is the part worth recording at length

**(a) `synth.rs`'s `name_claims_bold` doc.** It said the heuristic is *"used
only in the direction where being wrong is safe … **never to refuse an
edit**"*. **True when written; falsified by a later caller** —
`gate_synthesis` is the second of exactly two call sites and it refuses an
edit. **`cargo doc` cannot check a claim about callers.** The old wording is
kept **STRUCK, not replaced**, so a reader can see what the comment used to
promise. This is `R223`'s first instance (minted below).

**(b) `gate_synthesis`'s own doc.** It said that asking for synthetic bold on
`Times-Bold` *"is refused with that same face named"*. **Read from source:
`!is_self` SKIPS it, so it is never named.** Nobody had reported this either;
it was found by reading the function against its own comment while changing
the predicate. This one is **`R93`'s shape** — a comment that was simply wrong
about the code beside it — not `R223`'s.

**(c) `format.rs`'s `RealFaceAvailable` message named a remedy it had not
checked.** **`R222`** — a message that names a remedy is **making a claim**,
and the format string carried the same unchecked claim the doc comment did.
The rule minted two filings ago fired on its first live change.

**(d) ★★ `docs/core-api/03-capabilities.md` §3.6 carried *"So between the two
verbs, EVERY PAGE IS COVERED"*, WHICH PDFCE SENT TO `pdfceGUI` IN THAT FORM,
AND WHICH WAS FALSE.** Corrected with the old wording **struck** and **the
shape named**: a **universal quantified over all cases and verified on the
cases that came to mind** — `R220` clause (d), wearing the opposite sign to
*"no such verb exists"*. **THE NEIGHBOURING SENTENCE, *"do not grey out a bold
button"*, WAS AND REMAINS TRUE and was deliberately NOT touched** — the 296th
filing's *Next up* entry named correcting the wrong sentence of the two as
*"the available mistake here"*, and it was avoided by name. Acceptance
criterion 6 met.

**★ What (a)–(d) have in common, and it is the transferable half.** Not one of
them was reported by a gate, a test, a compiler or a person. All four were
found by **reading the documentation against the code while changing the
code** — which is the only moment at which the two are both in front of the
same reader. `check-ui-strings.sh` verifies a literal's *location*;
`check-disclosure-channel.sh` verifies a note's *route*;
`check-metrics-line-contract.py` verifies a metrics line's *shape*. **None can
verify that a sentence is true**, which is the standing warrant for declining
a gate here (`R222`, and it is not weakened by four more instances).

##### ★ TWO IN-REPO `pdfce-gui` TESTS CHANGED EXPECTATION ON PURPOSE, AND WHY THAT IS A FINDING RATHER THAN A CHORE

Two tests in `crates/pdfce-gui` asserted `Times-Bold` and now assert
`Calibri-Bold`. **They PASSED THROUGHOUT THE DEFECT**, because they asserted
**the NAME the gate produced** rather than **that the named face worked**. A
test that pins an output string pins the implementation; a test that pins the
property pins the behaviour. **The property — that the named face is one
`set_font` accepts — now lives in
`crates/pdfce-core/tests/synthesis_gate.rs`**, where it can be a property
rather than a string, and where it is out of crate and therefore feels a
consumer's constraints.

**Tests: +8 out-of-crate** (`crates/pdfce-core/tests/synthesis_gate.rs`).
**TWO SABOTAGES, both caught:**

- dropping the acceptance filter (restoring the pre-`144.0` predicate) ⇒ **4
  of 8 red**;
- dropping the branch-2 fallback ⇒ **2 of 8 red**, and **the two that stay
  green are exactly the branch-1 and branch-3 tests** — the right
  discrimination, which is what makes the second sabotage evidence about
  *coverage shape* rather than merely about coverage.

**Also fixed while there, and it is a real hazard rather than tidying.** An
**O(n²) per-entry sibling scan over an attacker-controlled `/Font` dict** in
the pre-flight, replaced by **one pass into a family map**. Fine at the
~20 resources a real page carries; **a hang at the ~50,000 a crafted one
can** — in a query a shell may call **every frame** while a combo box is open,
which is exactly what `pdfceGUI` says it will do (their own note, this
session: *"the face list is drawn per frame while a combo is open"*). A
quadratic in a per-frame query on hostile input is a denial-of-service, not a
performance note.

#### `Pass 145.0` (`0c48bbf`) — THE WHOLE-OPERATOR PIN, AND THE INVARIANT ANSWER

**New:** `FormatRequest::whole_operator(page_index, span)` and a
`FormatRequest::pinned(span)` builder. `whole_operator(page, span)` is
**equivalent to `FormatRequest::new(page, "").pinned(span)`** — both spellings
work and **produce identical bytes, pinned by a test** rather than asserted.
`EditRequest` gets the same affordance (empty `find` + `pinned_span`), because
**the two verbs share one locator** and giving the affordance to only one of
them would have been a new asymmetry.

Implemented as **`effective_find` in `text_edit::edit`, resolved ONCE right
after the anchor is located**, so the code-range match, the font-coverage
gate, the synthesis gate and every disclosure count **read one string**. That
is the structural choice: four consumers of the resolved text, one
resolution.

**AN EMPTY `find` WITH NO PIN IS STILL REFUSED, by the same name it always
was** (acceptance criterion 1, met as written) — a caller that forgot to pin
gets a refusal, not silent whole-operator behaviour. **Both CLI verbs refuse
it with a message naming the FLAG that would fix it**, which core cannot know
about; that split is the reason the refusal exists in two places rather than
one.

**★★ THE SUBTLE HALF, and it is the defect a shallower fix would have
shipped.** `plan_font` used to check encoding coverage against **`req.find`**.
On a whole-operator request that is `""` — and **every face covers the empty
string** — so a family change to a face that **cannot show the run** would have
been **ACCEPTED**. `plan_font` now takes the **resolved** text. Pinned by a
named test. Note the shape: the new affordance did not break coverage
checking, it **hollowed it out silently**, and the only symptom would have
been a run changed to a face that renders nothing.

##### ★★★ THE INVARIANT ANSWER — OWED EITHER WAY, AND NOW MEASURED

`crates/pdfce-core/tests/operator_span_invariant.rs` walks `fixtures/`:

| quantity | value | per-item form (hard rule 10a) |
|---|---:|---|
| files walked | **4,289** | — |
| files with text | **1,623** | 37.8 % of 4,289 |
| runs | **18,559** | 11.4 runs per text-bearing file |
| glyphs | **669,436** | 36.1 glyphs per run |
| `operator_span` groups | **29,246** | **1.58 groups per run**; 22.9 glyphs per group |
| **non-contiguous groups** | **0** | 0 of 29,246 |
| **groups not indexing text cleanly** | **0** | 0 of 29,246 |

⇒ **THE INVARIANT HOLDS.** `pdfceGUI`'s shipped workaround — *"the glyphs
sharing one `operator_span` always slice a contiguous, matchable range out of
the run's text"* — **is sound**, and it is now **a documented guarantee plus a
test that re-runs on every `cargo test`** rather than an undocumented
behaviour they were relying on. **Sabotage-checked**: excluding one glyph per
group from the coverage computation turns the probe **red**, so the zeroes are
zeroes rather than a probe that measures nothing.

**This is the branch the 296th filing said was NOT symmetric**, and the
asymmetry resolved the good way: had it failed, a build their operator is
using would have been resting on luck and they would have needed telling
urgently. It held, so what is owed instead is a **guarantee**, which is
`decision 094` below and the channel reply.

##### ★★ THE MULTI-OPERATOR CLAIM — FILED AS THE REPORTER'S ACCOUNT, EXPLICITLY UNVERIFIED — IS CONFIRMED

**2,420 of 18,559 runs (13.0 %) carry glyphs from more than one show
operator.** **Common, not exotic.** Their third table row was right.

Two consequences, and the second is the rule-4 one:

- **It is what makes the whole-operator affordance load-bearing rather than a
  convenience.** On 13 % of runs, a `find` string rebuilt from `TextRun::text`
  names a range across several operators, which `match_run` cannot express —
  the reporter's third failed attempt, now explained rather than relayed.
- **The report carries a `whole operator:` disclosure naming the case**
  (`CLAUDE.md` rule 4). **The EXTENT was pdfce's choice, not the operator's** —
  the caller said *"this pin"*, pdfce decided how far that reaches — so the
  choice is disclosed off-canvas, and printed by the CLI. Acceptance criterion
  2 met.

**One probe, two answers**, exactly as the 296th filing's method note asked.
Built once.

##### THE DOCS HALF

`docs/core-api/01-reading-and-model.md` gains a new **§8.4.0** stating the two
facts a caller building a locator needs, plus the guarantee:

- **`text.chars().count()` is NOT `glyphs.len()`** — `/ToUnicode` maps a code
  to a **STRING** (ISO 32000-1 §9.10.3), so one glyph can carry several
  characters. **Measured 1 of 191 synthetic runs** — **and THAT RATIO IS THE
  TRAP**: near-zero on synthetic text, **routine on real typeset copy**. A
  `find`-based locator therefore looks correct in every synthetic fixture a
  shell writes for itself. *(The 296th filing recorded the same single
  offender against a different denominator — 1 across 256 fixture PDFs. Same
  fact, two denominators; both are stated here because a bare "1" is not a
  measurement.)*
- **A `TextRun` is not a show operator** — the 13 % table above.
- **The invariant, as a guarantee**, with the 29,246 / 0 numbers beside it, so
  the guarantee carries its own evidence rather than pointing at a filing.

`docs/core-api/02-editing-and-saving.md` gains the `FormatRequest` half.
Acceptance criterion 4 (both doc gaps closed in the same change) met.

##### CLI (rule 11), AND IT CLOSES A LOOP THAT COULD NOT PREVIOUSLY BE CLOSED

- **`extract-text --json --spans`** emits **`op_start` / `op_len` / `stream`**
  per glyph. **Without the flag those fields are ABSENT, not zero** —
  provenance capture is off by default and *"not captured"* must not read as
  *"offset 0"*. `stream` is `"page"` or `"form:N"` and **is not optional to
  read**. This is the field whose absence made the 296th filing unable to
  settle the multi-operator claim from outside; it can now be settled from
  outside by anyone.
- **`format-text --pin-span START:LEN`** and **`edit-text --pin-span
  START:LEN`**. **`START:LEN`, not `START:END`**, because that is the shape the
  value has everywhere else it exists — `ByteSpan` carries start+len, and the
  JSON emits `op_start`/`op_len`. Two spellings of one value is how a caller
  gets it wrong once and never notices.

##### ★★ TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY RUNNING THE BINARY, NOT BY THE TESTS — BOTH IN THIS PASS'S OWN NEW CODE

1. **`cmd_edit_text` PARSED `--pin-span` and never attached it.** The refusal
   read *"empty find text"* — **exactly what the feature was supposed to
   remove** — and **every unit test passed**, because they exercise the core
   API directly. A CLI flag that is parsed and dropped is invisible to any
   test that does not go through `main`.
2. **A shipped `pdfce-cli` refusal carried FOURTEEN baked-in spaces**, and
   **`check-string-gaps.sh` reported PASS on it.**

**The generalisable half:** the suite is 4,463 tests and neither defect was in
its reach, because both live in the **shell layer between the flags and the
core API** — the one layer a core-API test cannot exercise by construction.
Driving the release binary is not belt-and-braces here; it is the only
instrument that covers that layer.

##### ★★★ THE GATE THAT UNDER-REPORTED, FIXED AS A CLASS

**This is the THIRD time `check-string-gaps.sh` has missed by admitting only
the spelling somebody had already seen.** Its own header says the previous
repair *"widens both ends of the class rather than only the end that
failed"* — and it widened both ends to `{`/`}` **and stopped**.

**The next miss was `"…with an empty              --find to mean…"` — TWO
holes at once:**

- the literal **was not recognised as prose** (an `eprintln!`, not an
  `#[error(...)]`), so the prose rules never ran on it;
- and **even in prose mode the trailing class did not admit a HYPHEN** — and
  **the next word after a gap in a CLI diagnostic is, more often than
  anything else, a `--flag`.**

**Fixed by the same structural argument that scoped the `{}` widening:** a
literal opening with **the binary's own diagnostic prefix** (`"pdfce-cli: "` /
`"pdfce-gui: "`) is **a sentence an operator reads**, never an aligned report
column. That is a property of the string's *role*, not of the characters that
have failed so far.

**MEASURED BEFORE WIDENING**, which is what makes the scoping a decision
rather than a guess:

| widening | findings | legitimate (aligned columns, DXF byte streams) | true defects |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| blanket trailing-class widening | **24** | ~18 | 1 |
| **scoped to prose** (diagnostic-prefix rule) | **1** | 0 | **1** |

⇒ **The scoped rule found exactly the defect and nothing else.** A gate that
reports 24 findings of which ~18 are legitimate is a gate that will be
switched off (`D:/dev/rag/rust/ci_gate_red_at_baseline_enforces_nothing.md`).
**A self-test fixture for the shape was added**, so the third miss cannot
become a fourth silently.

**★ THE TRANSFERABLE STATEMENT, NOW THREE FOR THREE:** *in prose mode the
trailing class should be read as **"anything that starts a word"**, not as a
list of the characters that have failed so far.* Three repairs, each one
admitting only the spelling that had just been seen, is the same shape as
`R220`'s three-deep escalation — **a repair that generalises to the instance
rather than to the class is a repair that schedules its own successor.**

#### Decision minted — **094**

**The `operator_span`-slice invariant is a GUARANTEE pdfce publishes to
consumers, not an implementation detail.** `ARCHITECTURE.md` §12, filed this
same edit, with the §5 body section given a pointer. The 296th filing's
`Pass 145.0` entry named this a decision-log candidate **conditional on the
invariant holding**; it held (29,246 groups, 0 exceptions), so the condition
is discharged and the record is owed.

**What the decision costs**, because a guarantee is a constraint on future
work and that is the half worth writing down: `text_extract/layout.rs`'s run
segmentation may no longer be refactored in a way that lets one
`operator_span` group's glyphs become non-contiguous within a run, **even if
no pdfce feature notices**. The test is the enforcement; the decision record
is why the test may not be deleted when it looks redundant.

#### Decision **DECLINED** — `accept_font_target` as the single acceptance predicate

The dispatch offered this as a second decision-log candidate. **Declined, and
the reason is recorded so a future session does not read the absence as an
oversight.** It is an **application of `R221`** — an existing standing rule —
to a new subsystem, not a new architectural boundary, a new crate split, a
library choice or an invariant definition. Filing every correct application of
a standing rule as a decision would make the decision log a duplicate of the
Shipped section and would dilute the records that do constrain future work.
**Precedent:** the 295th filing declined a mint on exactly this ground (*"a
habit … is not an architectural decision this role may take"*). The `R221`
instance itself **is** recorded — in the `Pass 144.0` section above and in
`R221`'s own entry, which already carries this session's inversion of its risk
analysis.

#### Standing rule minted — **`R223`**

**A DOC COMMENT'S CLAIM ABOUT ITS OWN CALLERS IS A MEASUREMENT WITH NO
RECOMPILE BEHIND IT.** Full text in *Standing rules*. Minted at **n = 2 across
two independent subsystems**, which is precisely the condition the **previous
decline stated**: the earlier instance (`ocr/layer.rs`, whose doc comment was
wrong about its own callers **three times in one session**) was declined
promotion on the argued warrant that *"all three wrong readings are of one doc
comment, in one file, inside one session's churn — **not the shape of a defect
recurring across independent subsystems**."* `text_edit/synth.rs` is a second,
independent subsystem, found by a different mechanism, months of Passes later.
**The decline named its own falsifier and the falsifier arrived**, which is a
better warrant for minting than a bare count.

### `Pass 140.2` (`25d73d7`) — ★★★★★ **AN IMAGE'S OWN COLOUR CONVERSIONS REACHED NOTHING AT ALL: `image::decode` CONSTRUCTED TWO `ColorDiagnostics`, WROTE TO BOTH, AND DROPPED BOTH — SO A BROKEN `/tintTransform` PAINTED A NEUTRAL STAND-IN AND PDFCE SAID NOTHING, WHICH IS A RULE 4 *SILENCE* AND NOT A MISSING STATISTIC** — ★★★★ **TWO CORRECTIONS TO `70c5919`'s COMMIT MESSAGE, WHICH THE 294th FILING RELAYED AS ITS OWN:** the *"292 distinct tuples behind 25,870 texels"* cost figure is **WRONG** (that counter had **no image contribution at all**), and **ROUTE 4 ALONE ACCOUNTS FOR THE ENTIRE FIX ON THE REPORTED PATCH** — established by ablation, and **route 4 was not in the bug report** — ★★★ **THE 294th FILING'S HARD-RULE-11 SWEEP REPORTED FOUR SURVIVORS AND THERE WERE FIVE**; the fifth was a **format string**, and three findings come out of it, all new — ★★ standing rule **`R222`** minted: **when a doc-comment claim is corrected, grep the FORMAT STRINGS for the same claim in the same change** — ★ **A SABOTAGE SURVIVED AND IS RECORDED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: it falsified a claim in the CODE COMMENT, not a defect in the code** — 2026-08-27 (295th filing)

**Sourcing.** Shell held and used (hard rule 8). `git show 25d73d7` is the
primary source and every engineering figure below is the **engineer's,
relayed** and labelled as such — this role ran no build, no test and no
render. Every claim about the source tree or the git state was produced
here by `git`/`grep`/`sed` on live files, and the command is named beside
it. `python tools/check-ledger-numbers.py` was run **before** any edit and
**again after**; both runs are quoted in the *Ledger* below.

**`Pass 140.2` was confirmed free before minting.** The pre-edit run
reported *"Pass families with headings : up to 143 (highest ID 143.0)"* and
listed `140` under **CLAIMED BUT NOT YET HEADED** — the 294th filing's own
reservation (*"`Pass 140.2` is claimed in the engineer's uncommitted working
tree — do not reuse it"*). Claimed by this Pass, headed here for the first
time, so hard rule 2 is satisfied: the ID goes to the work it was reserved
for.

#### What was wrong

`crates/pdfce-render/src/image.rs`'s `decode_sampled` converts every texel
through `crate::color`, which counts its own shortfalls — a missing or
malformed `/tintTransform`, a `/Separation /All` approximation, an ICC
alternate taken. Those counts went into **two local `ColorDiagnostics`
values (`scratch_diag`, and the `TintCache`'s own `diag`) that were
constructed, written to, and dropped at the end of the function.**

The visible consequence: an image whose `/Separation` carries a broken
transform renders as `separation_to_rgb`'s **neutral stand-in** — a colour
the document never specified, whose own note says *"lightness preserved,
hue is not the document's"* — and **pdfce reported nothing at all.**

**This is a `CLAUDE.md` rule 4 violation, not a missing statistic**, and the
distinction is the entry. Rule 4 forbids **silence** about an inference, and
its own text says the obligation *"bites hardest on inferences the operator
**cannot see by definition**"* — naming a font substitution that renders
plausibly. **A substituted image colour is the same case**: a plausible grey
looks exactly like a grey the file might have asked for. The fix routes the
account off-canvas to the CLI's printed note, which is where rule 4 says it
belongs; nothing about the **rendering** changes.

#### Measured, before → after (engineer's figures, relayed)

On a purpose-built **image-only** page whose `/Separation` carries a
deliberately malformed transform (wrong arity, wrong output count):

| fixture | `tint_applied` before | after | `tint_not_applied` before | after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `image-only-good-tint.pdf` | 0 | **1** | 0 | 0 |
| `image-only-broken-tint.pdf` | 0 | 0 | 0 | **1** |

**Both counters read zero on both fixtures before the fix** — the good page
and the broken page were indistinguishable from a page with no spot content
at all. Per hard rule 10a the denominator is stated: these are **counts per
distinct sample tuple, not per texel**, because `TintCache` exists precisely
so that one broken transform reports **once per distinct colour** rather
than once per texel; on these two fixtures the palette is one entry, so 1
tuple = 1 image. The shortfall half also produces prose on the CLI's note:
*"1 spot-colour conversion(s) had no usable `/tintTransform` … the lightness
is right and the HUE IS NOT the document's"*.

**Why the GOOD fixture is asserted as well as the broken one, and is not
padding.** A fix that routed only **failures** to the caller would satisfy
the shortfall half and leave the **census** half still lying by omission.
Only the good page tells those two apart.

#### ★★★★ TWO CORRECTIONS TO `70c5919`'s COMMIT MESSAGE — AND THEREFORE TO THE 294th FILING, WHICH RELAYED BOTH

`70c5919` is **not amended**; its hash is cited by the 294th filing's
*Shipped* entry, by `SESSION_LOG.md` and by `ARCHITECTURE.md`, and this
project has direct evidence of what rewriting a cited commit costs
(`tools/check-cited-commits-exist.py`, `0d9f4df`, fourteen pre-existing
casualties). The corrections are recorded **here**, and a dated correction
note has been placed in-line at each site in `docs/` that repeated either
claim — **corrected in place with a visible note, never silently
rewritten** (append-only discipline, hard rule 1).

**(a) The cost figure was wrong, and the true statement is STRONGER.**
`70c5919`'s message said *"292 distinct tuples behind 25,870 texels"* on the
patch that opened `Pass 140.0`, attributing `tint_applied = 292` to that
image's `TintCache`. **That counter had no image contribution whatsoever**
— it was the page's **path fills** — because the decode's diagnostics
reached nothing, which is the very defect this Pass fixes. The engineer
wrote a number into a commit message by attributing a counter to a producer
**that could not have reached it.**

Corrected, and better than the figure it replaces: **both images on that
patch are `/Indexed` with 256-entry palettes**, so their tint work is
bounded by the **palette** — **≤ 256 conversions per image, at decode time,
independent of the image's pixel count** — and `TintCache` is not involved
at all. That is a *stronger* cost claim than "one evaluation per 88.6
texels", because it is bounded by a structural constant rather than by a
measured ratio on one page.

**The synthetic worst case stands unchanged**: 16 bpc × 5 colorants (an
**80-bit key** the cache cannot pack), **490,000 texels**, a type 4
PostScript transform, **~670 ms → ~925 ms median = 1.37 µs → 1.89 µs per
texel, about +38 %**, filed as a **range not a point** because run-to-run
spread on this machine is ~15 %. It was measured on a **direct `DeviceN`
image**, which is the genuinely unbounded shape — so the worst case was
never resting on the wrong figure.

**(b) ★★ ROUTE 4 ALONE ACCOUNTS FOR THE ENTIRE FIX ON THE REPORTED PATCH,
AND ROUTE 4 WAS NOT IN THE REPORT.** Ablated on a debug build:

| configuration | `cmyk_bridged_pixels` | `cmyk_native_image_pixels` |
|---|---:|---:|
| `/Indexed`-over-`DeviceN` ink table **reverted**, direct `Separation`/`DeviceN` route left in place | **25,870** | **0** |
| both restored (shipped state) | **0** | **25,870** |

Reading the table: with **only the route the bug report named** in place, the
patch is **fully bridged** — that is, **completely unfixed**. The two
counters are complements, so the same 25,870 pixels are the whole patch in
both rows; there is no partial credit anywhere in it.

⇒ **Had the engineer implemented only the route the bug report named, the
reported defect would not have been fixed at all.** The route that actually
carried the fix — `/Indexed` over a `Separation`/`DeviceN` base, a duotone —
was found **by walking `R219`'s own checklist**, not by the report, not by a
test, and not by the operator.

**This is the strongest datum this project has for `R219`**, and it has been
folded into `R219`'s own entry under *Standing rules* as well as recorded
here. It converts the rule from *"enumerating the siblings is cheap and
saves the next session a bug report"* into *"on this instance, enumerating
the siblings is the only reason the fix worked."* A standing rule whose
value has been demonstrated this concretely should say so **where the rule
is read**, not only where the Pass is filed.

#### ★★★ THE STALE-CLAIM SWEEP — FIVE SITES, AND THE 294th FILING'S SWEEP FOUND FOUR

The 294th filing's hard-rule-11 sweep reported **four survivors** at
`70c5919` and recorded them as owed work. **All four were real and all four
are corrected in `25d73d7`.** There was a **fifth**, found only by grepping
**format strings**: `crates/pdfce-cli/src/main.rs`'s runtime note — the class
the **288th** filing recorded as invisible to every gate and left unresolved.

**Three findings, all new, and none of them is "the sweep should have been
more thorough":**

**(i) A stale claim can be repaired by a CODE CHANGE rather than by an edit,
leaving no trace of ever having been wrong.** From `Pass 130.1` until `Pass
140.0`, a `Separation`/`DeviceN` image outside overprint **did** bridge, and
`interpret.rs`'s *"what is left"* enumeration did not mention it — **false
for ten Passes**. `Pass 140.0` removed that population, which made the
**unchanged** sentence true again. Nobody edited it, nobody noticed it, and
the repaired text carries no marker that it was ever wrong. **A `git blame`
on a true sentence is not evidence the sentence was always true.**

**(ii) Two copies of one population claim disagreed for ten Passes, and the
MORE VISIBLE copy was the accurate one — so recency and location are both
worthless as evidence.** The CLI's runtime note (operator-facing, printed on
every subtractive page) listed that population **correctly** over exactly the
period the rustdoc comment (internal, read by maintainers) had it wrong. Then
`Pass 140.0` made **the accurate one** false. The natural heuristics both
fail here: *"the internal comment is closer to the code, trust it"* is wrong,
and *"the operator-facing string is more exposed, so it gets corrected more
often"* is wrong in the other direction. **When two copies of a population
claim disagree, neither's recency nor its audience is evidence of which is
right — only the code is.**

**(iii) The format-string gap has now cost a SECOND occurrence.** The 288th
filing recorded this class — a claim living in a `println!`/`eprintln!`
template, invisible to every gate this project owns — and said *"a fourth
occurrence would argue harder for promotion"*. **This is the second for the
format-string half specifically**, counted separately and deliberately: the
288th filing's tally was for the broader stale-disclosure class, and
conflating the two would inflate the count.

**★ THE PROMOTION QUESTION, DECIDED: MINTED AS `R222`, AND THE ENGINEER'S
REASONING FOR *NOT* GATING IT IS ACCEPTED IN FULL.** The engineer's view,
relayed verbatim in the dispatch, was that this *"still cannot be gated
mechanically (no script can content-check a claim's truth)"* but that the
**habit** is now clearly worth a standing rule. Both halves are accepted:

- **The gate half is DECLINED, permanently, and should not be re-proposed.**
  A gate would have to know what the current behaviour *is* — which is the
  very fact the disclosure exists to report. This is the identical warrant
  on which three prior requests to gate the disclosure-staleness class were
  declined (librarian hard rule 11's own text), and it is not weakened by a
  second occurrence.
- **The habit half is MINTED as `R222`** — see *Standing rules*. It is a
  **procedural commitment on the engineer's side**, the mirror of librarian
  hard rule 11's commitment on the filing side, and like both of its
  siblings (`R219`, `R220`) it is **checkable after the fact**: a reader asks
  whether the change that corrected a doc comment also grepped the format
  strings. Minted at **n = 2**, the project's standing bar, with the second
  instance found by a sweep that had already run once and reported clean.

**Why a librarian hard rule was not sufficient on its own.** Hard rule 11
already names `eprintln!`/`println!` strings in its scope, and it is what
found survivors 1–4. But hard rule 11 runs **at filing time — one commit
later at best**, and it binds the librarian, not the engineer making the
edit. The gap `R222` closes is the window between *"the engineer corrects a
doc comment"* and *"the librarian sweeps"*, which is exactly where this
survivor lived.

#### ★ A SABOTAGE THAT SURVIVED, RECORDED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER

Three sabotages of `Pass 140.2`'s two new tests (engineer's, relayed):

| sabotage | result |
|---|---|
| `decode` never merges its diagnostics into `notes` | **2 of 7 fail** |
| the interpreter drops what `decode` handed it | **2 of 7 fail** |
| only the **cache** is merged, not `scratch_diag` | **0 of 7 fail — SURVIVES** |

**The survivor is the entry, and it is a POSITIVE instance: the sabotage
caught a false claim in a CODE COMMENT, not a defect in the code.** The
engineer's first draft of that comment claimed the `scratch_diag` merge kept
*"every non-`Special` image"* from being silent. **That was false, and the
sabotage is what proved it** — deleting the merge changes no test because:

- `tint_cache` is `Some` **exactly when** the space is `Space::Special`, so
  the non-cache arm of the texel loop is reached only by `Gray`, `Rgb`,
  `Cmyk` and `Indexed` — whose conversions are **closed-form arithmetic that
  records nothing at all**. There is no shortfall for a non-`Special` image
  to report.
- `scratch_diag`'s **only** possible contribution is the `yields_cmyk` probe,
  and only for a transform that **LOADS** successfully and then **fails to
  EVALUATE** at an all-zero operand. A transform that fails to load leaves
  `tint: None` and `tint_to_cmyk` returns early without counting.
- **The fixtures' transform fails at LOAD**, which is the commoner
  malformation and the one worth pinning.

The comment now records the merge as **deliberately uncovered** and says
exactly why, rather than leaving it to read as tested. **A green sabotage
that is explained is a different artifact from a green sabotage that is
ignored**, and this project has a lesson on the distinction already
(`C:/personal_rag/pdf/lesson_20260819_green_sabotage_can_signal_fixture_insufficiency_not_just_untested_or_equivalent_code.md`).

#### ★ ONE OF THIS PROJECT'S OWN GATES BROKE ONE OF ITS OWN TESTS — filed as an OBSERVATION, not decided

`tools/check-image-colorspace-truth.py` writes a `_truth/` **subdirectory
beside the images it scores**. Pointing it at `fixtures/synthetic/images` —
the obvious thing to do, and what the engineer did while running the gate
sweep — made `every_fixture_either_imports_or_refuses_by_name` die on
`std::fs::read` of a **directory**, which on Windows is `PermissionDenied` /
*"Access is denied."*

**So the panic reads as a filesystem-rights problem and sends the reader
after their antivirus.** Fixed in `25d73d7`: the test now **skips
directories** and **names the failing path**.

**★ `.gitignore` would not have helped.** The failure is on **disk** and has
nothing to do with what is **tracked** — a distinction worth stating,
because `.gitignore` is the reflex answer to "a tool wrote a directory into
my tree" and it addresses a different problem entirely.

**⇒ OPEN OBSERVATION FOR THE ENGINEER, deliberately NOT decided by this
role:** *should the gate be writing into a fixture directory at all?* An
output directory beside the input is convenient and is why nobody noticed;
an output directory **outside** the fixture tree would make this class
structurally impossible rather than defended against per-test. That is an
engineering call about a tool this role does not own, and it is recorded
here so it does not evaporate — **not** promoted to a Pass, and **not**
answered.

#### ★ `ImageNotes` LOSES `Copy` AND `Eq` — a public type change, recorded, and a rule candidate at n = 1

`ImageNotes` is `pub` in `pdfce-render`; `Pass 140.2` drops `Copy` and `Eq`
from its derives, because `ColorDiagnostics` owns a deduped-and-capped
`Vec<String>` of notes and is neither. **This is a breaking change to a
public type's trait surface** and is filed as such rather than left to be
discovered.

The engineer's reasoning, relayed: keeping the derives would have meant
**leaving the field off the struct** — *which is the arrangement that made
this silent in the first place*. *"A diagnostics bag that grows is the
normal case; a `Copy` bound that decides what may be diagnosed is the tail
wagging the dog."*

**Recorded as a NAMED CANDIDATE at n = 1, not minted:** *a trait bound must
not decide what a type is allowed to record.* It is a real principle and it
is a sibling of `R221` (a parallel description of a capability drifts from
the capability); it is **one instance**, and this project's bar is two. If a
second derive-driven omission turns up, this is the entry to cite.

before. Every description of them is a claim about **which producers are
counted**, and all of them were written when the answer was "paths and
shadings only".

Now states that an image's own conversions arrived in `Pass 140.2` and that a palette's do not. |

the rustdoc for `ImageNotes::color`** — *"NOT included, and deliberately"* —

#### `Pass 140.0` — the image routes, and there are TWO of them

**Symptom, as reported.** A five-colorant `DeviceN` photograph rendered
visibly desaturated against the Acrobat reference — washed toward grey where
the reference is saturated green.

**Cause.** On a page compositing in a four-colorant buffer, a
`Separation`/`DeviceN` image resolved through its tint transform **to sRGB**
and never to its `DeviceCMYK` alternate, so it entered the buffer through a
`CMYK → sRGB → CMYK` round trip. **The two legs are different functions.**
The outbound leg is `Rgb::from_cmyk`, the calibrated conversion carrying a
rendering intent; the return leg is `overprint::rgb_to_cmyk`, naive
maximum-GCR — which is an exact inverse of `cmyk_to_rgb`, a *third* function
the paint colour never went through. **They are not an inverse pair, and code
that pairs them reads as an exact recovery.**

**Two routes were fixed, and only one was reported:**

3. a **direct** `Separation`/`DeviceN` image over a `DeviceCMYK` alternate — the reported one;
4. an **`/Indexed` image over such a base — a duotone** — **not in the report**, found by walking `R219`'s checklist.

Both now route through one new answer, `Space::to_cmyk`, so the per-texel path
and the palette-build path **cannot come to disagree**. (The numbering 3/4
continues the `R219` route enumeration below.)

**The trap the Backlog entry named is avoided.** The overprint colorant planes
are **not** reused. They hold `authored_tints`, which answers Table 149's
*"which components did the source SPECIFY"* — a different question — and they
return `None` for a spot-only `DeviceN`, where a plain render needs the
flattened tint and would otherwise paint **bare white paper**.

**Measured against the Acrobat reference on the patch that opened the Pass, at
scale 2** (engineer's figures, relayed):

| what | before | after | Acrobat |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| photograph region, dE | 33.06 | **16.85** | — |
| an inset patch of it, dE | 29.57 | **7.13** | — |
| saturation spread | 51.8 | **90.2** | 87.3 |
| `cmyk_bridged_pixels` | 25,870 | **0** | — |
| `cmyk_native_image_pixels` | 0 | **25,870** | — |

**The two counters are complements and moved as complements** — the same
25,870 pixels, relabelled from *"lost its ink on the way in"* to *"kept it"*.

#### ★ `Space::yields_cmyk` is a PROBE, not a structural predicate — and that was deliberate

The gate could have pattern-matched the colour space's **shape** (*is this a
`Separation`/`DeviceN` whose alternate is `DeviceCMYK`?*). It instead **asks
the real conversion function** with an all-zero operand, so there is **one**
answer to *"does this space have colorants"* rather than two descriptions that
can drift apart.

**A wrong probe cannot paint a wrong colour in either direction**, which is
what makes the choice cheap: a **false negative** bridges exactly as before
(the status quo, disclosed), and a **false positive** is caught by an
**all-or-nothing discard** that drops the planes for the whole image rather
than leaving a seam mid-photograph.

Standing rule **`R221`** is minted from this, at n = 2 — see *Standing rules*.

#### `Pass 140.1` — the path fill, and `Pass 140.0` is what exposed it

**It did not exist as a filed Pass before this session.** With only the image
half fixed, the new fixtures reported the **fill** and the **image** 8.3 to
9.0 mean levels apart on the same authored colour, and the **additive control
page** — which allocates no colorant buffer and therefore never took the round
trip — identified which half was wrong (engineer's figures, relayed; mean over
a 40×100 pt patch of each half, scale 2):

| page | fill | image | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Separation`, **additive** | 157,207,185 | 158,208,186 | agree — no round trip on this page |
| `Separation`, subtractive | 159,192,194 | 158,208,186 | ← the **FILL** is the outlier |
| `DeviceN`, subtractive | 160, 86,161 | 160,108,156 | ← likewise |

**The image agrees with its own additive rendering; the subtractive fill does
not.** So the fill was reconstructing its colorants from the already-resolved
sRGB by the same round trip. `Interpreter::authored_cmyk` now asks
`ColorSpace::to_cmyk` **first** and **falls through unchanged** for every
space that has no `DeviceCMYK` answer — a `Separation` over a `DeviceRGB`
alternate, a `DeviceGray` fill, a `Lab` fill: none of them reaches the early
return and none of their behaviour moves.

**★ Why nothing had ever reported this.** Before `Pass 140.0`, *both* halves
took the round trip and were wrong **together**. Fixing one half converts a
silent shared error into a visible disagreement, **and the disagreement is the
information** — the exact history `tests/shading_ink.rs` already records for
the shading half, one object type over.

#### Tests, and the sabotage that proves route 5 is genuinely covered

`tools/gen-devicen-image-fixtures.py` builds **four pages**; each draws the
same authored colour **twice**, once as a fill and once as an image, **so the
oracle is `fill == image` and needs no reference render at all.** The
`/DeviceN` page's tint transform is **deliberately not a pass-through**, so
*"what did the source specify"* and *"what does the transform produce"* have
different answers and a renderer cannot pass by confusing them.

Five integration tests plus two unit tests, **each sabotaged**:

| sabotage | tests failed, of 5 |
|---|---:|
| `carries_ink` loses the probe | 3 |
| indexed ink table only for `DeviceCMYK` | **1** (the duotone alone) |
| `Space::to_cmyk`'s `Special` arm → `None` | 4 |
| `Pass 140.1`'s early return removed | 4 |
| the `tinting` discriminator dropped | 3 |

**No two sabotages fail the same set**, and **the duotone route is caught by
exactly one test** — which is the evidence that route 5 is genuinely covered
rather than incidentally passing. A route covered by *zero* distinguishing
tests and a route covered by *one* look identical on a green run.

#### ★ A generator bug worth a line, because the error message names the symptom and not the cause

**A classic cross-reference table is written as ONE CONTIGUOUS SUBSECTION**, so
a gap in the object numbering **silently shifts every entry after it** and the
file dies with a message that names the symptom (a bad object at some offset)
and not the cause (a missing number, hundreds of bytes earlier). The fixture
generator now **asserts contiguity** rather than trusting it. This is the
write-side twin of §7.5.4's completeness requirement already recorded in
`C:/personal_rag/pdf/` — see *RAG escalation* in the session log.
