#### What shipped, in one paragraph

`docs/suite-operator-review-2026-08-21.md` found two instrument faults in
`tools/suite-check.py`: a contrast floor calibrated against the wrong
population, and a harness that only hunts a mark that should be ABSENT,
blind to the suite's other criterion — a mark that should be PRESENT. This
Pass repairs the first and replaces the second's false `clean` with an
honest, distinct `MARK?` verdict rather than a detector — a working-looking
colour-keyed detector was built, caught producing a false positive, and
thrown away. **Both repairs also correct the founding review itself**: its
diagnosis of fault 1 (needs an area term) does not survive re-measurement,
and its patch list for fault 2 (seven patches) over-counted by three from a
phrase-grep that found a mention, not a criterion.

---

#### ★★★ Fault 1 — the contrast floor: FIXED, but not for the diagnosed reason

`CONTRAST_MIN` 12.0 → 6.0, calibrated against the operator's own cell-by-cell
reading of `PCS 1.0` (the review's calibration set) — his four "clear fails"
(cells i/d/j/e) measure **10.7, 10.2, 7.8, 7.4** at the harness's own scale;
his two "faint outline only" (b/g) measure **4.1, 4.1**. An **empty interval**
from 4.1 to 7.4 — 6.0 sits in the middle with ~1.4 levels of margin either
side. Cross-checked before shipping: the pre-existing sub-perceptual
population stays ≤1.1 across every Acrobat render; `PCS 16.2`'s genuinely
invisible cells (1.3–3.3) stay rejected; across all 51 patches the change
flips **exactly one** verdict, `PCS 1.0` pass → FAIL.

**★★ The review's own diagnosis of this fault does not hold, and this is
worth recording as its own finding, not folded into "fixed."** §3 of the
review says the floor "has no area term" and that box 3's crosses are
"roughly three times the linear size" of the calibration patch's, so the
prescribed remedy was to make the threshold a function of mark size.
**Measured, before implementing it: every trap on `PCS 1.0` and the
`PCS 16.0` calibration patch is the SAME pixel size at this harness's render
scale — 36–38 px square, both.** An area term would have changed nothing on
this population; the fault was never geometry, it was one population's
threshold (calibrated on ten sub-perceptual swatches) applied to a different
population (moderate-contrast traps) with no second calibration point.
⇒ **A fix aimed at a misdiagnosed cause is more dangerous than no fix,
because it consumes the suspicion** — an area term would have shipped with a
plausible-sounding justification and no measurable effect on the false
`clean` it was meant to close, and the patch would have gone on reporting
clean with a fix already in place and a reason to stop looking.

---

#### ★★★ Fault 2 — the positive criterion: NOT a detector; a false `clean` removed and replaced by an honest `MARK?`

**★ CORRECTS THE FOUNDING REVIEW'S OWN LIST: FOUR PATCHES, NOT SEVEN.** The
review's list (`PCS 050/080/081/082/150/151/152`) came from a `grep` of the
suite's ReadMes for the phrase "check mark". `PCS 150`/`151`/`152` do NOT
belong — their own ReadMe text states the suite's **negative** criterion
(*"If a X can be seen, Optional Content is not handled right"*) and mentions
"check mark" only while describing what the FAILURE CROSS is drawn out of
("a cross consisting of 2 check marks"). **A grep for a phrase finds a
mention, not a criterion.** Re-verified 2026-08-24 against Acrobat renders of
all three: one check mark, "Default View", no cross, in both engines —
**`PCS 15.0`/`15.1`/`15.2` genuinely PASS**, discharging the review's owed
item 4 (three patches "no one has looked at"). The harness now reads each
patch's own extracted ReadMe text at runtime (the pattern `ref_style`
already used), so this list can no longer drift from the corpus by a stale
grep.

The four real check-mark patches score `MARK?` — a distinct verdict, counted
UNRESOLVED, never folded into `pass` or `FAIL`. Ground truth recorded BY
HAND in `tools/suite-check.py`'s own docstring, against Acrobat-Pro renders,
because no automated detector ships this Pass:

| PCS | Acrobat shows | pdfce shows | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `8.2` DeviceN (4 col.) | two olive marks ~46×56 px, upper-right of each image, plus a smaller inline one | inline mark only | **FAIL** |
| `8.01` DeviceN (6 col.) | two dark-green marks on the images plus ~15 more along the spot-colour gradient bar | none | **FAIL** |
| `8.1` DeviceN (5 col.) | same family | same absence | **FAIL** |
| `5.0` Font Substitution | a black glyph, embedded modified Symbol font | rendered correctly | **PASS** |

**★★ THE TRAP THIS RAISED, CAUGHT MID-SESSION, AND WHY NO DETECTOR SHIPS.** A
first detector keyed on the mark's OWN COLOUR (olive, measured from
`PCS 8.2`'s genuine mark). Run against `PCS 8.01` it reported the mark
PRESENT — matching the green stop of that patch's own spot-colour gradient
bar — while BOTH real marks were absent: a false green produced BY the fix
for a false green, on the very patch the operator had already flagged.
**The mark's colour is not a constant of the criterion.** Whatever
eventually adjudicates these four must key on presence relative to a
reference render, not on a hue. The working-looking detector was thrown
away rather than shipped; see the RAG finding below.

#### What shipped, in one paragraph

A non-isolated ordinary transparency group on a `DeviceCMYK` page was
composited as if isolated — its interior blended against a transparent
buffer instead of the page beneath it, and ISO 32000-1 §11.4.4's backdrop
removal never ran. **The second content walk now exists**, a line-for-line
port of the additive `Paint` arm. New in `CmykBuffer`: `child_from_backdrop`
(run 2's buffer, seeded from the parent's dirty region), `composite_non_isolated` (§11.4.4 removal then the element formula, soft mask applied
**after** the removal because the removal divides by the **unmasked**
`α_gn`), and `backdrop_present` (§11.4.5's "is the initial backdrop
transparent?" — deliberately **not** `dirty_region().is_some()`, because a
buffer written with transparent paint has a dirty rectangle and no
backdrop). `Canvas::group`'s `Cmyk` arm now runs the same three-way test the
`Paint` arm already used: `isolated || !backdrop_dependent || !backdrop_present` takes one walk, otherwise two. Allocation failure for the second
buffer falls back to the old approximation and still counts it, so the
disclosure stays honest under memory pressure.

#### End-to-end evidence — four purpose-built fixtures, because no corpus supplies any

`fixtures/synthetic/transparency/{nonisolated,isolated}_{multiply,normal}_cmyk.pdf`, generated by `tools/gen-nonisolated-group-fixtures.py` (hand-
written PDF bytes, no third-party file consulted — `LEGAL.md` §5). Results
at scale 4:

| comparison | pixels differing | notes |
|---|---:|---|
| non-isolated Multiply, old vs new | **40,000** | max delta 137 |
| isolated Multiply, old vs new | **0** | control — isolated path untouched |
| non-isolated Normal, old vs new | **0** | control — §11.4.4 NOTE 2 exactness |
| non-isolated vs isolated Multiply, **BEFORE** | **0** | the defect stated as a measurement |
| non-isolated vs isolated Multiply, **AFTER** | **40,000** | centre pixel `137,129,189` → `0,114,188` |

Red falls to zero on the last row: Multiply of magenta over cyan subtracts
red, so the fix is verified in **direction**, not only magnitude.

---

#### Two lessons from the fixture generator itself, both worth carrying

1. **A vacuous assertion beside a wrong literal is worse than no assertion.**
   The generator asserted `(catalog, pages, …) == (1,2,3,4,5,6,7)` — exactly
   what its own `add()` helper returns, so it could never fail — while the
   dictionaries beside it spelled `/GSO 7 0 R` and `/GSI 8 0 R`, both off by
   one: the outer graphics state picked up the interior's `Multiply` and the
   interior's own reference dangled. It rendered a plausible picture and
   tested the opposite of its claim. **Same family as `R162`** (an assertion
   proves nothing until the container is shown capable of holding the
   thing), instanced here in a fixture generator rather than a test. Fixed:
   the assert now checks the emitted reference **text**.

2. **★ The one that matters most — the feature's own precondition was
   invisible.** `interpret.rs` computes `needs_buffer = is_transparency_group && (!outer_is_neutral || isolated || knockout)`. A non-isolated
   group under a **neutral** outer state (`/BM /Normal`, `ca = CA = 1`, no
   soft mask) is painted **inline** — and painting it inline is not an
   *approximation* of non-isolated semantics, it **is** non-isolated
   semantics, because the interior blends against the real page. So the gap
   this Pass closes exists **only where a buffer is forced.** Buffering a
   non-isolated group is what turns it into an isolated one; the second walk
   is what turns it back. The second fixture attempt used `/ca 1`, rendered
   identically before and after, and looked like the Pass had done nothing.
   Every fixture now carries `/ca 0.5`, with the reason commented at the
   point where the `0.5` is written. **Generalised: a feature can have a
   precondition no test states, and a fixture that misses it is
   indistinguishable from a fix that does not work.** Written up at
   `D:\dev\rag\rust\a_fixture_that_avoids_a_feature_precondition_cannot_tell_a_fix_from_a_no_op.md`.

---

#### A third finding, about the code rather than the tests — `R143`'s pattern, NOT a new rule

The `Cmyk` arm justified its approximation with *"there is no way to hand
one to the other without the very round trip the colorant buffer exists to
delete."* True of the sRGB-interior era. **`Pass 97.1f` gave the child a
native colorant buffer**, and from that commit onward parent and child hold
the same four planes in the same space — the backdrop can simply be copied,
and the obstacle the comment described had already stopped existing. The
comment went on being quoted for three Passes. **Shape: a comment justifying
an approximation is not re-read when the thing it blames is removed,
because nothing links them — the approximation outlived its own reason.**

★ **Correcting my own first draft of this entry.** The draft proposed
minting this as a new standing rule (candidate `R218`), citing `CLAUDE.md`
hard rule 8's amendment as a second occurrence. **Checked against the
existing record before committing, and both halves of that draft were
wrong.** First: this exact shape is already `R143` — *"A refusal's stated
reason is re-verified before it is used to scope work"* (2026-08-05,
continuation 83), whose own worked instance (`R-INV-4`, composite text
editability) is the identical mechanism — a stated reason expires, the
approximation/refusal it justified survives unread, and downstream code
narrowed around it becomes false corroboration. Second: the cross-project
RAG file this pattern lives in,
`D:\dev\rag\rust\trust_but_verify_doc_comments_are_not_evidence.md`, records
an **explicit 2026-08-05 ruling that this pattern stays a RAG finding and
is deliberately NOT elevated into further pdfce standing rules per
occurrence** — a project rule governs how pdfce is scoped (that is what
`R143` already does); the general epistemic failure belongs in the

#### What shipped, in one paragraph

Both `tools/check-commits-filed.py` and `tools/check-passes-filed.py` join
on **"this commit's hash appears in `ROADMAP.md`/`SESSION_LOG.md`"**. That
join cannot be satisfied by the tip commit of any push, for any commit,
code or docs — the filing that would satisfy it is necessarily a *later*
commit. The existing docs-only exemption (`D:/dev/rag/rust/a_gate_joining_
on_a_hash_the_commit_itself_writes_is_unsatisfiable.md`, 2026-08-07) only
ever covered the ledger-writing commit itself; it did nothing for an
ordinary *code* commit whose filing is merely scheduled, not impossible —
which is every code commit, on its own CI run. **Both gates now defer the
join for `HEAD` alone**, on every run, printed on both the passing and
failing path, and the deferral evaporates the instant a following commit
exists. Real debt behind the tip — a genuinely older, unfiled commit —
still hard-fails, unchanged. A `--strict-tip` flag reproduces the old,
undeferred behaviour for the one caller that can actually satisfy it: a
librarian filing checking itself immediately before committing.

#### What is NOT weakened (carried forward because a future session will be tempted to misread the fix as a loosening)

  and never followed by a filing, which no later commit could have

- The deferral is **printed on both the clean and the failing path** — a

  `83409b3` above.
- `verify-release.py`'s comment and failure-hint text were corrected in

  longer has.

#### ★★★★★ THE CI FINDING — 14 red runs, one step, and a gate nobody was reading

**Measured** (`gh run list --limit 25 --json databaseId,conclusion,headSha`,
then `gh run view <id> --json jobs` on each):

| what | measured |
|---|---|
| consecutive failed runs, newest at `08a88bd` | **14** |
| last **green** run | **`32493456093`**, head `06aaad3` |
| of those 14, how many fail on the step `check that every code commit is filed` | **13 opened individually, all 13; the 14th is the same job in the same workflow** |
| the failing **job**'s name | `verify pdfce-gui strings live in ui_text.rs` — **the job name describes its first step, not the gate that failed**, a fresh instance of `D:/dev/rag/rust/a_ci_job_name_describes_its_first_step_not_the_gate_that_failed.md` |

**The dispatch reported two** (`c24ad7a`, `83409b3`). **It is fourteen.**
The dispatch's *reading* — *a gate that is already red teaches people to
ignore it, and the second failure hid behind the first* — is **correct,
and understated by a factor of seven.**

★★★★★ **THE MECHANISM, AND IT IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN CARELESS.**
`check-commits-filed.py` exempts docs-only commits, correctly (that
exemption is itself a recorded finding —
`D:/dev/rag/rust/a_gate_joining_on_a_hash_the_commit_itself_writes_is_unsatisfiable.md`).
So the gate is **red by construction on every CODE commit's own CI run**,
because that commit's filing is necessarily a *later* commit; it goes
green on the filing commit that follows. **A run of interleaved code
commits therefore produces a run of red CI**, and the signal degenerates
into a constant. ⇒ **What the gate actually reports is not "is the repo
filed?" but "was the last pushed head a filing commit?"** — and nobody
had asked it that question, so nobody noticed it had stopped answering
the first one.

★★★★★ **THE CONSEQUENCE FOR RELEASES, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A RELEASE
RECORD AND NOT A HOUSEKEEPING NOTE.** **`v0.7.0`'s tag was placed on
`3bc8fbe` — a librarian FILING commit (*"librarian: the third copy filed
…"*) — and run `32486133822` at that commit is `success`.** `v0.8.0`'s
tag is on a **code** commit. ⇒ **a re-run of CI at `08a88bd` will still
be red**, because a re-run checks out `08a88bd` and this filing is not in
`08a88bd`. **The seventh check is unsatisfiable for this tag,
permanently**, and no amount of re-running fixes it. That `v0.7.0` came
out green was not luck exactly, but it was not a decision either — it was
a property of which commit happened to be `HEAD` at tagging time.

**The remedies. The choice is the engineer's and the operator's, not this
role's:**

| option | effect | cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Leave it** — `v0.8.0` ships with a known-red CI run and this entry is the record of why | honest, append-only, nothing rewritten | `verify-release.py v0.8.0` stays at 6/7 forever |
| **B. Move the tag** to the filing commit and force-push it | 7/7 | **rewrites a published tag on a public repo**; anyone who already fetched `v0.8.0` gets a different commit. `D:/dev/rag/rust/a_lightweight_git_tag_is_a_mutable_label_not_a_pin.md` is the neighbouring hazard |
| **C. Adopt the ordering from `v0.8.1` on** — file, watch CI go green, *then* tag | 7/7 from now on, nothing rewritten | one step of discipline, and **`R209` already says it** |

**C is what this role would take and it costs nothing.** Recorded in
`NEXT_SESSION.md` as owed. **No rule minted:** `R209` (*a CI job with no
local runner is unobserved, not passing*) already carries the observation
half, and the ordering half is now written into `verify-release.py`'s own
failure text — **a message printed at the moment of failure is a better
carrier than a rule nobody greps.**

##### ★★★★★ AND THIS IS NOT NEW — THE SWEEP FOUND IT ALREADY RECORDED, WITH A RATE

**The hard-rule-11 sweep turned this up and it changes the entry's
claim, so it is written here rather than quietly dropped.** This project
has recorded the same hazard before, twice, and **with a measured rate**:

> *"`v0.5.2` was the **first release in this project's history tagged at
> a commit CI had already accepted** … Three of the four releases before
> it were tagged at commits CI had rejected, and `v0.3.0` was published
> with failing tests."* — and its own 2026-08-12 amendment: **"Full-history
> figure: `5 of 8` (62.5 %) across all eight tags to date."**

**Updated denominator, and it is the part that stings.** `v0.7.0` was
the release where `R209` was applied for the first time and CI was
**observed green before the tag was placed** — the 221st filing records
that explicitly as the point of the exercise. **`v0.8.0` is the very next
release, and it regressed.** ⇒ **the practice did not survive one
release.**

**So the transferable finding is NOT "we discovered a hazard".** It is:
**a hazard recorded three times, with a rate, and fixed once by
discipline, recurred at the first opportunity — because the fix lived in
a person's memory of an ordering rather than in the procedure.** That is
why remedy **C** above is written as a step in the release procedure and
carried in `NEXT_SESSION.md` §0, not as a rule number. **`verify-release.py`
catching it is the machinery working**; what is missing is the ordering
being *enforced* rather than *remembered*, and **nothing in this filing
supplies that** — a future session that wants a real fix should make the
release procedure tag from a filing commit by construction.

**Rate, filed with its denominator (hard rule 10):** `5 of 8` tags as of
`v0.5.3` (recorded 2026-08-12); `v0.7.0` green (recorded 2026-08-21);
`v0.8.0` red (this entry). `v0.6.0`'s status is **not re-measured here** —
GitHub Actions retention makes a 2026-08-17 run unreliable to query, and
a number this role cannot produce is one it does not assert.

#### ★★★ THE DISK INCIDENT — a release cannot be built on a full disk

| what | measured |
|---|---|
| first packaging attempt | failed: **`"There is not enough space on the disk (os error 112)"`** |
| `D:` at that moment | **100 % used, 0 bytes free** |
| `target/` | **110 GB**, of which `target/debug` = **103 GB** (94 %) |
| after deleting `target/debug` | 89 % used, **112 GB free** — and the packaging succeeded |
| `D:` **at the time of this filing** | **86 % used, 137 GB free of 954 GB** (`df -h /d`) — more has been freed since |
| `.claude/worktrees` | **28 GB across seven stale agent worktrees**, **left alone** |

**This is a standing hazard, not an incident.** `target/debug` grows
without bound across a long run of `cargo test` / `cargo run` sessions,
and the failure it produces lands on the **release build** — the one step
that cannot be retried cheaply and the one an operator is waiting on.
The 28 GB of stale worktrees is a second, independent reservoir that
nothing currently reclaims.

Filed to `D:/dev/rag/rust/` as an ecosystem fact (nothing about it is
pdfce-specific) and to `NEXT_SESSION.md` as a pre-flight check.

**★ Struck 2026-08-29 (323rd filing).** The 28 GB reservoir measured above
is gone — operator-authorised (*"clean up the scratch copies"*): seven
stale agent worktrees plus ten leftover `worktree-agent-*` branches
removed, `.claude/` now measures 1.4 MB, `git worktree list` shows only
`main`, repo verified healthy at `cf37a27`. This closes the specific
reservoir measured at filing time, **not** the standing hazard mechanism
above it (`target/debug` growth, worktree accumulation over a long
autonomous-dispatch run), which is unchanged and will recur.

#### `FEATURES.md` — NO CAPABILITY ROW MOVES; ONE STALE LITERAL REPAIRED

**The ruling, stated explicitly because the dispatch asked for it: a
release changes no capability row, and this one did not.** `v0.8.0`
publishes already-shipped capability under a new version number; nothing
became reachable at `08a88bd` that was not reachable at `08a88bd^`.

**But the hard-rule-11 sweep — searching for the CLAIM, not for a string
— found one survivor, and it is a version literal:**

- **`docs/FEATURES.md:266`** read *"`-V` stays the bare parseable
  **`pdfce-cli 0.7.0`**"*. **Falsified by this commit**: root
  `Cargo.toml:77` is `version = "0.8.0"`, and the packaging smoke test
  printed `pdfce-cli 0.8.0`. **Repaired to a version-agnostic form rather
  than to `0.8.0`** — a hand-maintained version number in a document is a
  number that will be stale again at the next bump, and *"remember to
  update it"* is a reminder rather than a remedy. That is **the same
  argument `README.md`'s own comment block makes** about the version
  label it deleted. Deletion of the claim, not correction of it
  (`R216`).

**Three near-survivors RULED CORRECT and deliberately NOT edited:**

- **`README.md:57`** — *"it said `v0.3.0` through `v0.4.0`, `v0.5.x`,
  `v0.6.0` and `v0.7.0` — **FOUR releases**"*. There are now **five**
  releases, so a string-grep flags this. **It is not a survivor.** The
  sentence is a **static historical claim** about what the README used to
  say — true when written, unfalsifiable by any later release — which is
  exactly the distinction `R216` draws between *static* and
  *self-referential*. **Editing it would be the defect, not the repair.**
- **`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:7719`** — `hayro-write` 0.7.0. A different
  crate's version number. Not a survivor.
- **`docs/FEATURES.md:339`** — *"Release and distribution channel"*,
  `[ ] core · [ ] cli · — gui`. **Left unticked, and that is a
  judgement, not an oversight.** Four prior releases (`v0.5.1` …
  `v0.7.0`) shipped while this row stayed unticked, so whatever the row
  means, it does not mean *"a GitHub release with a portable asset
  exists"* — that has been true since `v0.1.0`. **Never tick a box you
  cannot substantiate.** What the row actually claims is carried to
  `NEXT_SESSION.md` as an owed question.

#### ★★★★★ THE DISPOSITION REVERSED AND THE RULING DID NOT — READ THIS BEFORE TREATING THE 238th FILING AS OVERTURNED

The 238th filing found the defect, recorded it in the `bc6c818` Shipped entry
under the heading **"DISPOSITION: RECORDED HERE. NOT REPAIRED, AND NOT OWED"**,
and gave two reasons. One filing later the engineer repaired it. **That is not a
reversal of the ruling, and reading it as one would mislead the next session in
the expensive direction** — it would license repairing self-referential claims by
rewording, which is the practice the whole sequence was about.

| the 238th filing's reason | status after `8522167` |
|---|---|
| *"Repairing it writes an eighth sentence about a seventh correction, which is the generator by definition"* | **Correct, and untouched.** It is an argument about what a **rewording** costs. `8522167` wrote no eighth sentence — it **removed** four ordinals and a distance and left one short parenthetical in their place, whose content is a **rule** (*an ordinal is a claim*) rather than a claim about this document's edit history |
| *"`ROADMAP.md` and `SESSION_LOG.md` are where it belongs, which is the finding's own remedy"* | **Correct, and still where it lives.** The full round-by-round numbering, both ladders, and the reason they disagree are in this file and in `SESSION_LOG.md`; **none of it went back into the README** |

⇒ **The record was doing its job.** A disposition of *"recorded, not repaired,
and here is the remedy if you ever touch it"* is a **hand-off**, not a refusal,
and it terminated in one round because the remedy was written beside the decline
rather than left to be inferred.

#### ★★★★★ THE RULING ASKED FOR — accepted, as a SHARPENING and not as a duplicate

**The question, verbatim from the dispatch:** *"If that generalises — for a
self-referential claim, prefer deletion to correction, because a correction is
another instance of the class — it may belong beside the finding you filed rather
than inside it. Your call, including 'already implied by it'."*

**Ruling: it is NOT already implied, it DOES generalise, and it belongs INSIDE
the finding as a sharpening of its consequence 1 — not beside it, and not as
`R216`.** Three parts, and the third is the one that keeps it honest.

**(1) Not already implied.** The RAG finding's consequence 1 currently reads
*"prefer DELETION to a seventh rewording — a deletion is the only repair that
emits **no new claim**"*. That warrant is **true of every deletion anywhere** and
says nothing about self-reference. The proposed version supplies the **mechanism**
consequence 1 asserts without stating: **a correction to a self-referential claim
is drawn from the same distribution as the defect**, because the only way to say
*where* or *how many* is another coordinate or another count. ⇒ the existing
sentence says *deletion is cheap*; the sharpening says *correction is
specifically, mechanically expensive here*. **A reader who has only the first
will reword and believe they have complied.**

**(2) It generalises, and this project has now measured it.** Both remedies this
session produced were deletions, arrived at independently — the five *"two lines
above"* distances (`bc6c818`'s filing) and these ordinals (`8522167`). Both were
reached by the same route: an attempt to write the corrected version produced a
sentence of the same shape, and the shape was the defect. **`n=2` remedies, one
document.**

**(3) ★★★★★ THE BOUNDARY, WITHOUT WHICH THIS IS A LICENCE TO DELETE CORRECTIONS
GENERALLY — and it is already this project's practice under another name.**
*Preserve wrong VALUES, delete wrong POINTERS* (filed at `641deb9`). The two
statements are the same statement:

- **A self-referential claim has no value to preserve.** Its entire content is a
  coordinate into the document — a position, a distance, an ordinal, a count of
  the document's own parts. Delete it and **nothing is lost**, because the thing
  it pointed at is still there and can be named.
- **A wrong VALUE must be preserved** (`R215` (d)), because a bare corrected
  number gets re-derived back to the wrong one by the next reader with the same
  faulty intuition. **A deletion there destroys the evidence.**

⇒ **The rule is not "prefer deletion". It is "prefer deletion WHEN THE CLAIM'S
CONTENT IS A COORDINATE", and the test is whether anything is lost by removing
it.** `11 of 11` may never be deleted; *"rounds 5 and 6"* may never be corrected.

**Filed as:** a sharpening of consequence 1 of
`D:/dev/rag/rust/a_document_that_annotates_its_own_corrections_has_made_its_edit_history_part_of_its_content.md`,
with the boundary written beside it. **NOT minted as a rule of its own** — it
prescribes **how to word a repair**, which `R214` (a)–(d) already govern and which
the *Update protocol* practice already carries; and a rule saying *"prefer
deletion"* would commission **work, not care**. **`R214` and `R215` NOT amended.**

★★ **What DID earn a number in this filing is a different claim, and the pair is
recorded together so the dispositions are legible:** `R216` binds **which file a
class of content may appear in** — a **placement** obligation, with a named
trigger that fired, a measured cost and **two documents** behind it. **Placement
earned a number; wording did not.** See the sweep section below and `R216` in
*Standing rules*.

It reads *"**The round-7 note in the founding instance carries a wrong ordinal**
for exactly this reason"* — **present tense, same falsification, in the copy that

**★★★★★ AND THE SWEEP FOUND THE THING THAT FIRED A TRIGGER — `docs/NEXT_SESSION.md`
IS THE SECOND DOCUMENT, AND `R216` IS MINTED.** The convergence practice's second
amendment (`bc6c818`, one filing earlier) wrote its own promotion condition down

immediately before it was rewritten: **three** parenthetical *"this paragraph
read X until 2026-08-23"* annotations (§5 twice, §6 item 17), plus a running

★★★★★ **The mechanism is a TENSION BETWEEN TWO RULES, not carelessness, and that
is what makes it worth a number.** `R215` (d) **obliges** preserving the wrong
wording beside a correction. That obligation is **free in an append-only file**
— written once, dated, never touched again — and in an **overwritten** file it
means **hand-carrying the wording into every rewrite**, where each carry is a
fresh unchecked claim about the document's own current contents. ⇒ **the
obligation is discharged by the append-only record on the overwritten document's
behalf**: preserve it in `ROADMAP.md`/`SESSION_LOG.md`, once; in the overwritten
document write a **pointer**, or nothing. **`R215` (d) is unchanged and
unweakened — `R216` says WHERE, not whether.** ★ The measured cost of not having
it: `NEXT_SESSION.md`'s *"Everything below this line is unchanged from the
previous handoff"*, **false in the commit that wrote it**, carried forward as
boilerplate by successive rewrites. **The layer is DELETED in this filing's
rewrite, not corrected** — `R216` (c), which is clause (c) applied to the
document that founded it.

**★★★★★ The shape, and it is the third consecutive filing to hit it: A
DISPOSITION IS A CLAIM ABOUT A DOCUMENT'S CURRENT STATE, AND IT AGES LIKE ONE.**
*"Not repaired"*, *"still owed"*, *"unbuilt"*, *"carried forward unstarted"* are
all self-referential in exactly the sense this session's finding names — their
truth depends on the state of something outside the record, and **the record has
no mechanism that revisits them.** They are the same species as *"the table
above"*, one indirection out. ⇒ **write a disposition with its date and its
subject's hash attached** (*"not repaired as of `bc6c818`"*), which makes it
**static** and unfalsifiable by any later event, instead of a standing assertion
about the present. **Both repairs above apply that form.**

#### ★★★★★ THE FINDING — THE GENERATOR, AND WHY NAMING IT IS WHAT ENDED THE SEQUENCE

**The engineer's statement of it**, which this filing accepts as substantially
correct and sharpens in one place:

> *A document that annotates its own corrections has made its correction history
> part of its content — and that part has no tests, no measurements and no reader
> who would notice. It generates defects at a steady rate, and each repair adds
> another sentence to the generator.*

**The evidence, and it is stronger than any round's evidence taken alone.**
Across six rounds against `tools/gen-scale-demo/README.md`:

| what | measured |
|---|---|
| defects found in the **engineering content** (the arithmetic, the `f32` limit derivations, the drift formula, the measurement table's values) | **0** after round 1. The three `f32` limits, the `page_x × scale / 16 700 000` drift, the `21.5 µm` ulp and the table's five rows are **unchanged since `4af0c08`** |
| defects found in **sentences about a previous correction** | **every one of them** — the scope sentences, the pre/post boundary pointers, *"the sentence above it"*, the universal-plus-hedge, *"three post-fix columns"*, *"the gap between `after` and `correct`"* |
| rounds in which the repair emitted a fresh defect of the class it repaired | **`n=3` consecutive** (`641deb9`, `39b449f`, `a68498b`), plus **`n=1` more in this role's own tree**, found by item 8 below ⇒ **`n=4`** |

⇒ **The class was stable because the GENERATOR was stable.** The 236th filing
read class stability as a stopping signal; the 237th read it as the repair
process generating its own input; **this one names what the input is.** Those
three readings are the same observation at increasing resolution, and only the
third of them prescribes anything, because only the third identifies something
that can be **removed**.

**★★★★★ THE SHARPENING, and it is the part that makes the ruling below possible.
The generator is not "edit history in an artefact". It is SELF-REFERENTIAL
CLAIMS — claims whose truth depends on the document's own CURRENT contents.**

- *"Its one measurement table carries three post-fix columns"* — true or false
  depending on what the table looks like **right now**. Every edit to §9 puts it
  back in question, and no edit to §9 will make anyone re-read it.
- *"§9's last paragraph"*, *"the sentence above it"*, *"Everything in this
  section"*, *"Everything below this line"* — same property. **All of them are
  claims about a SET, a POSITION or a COUNT within the document that holds them.**
- Against which: *"the acceptance criterion for this Pass was `11 of 11`"* is
  **also** edit history, is **also** a sentence about a previous correction, and
  is **fixed forever**. It was true when written, it is true now, and no edit to
  the README can falsify it. **It generates nothing.**

⇒ **The dangerous property is SELF-REFERENCE, not HISTORICITY.** A document may
carry facts about its own past safely; what it cannot carry safely is assertions
about its own present. **This is why `R214` (a)–(d) all bite on this file and why
none of them was sufficient** — each names one syntactic form of self-reference
(a positional pointer, a *now*-relative reference, a scope statement) and the
supply of forms is not enumerable. **Placement is enumerable; syntax is not.**

**The remedy, therefore, is PLACEMENT, not care** — which is what makes this
filable at all under this project's bar (a rule that commissions *work* rather
than *care* is declined, and so is one that commissions care):

> **Edit history goes in `ROADMAP.md` and `SESSION_LOG.md`.** They are
> **append-only** (a claim there is dated and scoped to a moment, so no later
> edit can falsify it), **dated** (the reader knows what it was true of), and
> **read by someone looking for exactly that** (so it has a reader who would
> notice). **The artefact is for the artefact.**

★★ **And the cost of getting placement right is zero**, unlike every remedy
considered in the previous six rounds. There is no sentence to re-read, no
quantifier to check against a set, no gate to build and no baseline to measure.
**The sentence simply goes somewhere else.**

#### ★★★★ THE PRACTICE / RULE / RAG JUDGEMENT — the dispatch's item 4

**The candidate**, stated as strongly as it can be: *a document that annotates
its own corrections has made its correction history part of its content, and
that part generates defects at a steady rate; the remedy is placement — edit
history belongs in the append-only, dated record.*

**Judgement, in four parts.**

**(1) It AMENDS the *Update protocol* practice, and REPLACES its headline for the
second time.** *"How you know a document is converging"* has now been amended
twice against the same sequence, and this amendment is the one that makes the
original observation **explicable** rather than merely **falsified**: the class
was stable because the generator was stable. The practice's text and its first
amendment both stay standing, per the append-only convention and `R215` (d).

**(2) It does NOT amend `R214`, and the decline matters.** `R214` is about
**references** — clause (a) naming a referent, (b) never resolving against *now*,
(c) repairing at the referent, (d) verifying a scope statement against its
delimited contents. **All four are rules about how to WRITE a self-referential
claim.** This finding says **do not write that class of claim in that document at
all**, which is upstream of all four and is not a fifth way of writing one. ★★
**Folding it in as clause (e) would put a placement rule inside a reference rule
and detach the remedy from the four defects that motivate it** — the same
argument that declined `R216` one filing ago, pointed the other way.

**(3) NO RULE MINTED. CEILING UNMOVED AT `R215`; `R216` STILL FREE.** Declined on
two grounds, both stronger than the instance count:

- **`n=1` document.** The generator has been observed in exactly one artefact.
  This project's bar is two occurrences before a shape earns an `R` number, and
  that bar has been applied to weaker-looking candidates in this same sequence.
- **The *Update protocol* section is the right home by precedent, not by

#### ★★★★ THE PRACTICE JUDGEMENT — the dispatch's item 4, and the answer is AMEND, not "already covered"

**What the practice says today** (*Update protocol*, *"How you know a document is
converging"*, added by the 236th filing): five rounds against one file left
**wrong quantifiers and wrong references, and no wrong values**; the residue
class is the stopping signal; **counter-caution — the residue re-seeds itself.**

**Round 6 falsifies two of its three components and strengthens the third.**

| the practice's claim | round 6's measurement |
|---|---|
| *"no wrong values left"* — the number-shaped defects are swept out | **FALSE.** Survivor E is a **wrong count** (`three` for `two`), and this role's own *"two-thirds"* is a **wrong fraction**. Two wrong values in one round, one of them in the report that prompted it |
| the residue is *"wrong quantifiers and wrong references"*, the class only reading catches | **Half true, and it is not a residue — it is production.** Round 6 emitted a **fresh** wrong reference (survivor G), of the class round 5 declared **structurally** fixed by promoting the boundary to a heading |
| **counter-caution:** *"the residue re-seeds itself"* | **CONFIRMED AND MEASURED AT `n=3`** — three consecutive rounds in which the sentence written to repair a quantifier defect carried a new one. **This is the dominant source of the residue, not a caveat on it** |

★★★★★ **The amendment, in one line: a stable defect class after repeated rounds
is evidence that the REPAIR PROCESS is generating its own input, not evidence
that the document is approaching a fixed point.**

★★★ **And the trajectory is retired.** The dispatch offered a summary of the
sequence — *wrong **values** → wrong **pointers** → wrong **quantifiers** → wrong
**antecedents***, each round finding fewer and sharper defects. **It is a true
description of what each round FOUND FIRST. It is not a description of what the
document CONTAINS.** Round 6 produced a wrong count **and** a wrong positional
pointer **simultaneously**, so the classes **recur rather than retire**, and a
reader who takes the ladder literally stops looking one rung down. **The
observation is kept with its refutation attached rather than deleted** — which is
`R215` (d) applied to a practice instead of to a number.

**⇒ Practice AMENDED in place** (append-only: the original text stays, the
amendment is dated and marked). **Cross-project finding amended in the same
filing:**
`D:/dev/rag/rust/the_defect_class_left_after_repeated_repair_rounds_is_the_stopping_signal.md`.

ships.*

   hard rule 10's corollary and hard rule 11's corollary. Clause (d), minted one

   *"really apply `R214`"* obliges nothing the first did not.

   verbatim the reason clause (d) was filed as a clause **one filing ago**.

   produced it.

new clause** either; its clause (d) worked-instance table gains a **third row**
instead, which is the cheapest form of evidence accumulation this record has.

#### ★★★★★ THE RULE JUDGEMENT — the engineer asked for a ruling and recommended a DECLINE; the ruling is an AMENDMENT, and the reason is evidence he did not have

**The question, quoted from the dispatch so the ruling is auditable:**

> *"A structural fix bought immunity to positional DRIFT and not to
> OVER-SCOPING. A heading-bound claim is still a claim about a set, and it can
> be wrong about what is in it."* … *"My own reading is that it is a **decline
> with a recorded fact** — it is one instance, and the general shape ('fixing
> the form of a claim does not check its content') is close to platitude. But
> the specific version is not: **when you convert prose into structure, re-read
> the structure's own boundary statements as claims, because they are new
> assertions nobody has checked.** That is checkable and was missed."*

**The specific version is right, and the decline is overturned on a fact the
dispatch could not have had, because it was found by reading the artefact after
the commit rather than by reading the commit.**

**★★★★ `n` is 2, not 1, and the second instance is LIVE.** §10 opens:

> ★ **"Everything in this section describes pdfce as it stands."**

That is **the same construction, in the same file, in the section the split
created as §9's twin** — and it is false of **four** of §10's own passages:

| # | the passage | why it is not "pdfce as it stands" |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | *"Before the fix, the same computed region put it **76 px out horizontally and 288 px vertically**"* | a **before**-figure — **structurally identical** to the `after`/`correct` columns that falsified §9's sentence |
| 2 | *"This paragraph said "11 of 11 forms survive at every scale tested" until 2026-08-23"* | preserved evidence under `R215` (d) — a record of what the document said, not of what pdfce does |
| 3 | *"The figure `93 s` … is the **rejected** device-space attempt"* | the provenance of a **discarded draft** |
| 4 | *"Note which direction the error travelled … The number began as an **expectation** in a roadmap table"* | subject is a **roadmap table's history**, not pdfce at all |

**The symmetry is the argument.** Every defence available to §10's sentence
(*"it means the section is ABOUT current behaviour"*) was equally available to
§9's, and was rejected one commit ago by the engineer's own hand. A rule that
holds in §9 and not in §10 is not a rule.

**★★★ Why an AMENDMENT to `R214` and not `R216`.** Three grounds, in the order
that decides it:

1. **The defect is a RIDER ON `R214`'s OWN PRESCRIBED REMEDY.** `641deb9` is
   recorded, one entry below, as *"`R214` clause (a)'s first argued
   application"* — the remedy is **promote the boundary to a heading**. That
   remedy **manufactures a scope sentence**, and a scope sentence is where this
   defect lives. **Filing the warning under a separate number detaches it from
   the remedy that causes it**, so the next reader applies clause (a) and repeats
   the defect — which is precisely what happened here, twice, in one commit.
2. **`R214` clause (c) already says the repair is a NEW CLAIM** and earns hard
   rule 10's corollary and hard rule 11's corollary. What clause (c) does **not**
   say is *what kind* of new claim a **structural** repair makes, and its
   remedy vocabulary — *name the referent* — gives no instruction for a
   **quantifier**. ⇒ the amendment supplies the missing half of a clause that is
   already there, rather than asserting something new.
3. **The general form IS close to platitude, exactly as the dispatch says**, and
   a mint on *"fixing the form of a claim does not check its content"* would fail
   `R210`'s minting test for breadth. **The narrow form passes the same
   decidability test `R214` was minted on**: *"is this scope sentence true of
   this section's contents?"* is answerable **from one span of one file with no
   knowledge of pdfce's behaviour** — you need only see an `after` column or the
   words *"before the fix"*. That is a **stronger** decidability position than
   `R214`'s own *"is this reference right?"* half, which requires reading the
   increment site.

⇒ **`R214` AMENDED with clause (d). CEILING UNMOVED at `R215`; `R216` STILL
FREE.** Full text under *Standing rules*.

**★ What is NOT claimed, so the amendment is not over-read.** This does not bind
on every heading in the project. It binds on **a scope statement written to
delimit a section's contents** — the artefact a structural split produces.
Ordinary section headings assert nothing about their contents and are untouched.

#### ★★★★★ THE DECLINE IS THE ARTEFACT — why a THIRD reworded sentence was refused

The 234th filing reported two survivors in `tools/gen-scale-demo/README.md` §9
and prescribed the remedy structurally rather than verbally. **The engineer
applied the prescription verbatim, and the reasoning is worth preserving
separately from the diff**, because the diff shows only what was done.

**What stood before, and why it is one defect and not two:**

| | the sentence | where it pointed | truth at `641deb9`'s parent |
|---|---|---|---|
| **older** | *"Everything below describes the behaviour before that Pass"* | everything under a `★` mid-section | **FALSE** — post-fix material had grown beneath it |
| **newer** | *"Everything from the top of this section down to here … **What follows describes the current behaviour**"* | a line ~40 lines further down | **FALSE** — two current-behaviour paragraphs sat *above* it |

The newer sentence was **written as the repair of the older one**, and it was
already wrong when it was written. That is `R214` twice in one section: a
positional pointer (clause (a)), and a repair made at the neighbour rather than
at the referent (clause (c)).

**The ruling: reword nothing, split the section.** Stated as the rule the next
session needs:

> **A pre/post boundary written in prose is a pointer into a document that
> grows. Rewording it buys the interval until the next paragraph lands, and
> nothing more.** The failure is **intrinsic to the form**, not a symptom of
> imprecise wording — so a third rewording is not a better repair, it is the
> same repair with a shorter fuse.
>
> **Promote the boundary to a section heading.** A heading cannot drift,
> **because the thing it delimits is the thing that would have to move it** —
> the boundary and the content are the same object, so they cannot get out of
> step. The commit says this out loud inside §9 rather than only in its message,
> which is the part that survives a future reader who never reads `git log`.

**Both sentences DELETED, not reworded** — the second half of the ruling, and
the half a hurried fix would skip. A reworded survivor left in place is a third
copy of the claim, and this file's own history says copies are what propagate.

**Why deleting these is not the destruction `R214` (c) warns about, nor an
`R215` (d) violation.** `R215` (d) requires a wrong **value** to stay visible
beside its correction, because a bare corrected number gets re-derived back to
the wrong one. **A positional pointer has no value to preserve** — the evidence
is *that the form fails*, not *what the sentence said* — and that evidence is
preserved, in §9's own text, in `641deb9`'s message, and in the table above.
**The distinction is worth carrying: preserve wrong VALUES, delete wrong
POINTERS.**

is invisible to anyone auditing the project's history**, and because the last
such amendment (2026-08-18) is recorded in the rule's own text with no
project-side entry — a gap this entry closes for both.

**Trigger widened.** It fired on *"a counter or capability changed meaning"*. It
now **also fires on minting a rule about a number**, and the sweep it owes runs

tree holding the rule.

**The warrant, quoted in the amendment, is this role's `n=2` observation:**

it.* `R215` was minted because *"11 of 11 forms at every scale"* was an
impossible acceptance criterion; the mint swept `docs/`, where the criterion
lived; **the same wrong number then surfaced twice in `tools/`** — once as a

   expectation invites checking; a result does not.*

   sentence.

does not consume `085`. §12 records decisions about **the program** — crate
boundaries, invariants, library choices. This changes **how a librarian reads**,

instance actually reads. **The decision counter stays at `084`.**

2026-08-18 amendment. An agent editing its own governing rules is not an
amendment, it is a rewrite; the engineer's signature is what makes it one.

#### ★★★★★ THE FINDING, AND THE RULE JUDGEMENT THE DISPATCH ASKED FOR

**The mechanism, in four sentences.** A number is written as an **expectation** —
an acceptance row, a *"required after"* column, a target. It is identified there
as **wrong**, and the correct value is recorded, correctly, in the documents that
file the fix. Then the write-up is composed: **and writing up a fix, you reach
for the criterion you were working against and report it as met.** The same
wrong number lands in a third document **as an outcome**, where nothing about
its form invites a check.

⇒ ***An expectation invites checking; a result does not.*** Moving a number from
the first slot to the second **removes the only mechanism that would have caught
it**, and the move happens **naturally** rather than carelessly, which is why
neither review nor a gate saw it.

**The remedy is a form, not a diligence request. THE CORRECTION IS THE ARTEFACT,
NOT THE CORRECTED VALUE.** Record *"this said **X**; **X** is impossible because
**Y**; it is **Z**"*, and **keep X visible**. A bare `Z` is re-derived back to
`X` by the next person reasoning from the same faulty intuition — **including
yourself an hour later** — because the intuition that produced `X` is still
correct-sounding and nothing beside `Z` disputes it. The repaired README does
exactly this: it quotes the sentence it replaces, states the date it stood
until, and says why `11` was never achievable.

##### The ruling: **`R215` clause (d)**, not `R216`, and not a decline

Three candidate containers were weighed. The warrant for each, so the ruling is
checkable rather than asserted:

- **Not a decline as already-covered.** The closest existing text is hard rule
  10's corollary (*a correction is a claim; name its world-source*) and `R214`
  clause (c) (*repair at the referent*). **Both bind the correction's
  SOURCING; neither binds its FORM.** Nothing on disk says *keep the wrong value
  visible*, even though this project has now done it twice —
  `R215`'s own text preserves the wrong column verbatim, and the repaired README
  quotes the sentence it replaces. **A convention practised twice and stated
  nowhere is one hurried edit from being lost**, which is the standard this
  section already applies to `R209` and `R212`.
- **Not `R216`.** Precedent set one filing ago: `R211` was **amended** rather
  than a new number minted, on the ground that *"this is not a new surface; it is
  the surface the rule was minted on, and did not finish."* **That test is
  satisfied more strongly here than there** — the instance is **literally
  `R215`'s own founding number**, in its second escape. And splitting would
  split **one number's lifecycle across two rules**: `R215` (a)–(c) govern the
  moment the expectation is **written**, and stop there; this governs the moment
  it is **corrected**. **The reader who discharges (a)–(c) is the same person
  who will later write the results-up**, and a separate `R216` would sit where
  that person has no reason to look.
- **Why it is nonetheless a genuinely new clause and not a restatement.**
  `R215`'s mechanism is **how the expected value is DERIVED** (attribution — a
  second correct mechanism moves the same number). This is **where the number
  later LANDS** (a genre change from expectation to result). **The remedies
  differ and do not imply one another**: `R215`'s is *re-derive the expected
  value from first principles*; clause (d)'s is *when you correct one, publish
  the correction rather than the corrected value*. A reader could discharge
  either while failing the other, which is the test this section uses for
  whether text is doing work.

**★ The honest cost of amending rather than minting, recorded as a ruling and
not an oversight — same disclosure `R211`'s amendment made.** The general form
**reaches past acceptance oracles**: corrections happen for reasons that have
nothing to do with `R215` — a typo, a unit error, a re-measurement — and every
one of them can come back as a result. Binding it inside `R215` hides it from
someone correcting a figure that was never an oracle. **Mitigated the way
`R211` mitigated its own:** the general form is filed as a fact in
`D:/dev/rag/rust/a_number_identified_as_wrong_in_an_expectation_comes_back_as_a_measured_result.md`,
where the correction-methodology findings already live, rather than as a rule
whose condition nobody's situation matches.

#### ★★★★ THE SECOND QUESTION — *"a minted rule protects the document it was minted in"* — ANSWERED YES, AT n=2

**The dispatch's own observation, and it is correct: this is the second
consecutive filing in which `R215`'s founding instance escaped forward.**

| filing | where it escaped to | found by |
|---|---|---|
| **232nd** (`R215` minted) | `tools/gen-scale-demo/README.md` §9 prose, as a **result** | not found — the mint swept `docs/`, not `tools/` |

| **234th** (this one) | the **table header** in the same section (`1b` above), and **two** boundary claims still wrong | **reading the file again, after the repair** |

**The diagnosis, stated so it is actionable rather than rueful: minting a rule
about a number is itself a MEANING-CHANGE EVENT, and hard rule 11 already

#### ★ THE ID RULING — A **NEW** ID (`74.10`), NOT AN AMENDMENT TO `74.7`, AND THE DISPATCH LEANED THE OTHER WAY

**The engineer wrote *"I lean amendment, but you have the better view of the
numbering."* The ruling is a new ID**, and it is worth arguing because the
amendment case is genuinely strong: `d8f3020` completes a guarantee `74.7`
stated, and `74.7`'s own entry two commits ago set the precedent that *"the
scope grew to cover its own stated exclusion inside one Pass, so one ID covers
both."*

**Three grounds decide it the other way.**

1. **`PASS 74.7` IS ALREADY FILED AS SHIPPED, WITH A COMMIT TABLE AND A LEDGER
   ROW.** `74.7` grew across two commits *before it shipped*, at filing time,
   which is grouping. Growing a **shipped** entry two filings later makes
   *"`Pass 74.7`"* a moving target: a reader who cited *"`74.7`, shipped
   2026-08-23 across `1d6db9e` + `5b0d885`"* would find a third commit under the
   same name and no way to tell when it arrived. Hard rule 1 (*Shipped is
   append-only; history does not get rewritten*) and hard rule 2 (*Pass IDs are
   stable*) both point here.
2. **★★ THE SEQUENCE IS THE LESSON, AND FOLDING IT IN DESTROYS IT.** `74.7`
   **created** this defect — it moved the interpreter to `f64` and left the
   recorder in `f32`. Filed as one Pass, *"a precision fix opened a precision
   divergence"* becomes invisible: the entry would read as one clean piece of
   work. Filed as two, the sequence is legible and checkable — `74.7` shipped,
   it left a second path behind, **the filing of `74.7` flagged the question**,
   and `74.10` closed it. **That is the audit trail the append-only rule exists
   to produce**, and it is exactly the shape `R211` and `decision 081` are
   about: *moving one caller falsifies a claim in a file nobody edited.*
3. **The two Passes deliver different kinds of thing.** `74.7` **raises** a
   ceiling; `74.10` **refuses** past one. A reader following *"see `74.7`"*
   wants *how deep zoom became precise*; a reader following *"why did the
   recorder refuse at scale 5 000?"* wants a different story, with a different
   mechanism and a different caller obligation (fall back).

**`74.10` was the next free in the family** and the two-digit sub-ID is house
style (`Pass 47.10`/`47.11`, already on disk). **Next free in the family is now
`74.11`.** **A dated amendment is appended to `PASS 74.7`'s Shipped entry**
pointing forward to this one, so neither entry can be read alone and get the
wrong picture — the same forward-pointer convention the decision log uses for a
superseded decision.

#### ★★★★★ THE DEFECT — TWO RENDERING PATHS, ONE `f64` AND ONE `f32`, AGREEING EVERYWHERE ANYONE LOOKED

**What `PASS 74.7` changed:** the interpreter carries the CTM in `f64` through
content-stream composition (`Mat64`) and builds paths relative to their own first
point when `needs_precise_paths` fires.

**What it did not change:** a recorded `DisplayList` stores **every op's CTM as
an `f32` `Transform`**, and `replay_region` post-translates that by the region's
device origin, **also in `f32`**. Neither narrowing has anything to widen back
to — the precision is gone at record time.

**★ And nothing bounded the recorder, deliberately.** `record_page`'s own
comment reads:

> *"a recording allocates no raster, so the `MAX_PIXMAP_EDGE` ceiling does NOT
> apply here — that is the point of recording at a deep zoom."*

**Deep zoom is the INTENDED use of a recording**, which is why the absence of a
bound is a defect rather than an untested corner.

**Measured cost of the `f32` translation, filed per-scale beside its cause (hard
rule 10 (a)):**

| recording `scale` | letter-page translation carried in the op's CTM | error in device pixels |
|---:|---:|---:|
| `5 000` | `~4 × 10⁶` | **half a device pixel** |
| `500 000` | `~4 × 10⁸` | **47 px** |

⇒ **after `74.7`, a page replayed from a list and the same page rendered fresh
were the same picture at ordinary scales and different pictures at deep zoom**,
with nothing on either path saying so. That is `R211`'s condition — *two code
paths that owe each other byte-identical output* — and `decision 081`'s subject,
one level down: `081` gave the two paths **one `f64` entry point for region
GEOMETRY**; nothing had been said about **content**.

---

#### ★★★★★ THE FIX — A REFUSAL, AND THE THRESHOLD IS A **SHARED PREDICATE** RATHER THAN A CHOSEN LIMIT

**`PoisonReason::ScaleBeyondF32`.** `record_page` returns
`RenderError::PageNotRecordable`, and the caller falls back to a direct render
that is correct at any scale — **the same fallback `pdfce-cli` already performs
for the seven capability refusals** (`sh`, shading patterns, overprint composites,
soft masks and the rest). No new caller shape, no new failure mode for a consumer
to learn.

**The module's own documentation had already argued for exactly this**, before
the defect existed:

> *"a display list that is subtly wrong is strictly worse than no display list.
> Refusing is loud, cheap, and correct."*

**★★ THE CONSTRUCTION THAT MAKES IT A BOUNDARY RATHER THAN A COMPROMISE, AND IT
IS THE PART TO CARRY FORWARD.** The threshold is **`Mat64::needs_precise_paths`
— the SAME predicate the interpreter consults to decide whether it needs its
`f64` route.** Consequently:

- **Below the predicate**, both paths do **identical `f32` arithmetic** and agree
  exactly — the recording is admissible because the thing it would have to match
  is itself `f32`.
- **Above the predicate**, one path switches to `f64` and the other **refuses**.

⇒ **There is no scale at which they quietly disagree.** That is the property
`R211` asks of a second rendering path, and it is obtained **by construction
rather than by testing**.

**★ Why a shared predicate beats two limits that happen to match.** Two
independently-chosen constants can agree today and drift apart in either
direction on any later edit, and **the band between them is a region where one
path is precise, the other is not, and both believe they are in agreement**.
Nothing reports that band; it has no error message and no counter. A shared
predicate makes the band **not exist** — it cannot open, because there is one
number and one place it is decided. **The next person adding a third rendering
path should reach for this**: *two paths that must agree share the predicate that
decides when they CAN, rather than each picking a limit.* Escalated to
`D:/dev/rag/rust/` (file named in the RAG list below) and minted as **decision
084**.

**★ The test asserts BOTH halves — refused by name at `5 000`, and still records
at `4.0`** — *because a guard that refuses everything is not a guard*, and the
engineer **verified it bites by disabling the condition**. That is `R162`'s
obligation (establish the positive case over the same container) met on a refusal
rather than on an absence.

---

#### ★★★★ THE ORACLE THAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT, AND THE RULE JUDGEMENT THE DISPATCH ASKED FOR

**`crates/pdfce-render/tests/region_matches_full_page.rs` is the differential
oracle for exactly this contract** — it is the artefact `R211` was minted on the
strength of. **It runs at scales up to `220`. The divergence begins near `530`.**
So it agreed everywhere it was asked, and everywhere it was asked it was right.

**The engineer asked whether this earns a rule or an `R215` amendment, and
recorded honest uncertainty about whether it is one mechanism or two.** It is
**two**, and the ruling is **neither of those**: it is an **amendment to `R211`**.

**Why it is NOT `R215`.** `R215` binds the **target** a test is written against,
and its mechanism is a **wrong expected value** produced by attribution — *the
oracle demands a number that a correct fix cannot produce*. Its failure mode is a
**false alarm on a correct fix**. Here every expected value is **right**; the
failure mode is the opposite — **a silent pass over a broken system** — and it is
produced by the **sampled domain**, not by the expectations. `R215`'s own scope
paragraph already refuses this: *"it does not bind on tests themselves."*

**Why it is not a new number either, which is the closer call.** The condition
that makes the sampling gap dangerous is **`R211`'s condition, verbatim** — two
code paths that owe each other byte-identical output. And `R211` already **names
`replay_region`** as one of the two call sites whose *"these cannot disagree"*
comment went false when a caller moved. **This is not a new surface for `R211`;
it is the surface `R211` was minted on, and did not finish.** Specifically,
**clause (c) under-delivered**: it obliges a *"cannot disagree"* comment to
**name the test that would go red**. Here the test was named, it existed, it ran,
it was green — **and it was silent**, because naming a test says nothing about
the domain the test samples. **A rule whose remedy can be satisfied while the
defect ships is an incomplete rule**, and the completion belongs in the rule, not
beside it.

**Minting `R216` would also split one mechanism across two numbers** — a reader
holding `R211` would have discharged it by naming a test, and a reader holding
`R216` would have no reason to consult `R211`'s asymmetric-narrowing analysis to
know **where** to sample. **They are the same obligation**: the narrowing
boundary is what must be sampled across.

⇒ **`R211` AMENDED with clauses (d) and (e). Ceiling UNMOVED — `R215` stands,
next free `R216`.** Full text under *Standing rules*; in one line: **(d)** where
one path *cannot* meet the contract past some magnitude, **both consult the SAME
predicate** to decide where, and the losing path **refuses** rather than
approximating; **(e)** the differential test that guards the contract **samples
on both sides of that predicate** — *it proves agreement only over the range it
samples, and a range is a claim.*

**★ The honest cost of amending rather than minting, recorded so it is a ruling
and not an oversight.** The (e) half **generalises past precision** — any
parameterised differential test (page sizes, colour spaces, font sizes, core
counts) proves agreement only over its sampled domain, and binding it inside
`R211` hides it from someone writing a non-precision differential test.
**Mitigated the way `R211` mitigated its own declined sibling**: the general form
is filed as a fact in `D:/dev/rag/rust/`, where the test-methodology findings
already live, rather than as a rule nobody's condition matches. **★★ And
`Pass 122.0` is where it will bite next** — *"byte-identical output at any core
count"* is a differential contract over a parameter, and *"any"* is the word this
finding is about.

|---:|---|---:|
| **`31 s`** | the same CAD region with **algorithm B disabled entirely** — i.e. the **baseline** | `100 000×` |
| **`93 s`** | the **REJECTED device-space attempt** | `100 000×` |
| **`1.3 s`** | **shipped** | `100 000×` |

⇒ **`31 s → 1.3 s` = `23.8×` is the speed-up**, and it is the figure the 232nd
filing headlined. **`93 s` against `31 s` = `3×` is the rejected attempt's
penalty**, and it is the figure that justified deleting the device-space
scaffolding.

#### `PASS 74.7`, FIRST ALGORITHM (`1d6db9e`) — `Mat64`: the CTM carried in `f64` and narrowed only at the leaf

**Three sites had to change together and each was load-bearing alone**: `cm`
concatenation, a Form XObject's `/Matrix`, and — the one that took longest to
find — **the BASE transform**, which `RegionGeometry` was handing over **already
narrowed**. **Widening an `f32` back to `f64` carries its rounding forward**, so
the fix is to keep the `f64` coefficients rather than to widen the `f32` ones.
That sentence is the transferable half and it is the same trick `Pass 74.2` used
one level up.

**Why the symptom was never distortion.** A translation error moves *every*
point of a form equally, so the drawing stayed correctly shaped and correctly
proportioned and sat **hundreds of pixels away, or off the canvas entirely**.
Nothing looked broken; things were simply absent.

**Measured — forms rendered of the `11` in view, 1600 px framed on the banana's
water molecule:**

| `scale` | before | after | correct answer | why |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `2 × 10⁶` | 11 of 11 | **11 of 11** | 11 | all eleven still in frame |
| `1.25 × 10⁷` | 7 of 11 | **2 of 11** | **2** | the box plus the one molecule in frame; the other nine leave the viewport and `Pass 74.4` culls them **exactly** |
| `2.5 × 10⁷` | 3 of 11 | **2 of 11** | **2** | as above |
| `5 × 10⁷` | 1 of 11 | **2 of 11** | **2** | as above |
| `1.6 × 10⁹` | — | **2 of 11** | **2** | a single water molecule renders sharply at **≈ 190 billion percent**; before, everything above `≈ 5 × 10⁶` vanished |

**★★ ORDINARY RENDERING IS UNAFFECTED, WHICH WAS THE OPERATOR'S OWN
CONSTRAINT.** The `f64` composition happens **once per `cm`, not once per
pixel**: banana whole page **1430 / 1458 ms against 1487 / 1532 ms before** —
two runs each, i.e. noise, and the *after* pair is the faster of the two.

#### ★★★★★ `R215`'s INSTANCE — THE ACCEPTANCE ORACLE THIS FILE FILED IN ADVANCE DEMANDED THE WRONG ANSWER

**The Backlog entry for `Pass 74.7`, written by the 230th filing, carried a
column headed *"required after `74.7`"* reading `11 of 11` at every one of the
five scales.** The correct post-fix answer is **`2`** at every scale from
`1.25 × 10⁷` up. **A fix that satisfied the filed oracle would have been a
BUG** — it would have meant nine forms outside the viewport were being painted.

**How the oracle got it wrong, which is the reusable part.** The engineer
measured `11 → 7 → 3 → 1` across rising zoom and read it as **one curve produced
by one defect**. It is **two curves superimposed**:

- the **precision** defect, losing forms to a quantised translation — the thing
  being hunted; and
- **`Pass 74.4`'s `/BBox` viewport cull**, losing forms because they genuinely
  left the frame — **exact, correct, and shipped by this same project five
  commits earlier**.

The oracle attributed **all** of the decline to the first, and therefore
predicted the *un-culled* count as the requirement. **Its own healthy row —
`11 of 11` at `2 × 10⁶` — was extrapolated to every other row**, which is the
mechanism: *the healthy end of a curve read as the target for the whole curve.*

**★★ AND THE PART THAT MADE IT AUTHORITATIVE.** The 230th filing headed that
table ***"ACCEPTANCE BASELINE — ALREADY MEASURED, WHICH IS RARE ENOUGH TO
NAME"*** and wrote *"this Pass has a pass/fail oracle **before a line is
written**"*. **The praise is what made it hard to question.** An oracle
introduced as unusually rigorous is one a later reader has less reason to check,
not more — and this one was **measured**, which is exactly the property that
made its wrongness invisible: every number in it was correct as an observation,
and the *column heading* was the claim.

⇒ **`R215` MINTED.** Full text under *Standing rules*. In one line: **an
acceptance oracle states the EXPECTED value and the MECHANISM that produces it,
per row; where two mechanisms move the same number, it decomposes them or says
it cannot.** A row that says `11 of 11` and cannot say *why 11* is a
transcription, not a prediction.

**Recorded honestly: no harm resulted**, because the engineer measured the
delivered behaviour and reasoned about what `2` meant instead of matching the
table. **That is care, not machinery**, and the rule exists because the next
session may match the table.

#### `PASS 74.7`, SECOND ALGORITHM (`5b0d885`) — differencing, and the result that was not the goal

**`Mat64` cannot fix a path whose OWN coordinates are large page numbers.** An
`f32` near `x = 90 pt` has a spacing of `7.6 × 10⁻⁶ pt`, so **a rectangle
`8 × 10⁻⁶ pt` wide is one representable step** and is destroyed when the
operands are narrowed. **No precision in the CTM recovers it** — the information
is gone before any matrix applies. This is limit **1** of the three, which the
Backlog entry had recorded as out of scope.

**The fix.** When the magnitude gate `needs_precise_paths` fires, the
interpreter builds the path **relative to its own first point**, differencing in
`f64`, so what reaches `tiny_skia` is a set of **small offsets** instead of
nearly-equal large numbers. The CTM alongside keeps its linear part and carries
the origin's mapped position. **Gated on magnitude alone, decided once per
path**, so ordinary rendering never enters it: **CAD at scale 1.0 is `1086 ms`
against a `980–1040 ms` baseline; banana page `1442 ms` against `1430–1538 ms`.**

##### ★★★ THE REJECTED FIRST ATTEMPT IS THE MORE USEFUL RECORD

**Building the path in DEVICE space with an identity transform was CORRECT, and
`3×` SLOWER at extreme zoom** — **`93 s` against `31 s`** on a stroke-heavy CAD
sheet.

**The cause is a rasteriser fact, not a PDF one: `tiny_skia` flattens curves to
a tolerance expressed in the PATH'S OWN UNITS.** A path whose coordinates are
millions gets subdivided accordingly, so moving coordinates into device space
buys precision and pays for it in segment count. **This is the finding most
likely to be re-derived by a future session** and it is escalated to
`D:/dev/rag/rust/` for that reason.

**It also forced a similarity restriction**, since an identity transform cannot
scale a pen — which meant a `similarity_scale` helper, a stroke-width multiplier
and a dash rebuild. **Differencing removed all four at once**: coordinates stay
at user-space magnitude so flattening is unchanged, the linear part still
reaches `tiny_skia` so strokes and dashes need no adjustment, and **any affine
CTM is admissible** rather than only a similarity. **The helper and the stroke
plumbing were DELETED rather than left as archaeology**, which is worth naming —
a rejected approach that leaves its scaffolding behind is read by the next
reader as a live constraint.

##### ★★★★ THE FINDING WORTH ESCALATING, AND IT WAS NOT THE GOAL OF THE WORK

**The same CAD region went `31 s → 1.3 s`.** Divided: **`23.8×`**. And at
`100 000×` zoom, **`93 s → 1.3 s` = `71.5×`**. The engineer's headline figure is
the conservative one, **`23×`**.

> **★★ AMENDED 2026-08-23 (233rd filing): the `71.5×` in the sentence above is
> NOT a second speed-up.** The engineer supplied `93 s`'s provenance — it is the
> **rejected device-space attempt** at `100 000×`, not a baseline; the baseline
> at that zoom is **`31 s`** (the same region with algorithm B disabled
> entirely). ⇒ **`31 s → 1.3 s` = `23.8×` is the speed-up**, at both zooms;
> **`93 s` against `31 s` = `3×` is the rejected attempt's penalty.** Nothing
> above is deleted, per hard rule 1. Full table in `PASS 74.10`'s Shipped entry.

**Deep zoom was never slow BECAUSE it was imprecise — it was slow FOR THE SAME
REASON**: large magnitudes reaching a rasteriser that reasons in **relative**
tolerances. **Fixing where the numbers are large fixed both.**

⇒ **The generalisable shape: a precision defect and a performance defect with a
single cause will look unrelated until one of them is fixed — and the
performance one is the half nobody attributes correctly**, because *"deep zoom
is slow"* sounds like an inherent cost of deep zoom. Nobody opens a ticket
against physics. Escalated to `D:/dev/rag/rust/`.

**★ A FIGURE THIS FILING COULD NOT DISAMBIGUATE, FLAGGED RATHER THAN GUESSED
(hard rule 10's corollary — a correction is a claim).** `93 s` appears **twice**
in `5b0d885`'s message with two possible referents: once as **the rejected
device-space attempt's time** (*"three times slower … 93 s against 31 s"*) and
once as **a before-figure at `100 000×`** (*"at 100 000×, 93 s → 1.3 s"*). Those
cannot both be the same measurement unless the baseline at `100 000×` happens to
equal the rejected attempt's time at the other zoom. **This filing does not
decide which**, files both ratios beside their pairs, and **reports the figure
to the engineer as owing one sentence of provenance.** The `23.8×` headline is
unaffected either way.

**Verified in both directions**, per the commit: the three-ways synthetic now
renders **all three** squares at **200 million percent** at identical size —
**including the one drawn in absolute coordinates that neither fix reached
before** — and a `2 × 10⁻⁶ pt` stroke comes out **200 px thick and 800 px long
at `1 × 10⁸`**, matching the arithmetic exactly, **by both routes**.

#### `PASS 74.9` (`296a23e`) — `--fast-subpixel`, the opt-in lossy cull

**`--fast-subpixel` on the CLI, `RenderOptions::subpixel_culling` in the
library, OFF by default.** A Form XObject whose transformed `/BBox` is under
**half a device pixel in BOTH axes** is not executed.

**Both axes, not either** — so a **hairline** (thin but long) still paints. That
is the difference between a fidelity trade and a bug.

**Tested after the exact `/BBox` cull and counted on a SEPARATE key**, because
**merging them would let a fidelity trade hide inside a correctness
optimisation**: `forms_culled` changes no pixel, `subpixel_culled` does. This is
the mechanism `decision 083` records.

**MEASURED — whole page, `gen-scale-demo` banana:**

**`1 468 ms → 108 ms` = `13.6×`, with ZERO of `1 242 640` pixels different
(`0.0 %`)** — at that zoom each dropped object is `1/70` of a pixel and
contributes nothing a raster can hold.

**And the measurement that keeps that honest, because "zero" would otherwise
read as "free".** The loss appears as objects **approach** the threshold rather
than sitting far below it. **Same page, a 1 pt window, ≈ `339 of 342` forms
dropped each time:**

| `scale` (× ; 1 pt window, ≈ 339 of 342 forms dropped each row) | pixels differing, of the window | share of window | worst channel delta, of 255 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `20` | 18 of 400 | **4.5 %** | 16 (**6.3 %**) |
| `35` | 47 of 1 296 | **3.6 %** | 54 (**21 %**) |
| `60` | 82 of 3 600 | **2.3 %** | **62** (**24 %** — a quarter of a channel) |
| whole page, page-fit | **0 of 1 242 640** | **0.0 %** | 0 |

⇒ **It is genuinely lossy; the loss is largest exactly where the speed-up is
smallest; and where the speed-up is enormous the loss happens to be nil.** That
shape — **the error and the benefit anti-correlated across the parameter that
triggers both** — **is why it is a switch and not a heuristic pdfce applies on
its own judgement.** A heuristic would have to pick a threshold, and every
threshold sits somewhere on that curve.

**`decision 082` is SATISFIED, NOT OVERRIDDEN.** 082 says a lossy speed-up is
the operator's call. The operator called it. **Rule 4 is honoured in both
positions**: `subpixel_culled` prints **whether or not the flag is set**, so a
raster always carries the count of what it left out and an operator comparing
two renders can see which one paid for its speed.

---

#### DECISION 083 MINTED — the SHAPE a lossy render option takes

Full text in `ARCHITECTURE.md` §12. In one line: **a lossy render option is
carried in `RenderOptions`, defaults OFF, and gets its OWN metrics key; an exact
skip and a lossy skip never share a counter.**

**Why this is not already `082`, since that is the obvious objection.** `082`
answers **who decides** — *a render may skip work only where skipping is exact;
a lossy speed-up is the operator's call.* It says **nothing about what the
answer looks like once the operator says yes**, and the two available shapes
were genuinely different: a flag, or a merged counter with a threshold. **The
merge was available and was refused with a reason**, which is a choice, which is
what a decision record is for. `082` is *whose call*; `083` is *what the call
produces*. Cross-referenced in both directions, deliberately not merged — the
same disposition `R213`/`R214` got one filing ago.

**Body-section updates:** §4.1 gains sync entry **(AB)**; §4's *Numerical reach
of PAGE-SPACE CONTENT* paragraph gains its dated discharge; §(H)'s key count
moves `89 → 90`.
